sections.title: Short Title and Citation
sections.brief: This compilation is the Codex of the Mages' Guild, cited C.C.D. State who may cite it in filings. Dry.

body.heading: Short Title and Citation
body.text:
This compilation is the Codex of the Mages' Guild, cited C.C.D. The authority of the Codex is derived from the foundational agreements established within the Autumnwood Accords, serving as the primary regulatory framework for all arcane activities sanctioned by the Guild. Any legal filing, petition for research, or appeal of disciplinary action must reference the specific section of the C.C.D. to be deemed admissible by the Archmage Sovereign or the presiding council of the Accords Desk. The Codex serves as the definitive record of the Guild’s internal governance, distinguishing between the preservationist requirements of the Conservators and the experimental liberties granted to the Innovators.

The C.C.D. is the sole authoritative text for the interpretation of magical conduct within the Midlands and any territories under Guild jurisdiction. No external decree, local ordinance, or private pact shall supersede the provisions contained herein unless expressly stated in a formal amendment signed by Archmage Veyra. All practitioners, from high-ranking Archmages to the lowliest initiate, are expected to maintain a copy of the Codex or have immediate access to a verified transcription for the purposes of compliance. Failure to cite the correct section during a formal inquiry may result in a procedural dismissal of the petitioner's claims, as the Guild maintains that ignorance of the C.C.D. is no defense against its mandates.

The citation of the C.C.D. must be precise. When referencing multiple statutes, the petitioner shall list them in ascending numerical order. For example, a violation involving both the unauthorized use of restricted materials and the breach of a sanctuary shall be cited as "see § 1.6 and § 1.15." The Clerk of the Accords Desk reserves the right to strike any filing that utilizes colloquialisms or non-standard shorthand in place of the required C.C.D. designations. The Codex is a living document of the Guild’s history and its future; to cite it is to acknowledge the weight of the Autumnwood Accords and the shared responsibility of the mages to maintain the stability of the weave.

body.heading: § 1.1 Short Title and Citation
body.text:
The present body of law shall be known formally as the Autumnwood Accords, hereafter referred to in all legal proceedings, administrative filings, and scholarly inquiries as the Codex of the Mages' Guild. The designation C.C.D. shall serve as the universal shorthand for all citations contained herein. Any individual, entity, or faction seeking to invoke the authority of the Guild must reference the specific section and subsection of the C.C.D. to ensure the validity of the petition. Failure to provide a precise citation may result in the immediate dismissal of the filing by the Accords Desk, as the Guild does not recognize vague references to "the rules" or "the laws."

Only authorized persons and entities are permitted to cite the C.C.D. in formal legal filings. This includes, but is not limited to, the Archmage Sovereign, the presiding heads of the Conservator and Innovator factions, and the Aegis Magi tasked with the enforcement of these laws. Furthermore, licensed practitioners of the arcane who hold a valid standing with the Guild may cite the C.C.D. in matters of judicial appeal or regulatory dispute. Any non-affiliate attempting to cite the C.C.D. in a public forum or a non-Guild court shall be deemed to be engaging in unauthorized advocacy and may be subject to a fine as established in § 1301.1.

The C.C.D. is the supreme governing authority for all magical manifestations within the Midlands and the Autumn Wood. While external laws such as the Iron Mandate may exist in neighboring territories, they possess no jurisdiction over the internal workings of the Guild or the conduct of its members while under the protection of the Accords. Conversely, the Guild shall not recognize the authority of the Silver Flame or the Regal Empire over any matter governed by the C.C.D. Any attempt to superimpose foreign law upon a Guild-sanctioned site is a violation of the Accords and shall be met with immediate jurisdictional severance.

All citations must be recorded in the official ledger of the Accords Desk. When a mage invokes a specific statute to justify a translocation, a research project, or a disciplinary action, the clerk of the desk shall verify the accuracy of the citation against the master copy. If a citation is found to be inaccurate, the filer shall be required to rectify the record immediately. The Guild maintains that the integrity of the C.C.D. is the foundation of magical stability; therefore, any deliberate falsification of a citation shall be considered a high-level breach of the Accords, punishable by the Paradox Trial as outlined in the relevant penal sections.

Reference is hereby made to § 1401.1 regarding the formal recording of historical annotations, which ensures that the evolution of these citations remains transparent to all authorized parties. All parties are reminded that the C.C.D. is a living document of the Autumnwood Accords, intended to balance the preservation of stability championed by the Conservators with the necessary progress sought by the Innovators. The Sovereign, Archmage Veyra, serves as the final arbiter in matters of citation interpretation where the text may be deemed ambiguous by the Accords Desk.

sections.title: Enacting Authority; Autumnwood Accords Desk
sections.brief: The Accords Desk issues this title. Conservators and Innovators both sit. Neither may pretend the other does not exist.

body.heading: Enacting Authority; Autumnwood Accords Desk
body.text:
The authority of this Codex is derived from the foundational agreements established within the Autumnwood Accords, serving as the primary regulatory framework for all thaumaturgical activity within the Midlands. The Accords Desk, established as the supreme administrative body of the Mages' Guild, is hereby designated as the sole issuing authority for this title. The Accords Desk is comprised of a dual-chambered oversight committee representing the two primary philosophical pillars of the Guild: the Conservators and the Innovators. By the very nature of the Accords, neither faction may claim exclusive jurisdiction over the interpretation of these laws, nor may either faction pretend that the other does not exist in the eyes of the sovereign.

Archmage Veyra, acting as the Archmage Sovereign, serves as the ultimate mediator in instances where the Conservators and Innovators reach an irreconcilable impasse regarding the interpretation of the Desk’s decrees. While the Conservators prioritize the preservation of established stability and the containment of forbidden schools, and the Innovators seek the advancement of restricted research under proper authorization, the Accords Desk serves as the neutral ground where these competing interests are codified into actionable law. Any attempt to bypass the Desk to enact unilateral policy by either Archmage Theron or Janna Brightspark shall be deemed a violation of the Accords and subject to immediate review.

The Accords Desk holds the power of issuance, amendment, and repeal. All mandates issued under this title are binding upon all members of the Guild, regardless of their specific factional allegiance. The Desk shall ensure that the balance between traditionalist preservation and radical innovation is maintained through the rigorous application of these statutes. No individual member, regardless of rank, may issue a decree that contradicts the primary intent of the Accords Desk. Furthermore, the Desk maintains the right to suspend specific regulations during times of regional crisis, provided such suspensions are communicated to the Aegis Magi for enforcement.

body.heading: How to Read This Codex
body.text:
The interpretation of this Codex shall be governed by the strict linguistic standards of the Mages' Guild legal tradition. The word "shall" denotes a mandatory requirement; any failure to comply with a "shall" provision constitutes a breach of the Accords. The word "may" denotes a discretionary power granted to the practitioner or the Guild; the absence of a "may" provision does not imply a prohibition, but rather a lack of authorized privilege. "Must" is utilized in instances of absolute necessity where the preservation of the magical weave or the safety of the Midlands is at stake. Conversely, "reserved" indicates that a right or power is retained by the Guild and cannot be exercised by the individual.

The Quiet List is a specific regulatory designation; any matter listed therein is to be treated with the utmost discretion and is not subject to public recitation or dissemination. Practitioners are reminded that a reader who skips the definitions provided in this Codex remains fully bound by them. Ignorance of the specific wording of a statute shall not serve as a defense against a finding of violation. The Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy for the "impatient" reader who attempts to interpret a statute based on colloquial understanding rather than the precise legal definitions provided herein.

Cross-references within this Codex are to be treated as primary sources of authority. When a statute directs the reader to "see also" a specific section, the contents of that section are to be read in conjunction with the current provision to determine the full scope of the law. The Codex is a holistic document; therefore, a violation of a definition in § 1.6 may render a practitioner non-compliant with a seemingly unrelated conduct clause in later sections. All practitioners are expected to maintain a functional literacy of the Codex to ensure their actions remain within the bounds of the Accords.

body.heading: Persons Bound
body.text:
The protections, privileges, and penalties set forth in this Codex apply to all entities recognized as "Persons Bound" under the Autumnwood Accords. This includes all registered members of the Mages' Guild, all registered apprentices currently under a master’s tutelage, and all "temporary mouths"—individuals granted short-term magical residency or permission to conduct minor thaumaturgy within the Guild’s jurisdiction. Furthermore, any construct, golem, or animated object that holds a quill and is utilized for the recording of Guild business, or any guest who casts a spell of any magnitude within a Guild hall, is considered a Person Bound for the duration of their presence.

The scope of these laws is comprehensive. Any individual who derives power from the weave and operates within the Midlands is subject to the oversight of the Accords Desk. This includes independent contractors who have signed the Goodstyle Artisan liaison agreements, as they are recognized as allies and thus fall under the Guild's protective and regulatory umbrella. Failure by a Person Bound to adhere to the Accords may result in a Paradox Trial, as outlined in the penal sections of this Codex.

It is explicitly stated for the purpose of legal clarity that "mike" is not a person bound. "mike" is not a character within the jurisdictional reality of the Guild and therefore cannot be sued, prosecuted, or bound by the Accords. Furthermore, "Grime" is not a Guild office. Any correspondence directed to "Grime" regarding official Guild business shall be deemed null and void, as no such administrative entity exists within the official registry of the Autumnwood Accords. These exclusions are necessary to prevent the frivolous application of Guild law to non-entities or non-existent locations.

body.heading: Relation to Other Law
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords and this Codex constitute the primary legal authority for all matters concerning the mastery, use, and regulation of magic within the Midlands. It is a fundamental principle of Guild law that these Accords are distinct from the laws of rival powers. Specifically, the Iron Mandate—the legal code of the Regal Empire and the Iron Legion—is a rival law and holds no authority over the Guild’s internal operations or the conduct of its members while within the Guild’s sovereign territory. Any attempt to enforce the Iron Mandate upon a Guild member during a sanctioned research period shall be met with a formal diplomatic protest from Archmage Veyra.

Furthermore, this Codex does not recognize "Diet acts" as valid Guild stamps. Any local ordinance or minor decree issued by regional governing bodies that seeks to regulate magic without the express seal of the Accords Desk is considered a secondary, and often unenforceable, suggestion. The Guild does not recognize the authority of the Silver Flame's Edicts of the Flame as a governing law for its members, though it acknowledges the religious nature of such codes in matters of external diplomacy.

Regarding commerce and tender, it is strictly codified that the Wario Coin is not a recognized tender of the Mages' Guild. No Guild debts, fees, or fines may be settled using Wario Coins, and the Guild shall not be held liable for the exchange or valuation of such currency. Finally, in matters of geographical and metaphysical discovery, the Heartstone and any associated rifts are to be treated as "speech" until a formal survey is completed. The One-T cartography is recognized as a map and a tool of navigation; it does not, under any circumstances, constitute a raid license or a permit for unauthorized entry into restricted zones.

body.heading: Definitions
body.text:
For the purposes of this Codex, a "caster" is defined as any sentient being capable of manifesting the weave through the use of incantations, somatic components, or focused intent. A "value" refers to the quantified output of a spell, measured in either mana-density or localized environmental impact. "Material alteration" refers to any change in the physical properties of an object that persists after the cessation of the spell. "Transfiguration" is a specific subset of material alteration involving the change of one species or substance into another. "Disclosure" refers to the sharing of any Guild-protected information, including but not limited to the Quiet List or the specifics of restricted research.

A "familiar" is a sentient or semi-sentient entity bound to a caster via a formal pact, which may be subject to different regulatory standards than those applied to Persons Bound. A "pocket" refers to any localized fold in space-time, including pocket-dimensions or extra-planar apertures created for the purpose of storage or containment. The "Quiet List" is a non-public catalogue of sensitive magical phenomena, entities, or locations; any member who recites the contents of the Quiet List in a tavern or public forum shall be subject to immediate sanction.

A "Paradox Trial" is the formal judicial process utilized to adjudicate violations of the Accords by one's peers. The term "sanction" in this context refers to the sealing of a mage's magic. "Seal magic" is the act of binding a caster's ability to the weave so they may no longer manifest it. The "Aegis Magi" are defined as the enforcement arm of the dominant faction, tasked with the physical and magical policing of these regulations. All definitions herein are intended to be broad; any term not explicitly defined shall be interpreted in the spirit of the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: Construction; Aggregation of Conduct
body.text:
The Guild maintains a strict policy regarding the determination of violations. The fragmentation of conduct shall not prevent a finding of violation. If a mage commits a series of minor infractions that, when viewed in isolation, do not reach the threshold for a Paradox Trial, the Accords Desk reserves the right to aggregate these actions. If the cumulative effect of these fragmented acts demonstrates a pattern of negligence, malice, or systematic violation of the Accords, the totality of the conduct shall be judged as a single, cohesive breach.

This principle ensures that practitioners cannot circumvent the law by performing multiple small violations that individually fall below the radar of the Aegis Magi. For example, the repeated, minor unauthorized use of restricted research materials, while perhaps not constituting a "major" crime on its own, may be aggregated to prove a pattern of illicit research. Such a finding will result in a Paradox Trial where the full scope of the aggregated conduct is presented to the council of peers.

This construction is intended to protect the integrity of the magical weave and the safety of the Midlands from those who seek to exploit the nuances of the law. The Guild views the intent of the practitioner as a primary factor in the aggregation of conduct. A mage who intentionally breaks the law in small increments to avoid detection shall find their actions aggregated with the same severity as a single, large-scale violation. See § 1.2 for the authority of the Desk in overseeing these judgments.

body.heading: Effective Date; Savings
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords and this Codex shall take effect immediately upon the final sealing of this volume by the Accords Desk. All prior agreements, verbal pacts, and written treaties established by the Guild prior to the formalization of the Accords remain in effect, provided they do not directly contradict the primary mandates of the current Codex. In the event of a conflict between a prior Accords agreement and a new Codex entry, the Codex entry shall take precedence, as it represents the most current will of the Archmage Sovereign and the Accords Desk.

The "Savings" clause dictates that the repeal of a specific regulation does not automatically revive any repealed schemes or previous legal frameworks. For instance, if a specific restriction on blood magic is repealed, it does not mean that previous restrictions on necromancy are reinstated; each regulation exists as a distinct legal entity. Dead citations in Part XIV (or any subsequent part) do not revive repealed schemes; once a law is struck from the Codex, it ceases to exist in the eyes of the Guild, and no "ghost laws" may be invoked to punish modern practitioners.

Furthermore, any ongoing legal proceedings or Paradox Trials initiated under the previous iterations of the Accords shall be completed under the rules of those previous iterations. The Guild shall not retroactively apply new penalties to actions committed before the effective date of this Codex. This ensures a stable legal environment where mages can predict the consequences of their actions based on the law as it stands at the moment of the act.

body.heading: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
body.text:
The validity of any official Guild document, permit, or research authorization is dependent upon the presence of a valid Seal of the Accords Desk. For the purposes of legal distinction, certain items and occurrences do not constitute a valid seal. Specifically, any markings made by non-Guild entities, including but not limited to garlic bread on a map, are not recognized as seals. Such markings have no legal weight and do not grant the holder any permissions, privileges, or protections under the Autumnwood Accords.

Furthermore, the status of a certifying officer is strictly regulated. A concussed unnamed pilot, regardless of their previous status or proximity to a Guild transport, is not a certifying officer. Only those officially appointed by Archmage Veyra and bearing the proper insignia of the Accords Desk may issue seals of authority. Any document bearing a seal from an unauthorized source is considered fraudulent, and any practitioner who utilizes such a document shall be subject to immediate arrest by the Aegis Magi and a subsequent Paradox Trial.

The Guild warns against the "Seal of Convenience"—the practice of allowing a peer to sign off on a minor research permit to bypass the Desk's scrutiny. Such an act is a violation of the Disclosure and Authorization statutes. Only the designated officers of the Conservators or Innovators, as approved by the Archmage Sovereign, may apply the official stamps. This ensures that all magic remains under the oversight of the Accords Desk and that the balance of power between the two factions is maintained through proper, authorized channels.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
The inclusion of "Reserved" sections within this Codex serves a vital administrative purpose. A blank section or a section marked as "Reserved" is still a place in the book; it signifies a space held for future expansion, amendment, or the insertion of specific sub-clauses as the magical landscape of the Midlands evolves. The existence of a reserved catchline does not imply that the law is currently silent on a topic, but rather that the specific regulatory language for that topic is to be determined at a later date by the Accords Desk.

Any practitioner who attempts to argue that a lack of specific language in a reserved section constitutes a "loophole" for illicit activity is mistaken. The Guild maintains that the overarching principles of the Autumnwood Accords apply to all matters not explicitly covered by the current text. If a situation arises that falls under a reserved catchline, the Accords Desk shall issue a provisional decree until a formal statute can be drafted and filed.

The use of reserved sections allows the Guild to maintain a coherent structure while remaining flexible enough to adapt to new magical threats or innovations. It prevents the Codex from becoming cluttered with temporary measures that should eventually be codified into permanent law. When a reserved section is populated, it shall be integrated into the numbering system as a primary statute. Until such time, all matters falling into the scope of the reservation are governed by the general principles of Mana Reverence and the sovereign mediation of Archmage Veyra.

sections.title: How to Read This Codex
sections.brief: Shall, may, must, Quiet List, reserved, see also. A reader who skips definitions is still bound. Trip the impatient.

body.heading: How to Read This Codex
body.text:
The interpretation of this Codex shall be governed by the standard linguistic conventions of the Autumnwood Accords. Where the text states "shall," the provision is a mandatory requirement; failure to comply constitutes a primary breach of the Accords. Where the text states "may," the provision represents a discretionary permission granted to the practitioner, provided such exercise does not violate any prohibitive clauses found elsewhere in the Codex. The term "must" shall be construed as a prerequisite for the validity of any thaumaturgical act or administrative filing. Practitioners are cautioned that the absence of a "must" does not imply a waiver of safety or ethical standards, but rather a lack of specific regulatory oversight for the action in question.

Any matter designated as "reserved" within these pages is strictly off-limits to the unauthorized reading, recitation, or mental probing of any member. Such sections are withheld to protect the structural integrity of the Midlands' magical weave or to safeguard sensitive geopolitical interests of the Guild. The phrase "see also" serves as a formal directive to the reader to consult the referenced sections to ensure a complete understanding of the legal context. A reader who skips definitions is still bound by the Codex, as the Guild maintains that ignorance of the specific legal nomenclature does not constitute a defense against a finding of violation. The Codex is designed to be exhaustive; therefore, the impatient who attempt to bypass the dense prose of these regulations shall find their actions judged by the full weight of the surrounding statutes.

Legal scholars and practitioners are reminded that the intent of the Sovereign, Archmage Veyra, is to maintain a balance of order. Therefore, any ambiguity in the text shall be resolved in favor of the stability of the Midlands. If a clause is found to be contradictory, the most restrictive interpretation shall prevail until such time as the Conservators or Innovators provide a formal clarification. No individual practitioner may unilaterally redefine the scope of a statute through personal interpretation or "creative" casting. This Codex is the final authority on Guild conduct; any deviation from its established linguistic framework is a violation of the peace.

body.heading: Persons Bound
body.text:
The jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords extends to all entities capable of exerting a thaumaturgical influence or participating in the administrative functions of the Guild. This includes, but is not limited to, all full members, initiates, and apprentices currently under contract. Furthermore, any individual holding a Provisional Guild Pass, such as those issued to political intermediaries like Archie Miser, is bound by the restrictions herein. This jurisdiction also extends to "temporary mouths"—entities granted the right to speak on behalf of a master—provided they have been formally registered with the Aegis Magi. Any construct, golem, or animated object that possesses the capacity to hold a quill or perform administrative logging is considered a bound agent of the Guild and must adhere to all secrecy and conduct protocols.

Guests, visitors, and transient mages who cast any spell—regardless of magnitude or intended effect—within the physical confines of a Guild Hall or an Autumnwood Accord-sanctioned site shall be subject to the full weight of these laws. This applies even if the guest is not a member of the Guild, as the sanctity of the Hall is paramount. However, the Guild explicitly clarifies that "mike" is not a person bound by these Accords, as "mike" is not a character within the legal framework of this jurisdiction. Furthermore, it is hereby established that "Grime" is not a Guild office; any attempt to file grievances, petitions, or petitions for magical licensing at a location designated as "Grime" shall be deemed null and void.

All bound persons are responsible for the actions of their familiars and summoned entities, provided those entities are utilized in the pursuit of Guild-sanctioned work. If a construct or familiar commits a violation of the Accords, the primary caster shall be held liable for the repercussions. The Aegis Magi are authorized to enforce these boundaries with necessary force. Any individual found to be outside the scope of these definitions who nevertheless engages in unauthorized thaumaturgy may be subject to emergency detention and subsequent adjudication under the Paradox Trial, as outlined in § 1.6.

body.heading: Relation to Other Law
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords serve as the primary regulatory framework for the Midlands; however, they do not supersede the existence of external legal systems. It is explicitly stated that the Iron Mandate, being the law of the Regal Empire and the Iron Legion, is a rival law and is not recognized as a valid title or governing authority within this Codex. While the Guild may interact with the Empire or the Legion, the internal regulations of the Guild shall remain sovereign over all Guild-related activities. No "Diet acts" or local ordinances shall be considered Guild stamps or official Guild policy unless they have been formally ratified by Archmage Veyra and signed by the respective faction leaders.

Furthermore, the Guild declares that the Wario Coin is not a recognized form of tender for any Guild transactions, fees, or reparations. Any attempt to settle a debt to the Guild or a fine issued during a Paradox Trial using Wario Coins shall be rejected. The Guild maintains its own internal economy and does not recognize the currency of external entities as a means of legal satisfaction.

Regarding specific environmental phenomena, the Guild acknowledges the existence of the Heartstone and associated rifts. It is established that any speech or communication originating from such a rift is considered "speech" until a formal survey by a Guild-sanctioned cartography team has been completed. This ensures that the Guild can distinguish between natural phenomena and intentional magical communication. Additionally, the Guild clarifies that a One-T cartography map is a tool for navigation and geographical record; it does not constitute a raid license or a permit for the exploration of restricted zones. Possession of a map does not grant the right to violate the territorial integrity of the Accord boundaries.

body.heading: Definitions
body.text:
For the purposes of this Codex, the term "caster" shall refer to any sentient being capable of channeling, shaping, or projecting magical energy. "Value" refers to the quantified output of a spell, measured in both its magnitude of effect and its potential for collateral disruption. "Material alteration" is defined as any change to the physical properties of an object, including but not limited to its weight, density, state of matter, or chemical composition. "Transfiguration" is a specific subset of material alteration involving the total restructuring of a biological or inorganic entity into a different form. Any caster who performs transfiguration without a permit from the Innovators shall be subject to immediate review.

"Disclosure" refers to the sharing of any information regarding the Quiet List, the internal workings of the Aegis Magi, or the private research of the Conservators with any non-member or unauthorized personnel. A "familiar" is a sentient or semi-sentient entity bound to a caster for the purpose of service, companionship, or magical amplification. A "pocket" refers to any extradimensional space, regardless of its size or origin, created for the storage of items or the containment of entities. The "Quiet List" is a restricted catalog of prohibited spells and entities; its contents are never to be recited in taverns, public squares, or any other non-sanctioned assembly.

The "Paradox Trial" is the formal judicial process by which the Guild adjudicates violations of the Accords. It may involve a council of peers, a trial by arcane duel, or the sealing of a caster's magic. A "violation" is any act that undermines the stability of the Midlands or breaches the factional boundaries established by the Accords. All terms used in this Codex that are not explicitly defined herein shall be interpreted according to the common parlance of the Midlands as established by the Archmage Sovereign.

body.heading: Construction; Aggregation of Conduct
body.text:
The Guild maintains that the fragmentation of conduct shall not prevent a finding of violation. This means that a series of minor infractions, when viewed in aggregate, may be deemed a single, substantial breach of the Accords. The Guild does not require a single, catastrophic act to initiate a Paradox Trial; rather, a pattern of behavior that demonstrates a disregard for the safety of the Midlands or the integrity of the Accords is sufficient for prosecution. If a caster performs several small, unauthorized transfigurations over a period of time, these acts shall be aggregated to determine the severity of the penalty.

This principle ensures that mages cannot circumvent the law by performing "minor" illegal acts that, when combined, cause significant magical instability. The Aegis Magi are tasked with monitoring these patterns of conduct. A history of minor infractions shall be recorded in the caster’s permanent file and will be used as weight during any formal adjudication. If the aggregate of a caster's conduct reaches a threshold of "Significant Instability," the Conservators may move to seal the caster's magic permanently. This rule is consistent with the precedents established in the filed records regarding the assessment of rogue mages.

Furthermore, the intent of the caster shall be weighed alongside the physical outcome of their actions. A caster who intends to perform a minor material alteration but causes a significant rift due to incompetence shall still be held liable for the aggregate damage. The Guild does not recognize "accidental" magic as a complete defense against the consequences of the Act, though it may be considered a mitigating factor during the sentencing phase of a Paradox Trial. All conduct, whether singular or cumulative, is subject to the oversight of the Archmage Sovereign.

body.heading: Effective Date; Savings
body.text:
The provisions of this Codex shall take effect immediately upon the final ratification of the Autumnwood Accords by Archmage Veyra. All prior agreements, local pacts, and traditional mages' customs that do not directly conflict with the Accords shall remain in effect until such time as they are specifically repealed or superseded by a new entry in this Codex. These "Savings" clauses ensure that the transition to the new legal framework does not leave the Midlands in a state of lawless vacuum.

However, it is clearly stated that dead citations in Part XIV do not revive repealed schemes. If a section of the law has been struck from the Codex or designated as "repealed," no reference to that section in any other part of the book shall give it legal weight or validity. The Guild shall not be bound by the "ghosts" of old laws. Any practitioner attempting to cite a repealed law as a defense for a current action shall be found in contempt of the Guild and may be subject to a Paradox Trial.

Any permits, licenses, or protections granted under the previous administration shall remain valid until their expiration date, unless they are specifically declared void by the Conservators. This provides a period of stability for the Guild's existing infrastructure. Once a new statute is enacted, it shall supersede any conflicting prior law in its entirety. The Guild reserves the right to issue "Emergency Decrees" which may temporarily suspend specific sections of the Codex during times of high magical instability or external threat from the Regal Empire or the Silver Flame.

body.heading: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
body.text:
The validity of any Guild document, license, or permit is contingent upon the application of an official Seal of the Autumnwood Accords. A Seal is a specific, magically-resonant mark applied by an authorized official of the Guild. It is important to note that not all marks of significance constitute a legal Seal. Specifically, the presence of garlic bread on a map or any other culinary marking shall not be interpreted as a seal of authenticity or a grant of permission. Such markings are considered personal notations and hold no weight in the eyes of the Aegis Magi.

Furthermore, the Guild explicitly clarifies that a concussed unnamed pilot is not a certifying officer. No individual who is physically incapacitated, mentally distressed, or otherwise lacking the requisite training and designation may issue a Guild Seal or authorize the movement of magical assets. Any document bearing a seal from an unauthorized or incapacitated individual shall be deemed fraudulent. The Guild maintains a registry of all certifying officers; any individual not on this list is prohibited from applying the Guild's mark to any material.

The application of a Seal must be done in the presence of a Guild scribe or a designated Aegis officer to ensure that the correct magical signature is applied. If a Seal is tampered with, forged, or improperly placed, the document it accompanies is rendered void. This includes the physical integrity of the Seal; any smudge, alteration, or magical interference with the Seal's design shall be treated as an act of sabotage. Practitioners are advised to keep their Seals in secure locations, as the loss of a Seal may require a lengthy administrative process to recover or replace.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
The Guild acknowledges that certain sections of this Codex are to remain "Reserved." A reserved section is a placeholder within the legal framework that signifies a space in the book that is currently blank or withheld from the public record. The existence of a blank space does not imply a lack of law; rather, it indicates that the specific regulations for that topic are either being drafted, are classified as secret, or are currently under the jurisdiction of the Sovereign's private decree.

How reserved sections work is governed by the principle of administrative readiness. When a section is reserved, it is off-limits to all mages, including those of high rank, unless they are granted specific access by Archmage Veyra. A reserved section cannot be filled by the unilateral decree of a faction leader; only the Sovereign may authorize the transition of a reserved catchline into a functional statute. Practitioners who attempt to "fill in" the blanks of the Codex through unauthorized interpretation or by creating their own "sub-laws" shall be prosecuted for administrative heresy.

The presence of a reserved catchline ensures that the Codex is a living document. It allows the Guild to expand its regulatory reach as new magical threats emerge or as the Innovators push into new fields of research. While a reserved section may currently contain no text, it remains a place in the book that the Guild reserves the right to occupy at any time. Any attempt to bypass a reserved section to reach a subsequent law shall be viewed as a breach of the Codex's structural integrity. The Guild shall maintain the order of the pages as they are numbered; the sequence of law is as important as the law itself.

sections.title: Persons Bound
sections.brief: Members, apprentices, temporary mouths, constructs holding a quill, guests who cast inside a Guild hall. Mike is not a person bound. Grime is not a Guild office.

body.heading: Persons Bound
body.text:
The scope of these Accords shall extend to all entities whose actions, intent, or presence within the Midlands jurisdiction may exert a measurable thaumaturgical influence. For the purposes of liability and enforcement, the term "Persons Bound" shall encompass all registered Members of the Mages' Guild, including all initiated practitioners and those currently undergoing the tenure of an apprentice. Apprentices shall be held to the same standards of conduct as full members, though their liability for unauthorized research shall be mitigated by the presence of a supervising Conservator, provided such supervision was not willfully neglected.

Furthermore, the Accords shall bind any "temporary mouths" designated by the Archmage Sovereign to speak on behalf of the Guild in diplomatic matters. These designations shall expire upon the completion of the specific mandate or the expiration of the temporal window set by the Accords Desk. Any construct, regardless of its complexity of manufacture or origin, that is equipped with or holds a quill for the purpose of recording, drafting, or signing Guild documentation shall be considered a Person Bound for the duration of its active duty. This ensures that the intent of the Guild is preserved even when channeled through non-sentient artifice.

Guests who engage in the act of casting within any Guild hall, outpost, or sanctioned sanctuary shall be deemed Persons Bound for the duration of their residency within said grounds. This inclusion is mandatory to ensure that external actors cannot circumvent the safety protocols of the Autumnwood Accords by virtue of non-membership. All such guests shall be subject to the penalties outlined in the Codex, including the possibility of the Paradox Trial should their casting result in a structural or planar violation.

Notwithstanding the breadth of these definitions, the entity known as Mike is explicitly excluded from the definition of a Person Bound and shall not be subject to the jurisdictional reach of these Accords. Similarly, the location or concept known as Grime is not recognized as a Guild office and shall not be considered a seat of authority or a place of sanctuary under these laws. Any attempt to cite these Accords as applicable to the aforementioned entities shall be deemed a nullity. For matters regarding the specific limitations of jurisdiction, see § 1.5.

body.heading: Relation to Other Law
body.text:
The authority of the Autumnwood Accords is absolute within the Midlands, yet it exists in a state of perpetual friction with external legal frameworks. It is hereby clarified that the Iron Mandate, being the primary legal instrument of the Regal Empire and its subsidiary Iron Legion, is a rival law and shall not be recognized as a valid source of authority for internal Guild matters. While the Guild may acknowledge the existence of the Iron Mandate in matters of border defense or trade, the Accords shall supersede any Mandate-driven decree that conflicts with the preservation of magical stability or the rights of the Mages' Guild.

Furthermore, the Guild shall not be held liable for the actions of independent entities whose regulations are not sanctioned by the Accords. Diet acts, local ordinances, or minor regional decrees are not Guild stamps; the Guild shall not certify, endorse, or enforce any such measures unless specifically requested in writing by the Archmage Sovereign and formally ratified by the Accords Desk. Any practitioner acting under a local ordinance that violates the core tenets of the Accords shall be subject to internal disciplinary action regardless of their compliance with the local law.

Regarding the movement of assets and the valuation of goods, the Wario Coin is explicitly declared not to be a legal tender of the Mages' Guild. No debts, fines, or dues owed to the Guild shall be satisfied by the submission of Wario Coins, and the Guild shall not accept said coins as a valid form of payment for any services, materials, or licenses. Any attempt to use such currency in a Guild transaction shall be treated as a fraudulent offering.

Finally, special provisions are made regarding the Heartstone and its associated rifts. Any speech, communication, or telepathic transmission emanating from a Heartstone or a known rift shall be considered active speech for the purposes of the Accords until such time as the rift has been officially surveyed and stabilized by a certified Guild cartographer. During the period of instability, such speech shall be subject to the same monitoring and restrictions as public declarations. For more on the interpretation of these laws, see § 1.3.

body.heading: Definitions
body.text:
For the purposes of the Autumnwood Accords, the following definitions shall apply to all proceedings, litigations, and enforcement actions:

1. Caster: Any individual, construct, or entity capable of channeling, shaping, or manifesting arcane, divine, or primal energies, whether by birth, study, or external augmentation.

2. Value: The recognized worth of a magical item, service, or material as determined by the current market rates of the Goodstyle Artisans or the prevailing appraisal of the Conservator chair.

3. Material Alteration: Any change to the physical properties, molecular structure, or elemental composition of a non-living object through the application of magic.

4. Transfiguration: The specific act of altering the shape, form, or essence of a living being or a complex object into another distinct form, distinguishing it from simple material alteration.

5. Disclosure: The act of revealing Guild secrets, including but not limited to the contents of the Quiet List, to any non-member or unauthorized entity.

6. Familiar: A sentient or semi-sentient creature bound to a Caster through a formal pact, possessing a degree of autonomy but remaining subject to the Caster's primary magical influence.

7. Pocket: A localized fold in the fabric of reality, including but not limited to pocket dimensions, extradimensional spaces, or magically-enforced storage zones.

8. Quiet List: A non-public, restricted catalogue of sensitive information, entities, and magical anomalies that are not to be recited, shared, or acknowledged in public spaces, including but not limited to taverns and marketplaces.

9. Paradox Trial: The formal judicial process by which the Guild adjudicates violations of the Accords, involving a council of peers to determine the necessity of a Seal or a relocation to a pocket-prison.

For further clarification on the hierarchy of these definitions, see § 1.3.

body.heading: Construction; Aggregation of Conduct
body.text:
The Guild maintains that the intent of the Accords is paramount over the technicalities of sequence. Therefore, the fragmentation of conduct shall not prevent a finding of violation. A practitioner who commits a series of minor infractions that, when viewed in isolation, do not meet the threshold for a Paradox Trial, may still be found in violation of the Accords if the cumulative effect of those actions demonstrates a pattern of negligence, malice, or systemic instability.

This principle of aggregation ensures that the "slow erosion" of magical safety is addressed with the same rigor as a singular, catastrophic event. For example, a mage who repeatedly performs minor, unauthorized material alterations on public infrastructure may be held liable for a significant violation even if no single alteration caused structural failure. The Accords Desk reserves the right to aggregate multiple incidents over a period of no less than one lunar cycle to determine the severity of a breach.

This rule shall be applied consistently across all factions. The Innovators may not argue that their research is "incremental" to avoid the consequences of repeated minor violations, nor may the Conservators argue that a series of minor failures do not constitute a major breach of stability. If the aggregate conduct threatens the sanctity of the Autumnwood Accords, the Aegis Magi shall be authorized to intervene. For specific procedures on the recording of such conduct, see § 1.4.

body.heading: Effective Date; Savings
body.text:
These Accords shall take effect immediately upon the final sealing of this Codex by the Archmage Sovereign. All previous agreements, oral traditions, and written charters that have been superseded by the Autumnwood Accords shall remain in effect only insofar as they do not directly conflict with the provisions of this Codex. In the event of a conflict between a prior Accord and a current provision herein, the current provision shall prevail.

The "Savings" clause dictates that the repeal of a specific scheme or rule does not automatically revive any previous, repealed schemes that were previously integrated into the law. For instance, if a rule regarding the use of blood magic was repealed and replaced with a rule regarding restricted research, the repeal of the research rule does not reinstate the blood magic prohibition; rather, the legal vacuum shall be filled by the most recent standing Accord.

Dead citations—references to laws that have been formally struck from the Codex—do not possess the power to revive repealed schemes or grant authority to defunct organizations. Any practitioner found to be relying on a dead citation to justify their actions shall be subject to immediate review by the Accords Desk. The Guild shall maintain a registry of repealed laws to ensure that no "ghost laws" continue to influence the conduct of the populace. See § 1.2 for the overarching authority of these remaining provisions.

body.heading: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
body.text:
The validity of a Guild document, license, or decree is predicated upon the application of a recognized Guild Seal or a signature from a certifying officer. For the avoidance of doubt, the presence of any unauthorized mark, symbol, or culinary item upon a document does not constitute a legal seal. Specifically, garlic bread placed upon a map—regardless of its placement, quantity, or the intent of the person who placed it—is not a seal and confers no legal status, permission, or authorization.

Furthermore, the authority of a Guild officer is tied to their official capacity and the physical possession of their Seal. A concussed unnamed pilot, while perhaps possessing the knowledge of a Guild member or the title of a traveler, is not a certifying officer. Any document "signed" or "sealed" by an individual in a state of physical, mental, or magical incapacity shall be deemed void ab initio. The Accords Desk shall not recognize any mark made by an individual who is not currently holding an active, unexpired commission from the Archmage Sovereign.

This distinction is vital to prevent the subversion of Guild authority by those seeking to bypass the Paradox Trial or the restrictions of the Quiet List. All seals must be verified against the registry held at the Accords Desk. Any attempt to forge a seal, or to use a culinary item as a substitute for a legal mark, shall be considered a high-level violation of the Accords. For definitions of certifying officers, see § 1.1.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
This section serves as a formal reservation of the Guild’s right to expand the Codex as the nature of magic and the threats to the Midlands evolve. A blank space within this Codex is not a void in the law; it is a placeholder for future governance. The Archmage Sovereign, in consultation with the Conservators and the Innovators, may reserve specific sections for future inclusion, which shall be filled by decree as necessary.

The placement of a reserved catchline ensures that the structural integrity of the Codex remains intact as new laws are drafted. When a new law is inserted into a reserved section, it shall be numbered sequentially and cited in accordance with the standards set forth in § 1.3. The existence of a reserved section does not imply that the law is currently unwritten; rather, it signifies that the Guild acknowledges the necessity of future regulation on that specific topic.

Any practitioner who attempts to claim that a lack of specific wording in a reserved section constitutes a "legal loophole" shall be corrected by the Accords Desk. The Guild maintains the inherent right to interpret the spirit of the Accords in areas where the text is yet to be finalized. This ensures that the Accords remain a living document, capable of adapting to the shifting tides of thaumaturgical advancement while maintaining the foundational stability of the Autumnwood Accords. See § 1.2 for the overarching authority of the Sovereign to fill these blanks.

sections.title: Relation to Other Law
sections.brief: Iron Mandate is rival law, not this title. Diet acts are not Guild stamps. Wario Coin is not tender. Heartstone talk is speech until surveyed.

body.heading: Relation to Other Law
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords shall be understood as the primary and exclusive regulatory framework for thaumaturgical activity within the Midlands jurisdiction. All legal interpretations must prioritize the Accords over any external, secular, or competing legal structures that lack the specific endorsement of the Archmage Sovereign. It is expressly declared that the Iron Mandate, being the legislative output of the Regal Empire and the Iron Legion, is a rival law and possesses no jurisdiction over the internal governance, licensing, or ritual protections of the Guild. No provision of the Iron Mandate shall be cited as a justification for the suppression of Accord-sanctioned magic, nor shall any Guild member be compelled to acknowledge the Mandate as a binding authority in matters of arcane theory or practice.

Furthermore, it is established that local Diet acts, municipal ordinances, or regional common laws do not constitute Guild stamps or official authorizations. The presence of a municipal decree does not grant a caster the right to bypass the restrictions set forth in this Codex. Any action performed under the guise of "civil compliance" that violates the Accords shall be prosecuted as a primary breach. In matters of commerce, the Guild recognizes no external currency as a standard of internal transaction; specifically, the Wario Coin is not tender and shall not be accepted as valid payment for licenses, fees, or fines. All Guild debts and reparations shall be settled in approved sovereign currency or equivalent magical assets as determined by the Accords Desk.

Regarding the discovery of anomalous phenomena, the Guild maintains a strict protocol on the Heartstone and associated rifts. All speech, communication, or verbalized data emanating from a Heartstone site shall be legally classified as "speech" and afforded the protections of the Accords until such time as a certified survey team has conducted a full thaumaturgical audit of the site. Until the survey is complete, the site remains in a state of legal flux, and any unauthorized recording of such speech is subject to seizure. For the purposes of navigation, a One-T cartography document is recognized solely as a map; it does not constitute a raid license or a permit for entry into contested territories. See § 1.3 for linguistic conventions.

body.heading: Definitions
body.text: For the purposes of these Accords, the following terms shall have the specific meanings assigned herein: (1) Caster: Any sentient entity, regardless of biological origin, capable of manifesting intentional thaumaturgical effects upon the material plane. (2) Value: The measurable potency, duration, or area of effect of a magical phenomenon, as determined by the standard metrics of the Conservator branch. (3) Material Alteration: Any change to the physical properties, molecular structure, or state of matter of an object or environment through the application of external arcane force. (4) Transfiguration: A specific class of Material Alteration involving the permanent conversion of one species of matter into another, distinguished from temporary illusions or kinetic displacements. (5) Disclosure: The act of revealing restricted research, forbidden school methodologies, or Quiet List entries to any non-authorized entity, including the public or rival factions. (6) Familiar: A sentient or semi-sentient entity bound to a Caster via a formal contract, capable of acting as a conduit or sensory extension of the Caster’s will. (7) Pocket: A localized, self-contained spatial anomaly or dimension, whether natural or artificially constructed, used for the storage of items or the containment of entities. (8) Quiet List: A non-public, highly classified catalogue of restricted entities, locations, and prohibited methodologies; any recitation of the Quiet List in a public venue, such as a tavern or marketplace, shall be deemed a felony offense. (9) Paradox Trial: The formal adjudicatory process by which peers determine the guilt of a Caster, resulting in either the sealing of magic or the relocation of the offender to a pocket-prison.

body.heading: Construction; Aggregation of Conduct
body.text:
The Guild shall not recognize the fragmentation of conduct as a defense against a finding of violation. This provision ensures that a Caster who performs a series of individual actions, each of which may appear minor or legally ambiguous in isolation, shall still be held liable if the cumulative effect of those actions constitutes a violation of the Autumnwood Accords. The prosecution shall not be required to prove that a single act reached the threshold of a violation; rather, the prosecution may aggregate multiple instances of prohibited behavior to demonstrate a pattern of systemic breach.

For example, a Caster who performs three separate, minor unauthorized transfigurations over the course of a week may be found in violation of the Accords if those actions collectively result in a significant Material Alteration of a protected site. The intent to circumvent the law through "micro-violations" is explicitly prohibited. Any pattern of behavior that undermines the stability sought by the Conservators or the regulated progress sought by the Innovators shall be subject to the full weight of the Paradox Trial. This principle of aggregation applies to all sections of this Codex, ensuring that the spirit of the law is maintained despite the technicality of individual actions. See § 1.2 for the authority of the Accords Desk in these determinations.

body.heading: Effective Date; Savings
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords shall take effect immediately upon the ratification of the final seals by Archmage Veyra. All prior accords, treaties, and ephemeral agreements entered into by the Guild prior to the signing of the Accords shall remain in effect only insofar as they do not directly conflict with the provisions of this Codex. In the event of a conflict between a prior agreement and the current Accords, the Accords shall supersede the prior agreement in all matters.

Furthermore, this Codex provides for the "Savings" of existing rights and licenses. Any Caster who held a valid license prior to the enactment of these Accords shall retain said license until its natural expiration, provided they comply with the new regulatory standards. However, it is explicitly stated that dead citations within Part XIV of the old records do not revive any repealed schemes or defunct laws. The expiration of a law does not imply the preservation of the rights granted under said law; once a scheme is repealed, all associated privileges, exemptions, and protections are extinguished. The Guild shall not be held liable for the loss of privileges resulting from the transition to the current regulatory framework.

body.heading: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
body.text:
To ensure the integrity of official documentation, the Guild maintains a strict standard for what constitutes a valid Seal or Stamp of the Accords Desk. A seal is a unique, magically-reactive mark applied to a document to verify its authenticity, its origin, and the authority of the signatory. Any mark that does not possess the specific resonance of the Guild’s primary sigil shall be considered void.

It is explicitly clarified for the prevention of fraudulent claims that certain common objects or marks are not seals. Specifically, garlic bread placed upon a map, regardless of its placement or the intent of the individual, is not a seal and confers no legal status to the map it rests upon. Furthermore, a concussed unnamed pilot, or any individual in a state of physical or mental incapacity who is not a certified officer of the Guild, is not a certifying officer. Any document "signed" or "stamped" by an individual in such a state shall be deemed a forgery. No entity may claim that a mark of personal significance, a common culinary item, or the action of a non-certified individual constitutes a valid authorization under the Autumnwood Accords. See § 1.9 for further clarification on non-certifying marks.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
This section serves to establish the procedural integrity of the Codex. A reserved catchline indicates a specific location within the legal framework that has been set aside for future expansion or specific administrative use. The existence of a reserved section does not imply a lack of oversight; rather, it signifies that the Guild recognizes the necessity of evolving legislation in a dynamic magical landscape.

A blank section or a reserved catchline remains a valid place in the book and shall be treated with the same respect as a populated section. No Caster may claim that a lack of specific text in a reserved section constitutes a "loophole" or a license to act without restriction. If a conduct is not specifically addressed in a populated section, it shall be governed by the general principles of the Accords and the mediation of Archmage Veyra. The Accords Desk reserves the right to populate these sections at any time to address emerging threats, such as new schools of magic or external pressures from the Regal Empire. Any attempt to exploit the "blankness" of a reserved section to bypass the spirit of the law shall be met with immediate referral to the Paradox Trial.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.brief: Define caster, value, material alteration, transfiguration, disclosure, familiar, pocket, Quiet List, Paradox Trial. Numbered terms. Boring on purpose.

body.heading: Definitions
body.text:
The following terms are hereby established as the standard lexicon for all legal proceedings, adjudications, and regulatory oversight conducted under the authority of the Autumnwood Accords. Any ambiguity arising from colloquial usage shall be resolved in favor of these specific definitions. See § 1.1.

1. Caster: Any sentient entity, biological or otherwise, capable of channeling, weaving, or manifesting thaumaturgical energy, whether through innate ability, external artifacts, or learned methodology.

2. Value: The measurable significance of an object, spell, or magical effect, encompassing its market price, its historical weight within the Midlands, and its potential for collateral metaphysical damage.

3. Material Alteration: Any process by which the physical, chemical, or metaphysical properties of a substance are fundamentally changed through the application of magic, including but not limited to the shifting of states of matter or the extraction of essence.

4. Transfiguration: A specific sub-category of Material Alteration involving the complete structural reconfiguration of an object or organism from one form into another, requiring distinct licensing from the Innovator faction for high-complexity shifts.

5. Disclosure: The mandatory act of revealing the true nature, risks, and limitations of a magical effect, item, or research project to all relevant parties, including buyers, observers, and the Accords Desk.

6. Familiar: A non-human entity, spirit, or beast bound to a Caster through a formal symbiotic or servile contract, subject to the same jurisdictional regulations as the Caster themselves.

7. Pocket: Any extradimensional space, contained reality, or localized fold in the weave utilized for storage, habitation, or the concealment of items.

8. Quiet List: A non-public, classified registry of specific arcane arts, artifacts, or individuals whose existence or activities are deemed a risk to the stability of the Midlands. Reference see § 300.3 for procedural nuances.

9. Paradox Trial: The formal judicial process by which the Guild adjudicates violations of the Accords, involving a council of peers and resulting in sanctions ranging from magic sealing to permanent containment in a pocket dimension.

body.heading: Construction; Aggregation of Conduct
body.text:
The prosecution or adjudication of a violation under the Autumnwood Accords shall not be hindered by the fragmentation of a Caster’s actions into disparate events. The Accords Desk maintains the authority to aggregate multiple instances of minor non-compliance, even if separated by time, geography, or intervening incidents, into a singular finding of systemic violation. This principle ensures that a pattern of reckless conduct cannot be shielded by the mere fact that no single act reached the threshold of a felony.

Furthermore, the proximity of conduct to the prohibited schools—specifically those identified as forbidden by Archmage Theron—shall be considered an aggravating factor in the aggregation of conduct. If a Caster demonstrates a persistent inclination toward the Unsanctioned Arts, the Accords Desk may treat any subsequent minor transgression as a primary violation. The intent to circumvent the stability of the Midlands through a series of incremental, "legal" steps is viewed as a singular, continuous act of subversion.

This construction applies equally to the use of restricted research. A Caster who obtains permission for a single, limited experiment but subsequently expands the scope of that research through unauthorized iterative testing shall be held liable for the totality of the expansion. The burden of proof remains on the Caster to demonstrate that each step of a magical progression was independently authorized; failure to provide such documentation shall result in the aggregation of all associated activities under a single breach of the Innovator faction’s research protocols.

In matters of civil liability, the aggregation of conduct shall also apply to the distribution of magical goods. A merchant or Caster who knowingly sells a series of items that, while individually compliant, collectively facilitate a prohibited ritual shall be subject to seizure of all related stock. The Accords Desk reserves the right to interpret the "totality of the effect" as the primary metric for determining violation, rather than the isolated properties of individual components.

body.heading: Effective Date; Savings
body.text:
These provisions of the Autumnwood Accords shall take effect immediately upon the final ratification by Archmage Veyra and the subsequent recording by the Accords Desk. Any previous agreements, local customs, or minor pacts that conflict with the current Codex shall be rendered subordinate. However, where no conflict exists, prior Accords shall remain in force as supplementary guidelines to the primary regulatory framework.

The "Savings" clause dictates that the repeal of a specific magical regulation does not automatically restore any previous, superseded schemes that were explicitly struck from the record. For the purposes of legal clarity, any citation within Part XIV that refers to a repealed scheme is considered a "dead citation." Such citations possess no legal weight and do not revive the rules they once referenced. If a Caster seeks to rely on a defunct law, they must petition the Accords Desk for a formal "Re-enactment Decree," which is rarely granted and subject to the scrutiny of the Conservators.

The Accords Desk shall not recognize the validity of "Ghost Laws"—rules that have been functionally abandoned by the Guild but remain in printed archives. If a rule is not currently listed in the active Codex or explicitly preserved by a Savings clause, it is considered void. This prevents the manipulation of the legal system by citing archaic, often dangerous, methodologies that the Innovators have sought to abolish for the safety of the Midlands.

Any contracts entered into by mages prior to the enactment of the Autumnwood Accords remain binding provided they do not violate the fundamental prohibitions of the current Codex. In instances where a pre-existing contract requires the use of a forbidden school of magic, the contract shall be deemed "void ab initio" at the first point of violation. The Guild does not provide restitution for contracts rendered void by the Accords; the loss of such agreements is the sole responsibility of the contracting parties.

body.heading: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
body.text:
The validity of a magical authorization, permit, or certificate rests solely upon the presence of an official Seal of the Accords Desk or the specific authorized stamp of the respective faction (Conservator or Innovator). A seal is a unique thaumaturgical signature that verifies the authenticity of a document, the identity of the issuing officer, and the specific parameters of the granted permission. Any attempt to forge, replicate, or "echo" such a seal through sympathetic magic is a high felony, punishable by immediate Paradox Trial.

It is explicitly stated for the avoidance of doubt that certain common items or conditions do not constitute a legal Seal. Specifically, the presence of organic matter, such as garlic bread, placed upon a map or any other document, does not serve as a seal of authenticity, nor does it provide any legal protection or jurisdictional immunity. Similarly, the possession of a map—even one containing detailed cartography of the Heartstone or rift zones—does not constitute a raid license or a permit for unauthorized field use.

Furthermore, a person who is physically incapacitated, including those who are concussed, unconscious, or otherwise unable to provide coherent testimony, is not considered a certifying officer for the purposes of the Accords. Any "authorization" granted by an unnamed or incapacitated individual is null and void. A certifying officer must be of sound mind, hold a recognized rank within the Guild or a recognized ally such as the Goodstyle Artisans, and be capable of providing a clear, verbal, and magically-traceable affirmation of the document's contents.

Finally, the Accords Desk clarifies that the "Iron Mandate" is not a seal of this jurisdiction. Because the Iron Mandate is the law of the Regal Empire and the Iron Legion, it carries no weight within the Midlands unless specifically brokered by Archmage Veyra. Mages operating under the Mandate do not possess Guild seals and are subject to the full weight of the Paradox Trial should they interfere with the stability of the Autumn Wood.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
The inclusion of Reserved Catchlines within this Codex serves as a formal acknowledgement of the Guild's right to expand and refine the legal framework of the Autumnwood Accords as necessary. A reserved catchline is a designated space within the Codex intended for future legislative insertion. The presence of a reserved section does not imply a vacuum of law; rather, it signifies a designated area where the Accords may be amended to address emerging magical phenomena, new threats from the Cosmic Jesters, or technological advancements in the restricted research fields.

While a section may currently appear blank or contain only a placeholder, it remains a recognized part of the book's structure. This ensures that the internal numbering and organizational hierarchy of the Codex remain consistent even as new laws are drafted and ratified. Any legal argument suggesting that a lack of text in a reserved section constitutes a "permit for any action" is strictly prohibited. Absence of a specific prohibition in a reserved section does not equate to the authorization of conduct; all actions remain subject to the general prohibitions of the preceding sections and the overarching authority of Archmage Veyra.

The process for filling a Reserved Catchline involves a formal petition to the Accords Desk. Such petitions must be sponsored by either the Conservators or the Innovators. If a petition is approved, the new text shall be inserted into the reserved space, maintaining the existing numbering. If a petition is denied, the section shall remain reserved until a different proposal is submitted. This mechanism prevents the "ad-hoc" insertion of laws and ensures that every new regulation undergoes the proper mediation process.

Furthermore, the Accords Desk reserves the right to "Pause" a reserved catchline. If a proposed law is deemed too volatile or if its consequences are still being surveyed—particularly in the case of rift-adjacent magic—the Desk may place a stay on that section. During a stay, no law may be enacted in that section, and no Caster may cite it as a basis for behavior. This ensures that the legal evolution of the Midlands is deliberate, measured, and protected against the reckless impulses of the radical factions.

sections.title: Construction; Aggregation of Conduct
sections.brief: Fragmentation of conduct shall not prevent a finding of violation. Same rule as the filed photo.

body.heading: Construction; Aggregation of Conduct
body.text:
The legal interpretation of thaumaturgical transgressions under the Autumnwood Accords shall not be predicated upon the isolation of discrete acts. Pursuant to the principles of holistic oversight, the fragmentation of conduct shall not prevent a finding of violation. A mage who commits a series of minor infractions, each of which might individually fall below the threshold of a formal Paradox Trial, may nonetheless be found in breach of the Accords if the cumulative weight of said conduct demonstrates a systemic disregard for the safety of the Midlands or the integrity of the weave.

The Accords Desk reserves the right to aggregate multiple instances of unauthorized mana-leakage, minor property damage, or procedural negligence into a single comprehensive indictment. For instance, a practitioner who repeatedly fails to register minor sensory-scrying devices while simultaneously neglecting to report minor localized fluctuations in the ley lines may be prosecuted for a unified pattern of negligence. The prosecution shall not be required to prove that any single act constitutes a capital offense; rather, the evidence shall be presented as a continuous tapestry of non-compliance.

This construction is intended to prevent the "death by a thousand cuts" defense, wherein a rogue practitioner attempts to circumvent the Aegis Magi's oversight by ensuring that no single action reaches the requisite severity for intervention. By aggregating conduct, the Accords ensure that the spirit of the law—the preservation of stability as championed by the Conservators and the regulated advancement of the Innovators—is maintained against those who seek to exploit technicalities. See § 1.6 for further clarification on the lexicon of "systemic disregard."

All findings of violation based on aggregated conduct shall be recorded in the primary registry of the Autumnwood Accords Desk. The presiding council shall have the discretion to determine the appropriate severity of the sanction, ranging from a formal reprimand to a full Paradox Trial, based on the qualitative nature of the aggregated acts. This rule remains in effect regardless of the temporal distance between the individual acts, provided they can be linked to a singular intent or a recurring pattern of behavior.

body.heading: Effective Date; Savings
body.text:
The provisions of the Autumnwood Accords shall take effect immediately upon the ratification of the founding signatures by Archmage Veyra and the respective heads of the Conservator and Innovator factions. All prior Accords, temporary mandates, and localized magical treaties that were superseded by the ratification of this Codex are hereby rendered subordinate to the current framework. However, any specific protections or rights established in prior Accords that are not explicitly revoked by this Codex shall remain in force, provided they do not conflict with the primary objectives of the current Accords.

Regarding the preservation of existing legal statuses, the principle of "Savings" ensures that the transition to this new regulatory body does not result in a total vacuum of law. Any ongoing investigations, active seals, or pending Paradox Trials initiated under previous frameworks shall remain active and be adjudicated according to the procedural standards of the Accords Desk at the time of their commencement. The transition of authority from previous regimes to the current Accords Desk does not constitute a stay of execution or a dissolution of existing magical restraints.

Be advised that the presence of dead citations within Part XIV of the archival records shall not, under any circumstances, revive repealed schemes or defunct regulations. The mere existence of a reference to an obsolete law within a secondary text does not grant that law any legal standing or binding power. If a practitioner seeks to rely on a repealed mandate, they must demonstrate that the mandate was specifically preserved by a secondary "Savings" clause; otherwise, the Accords Desk shall treat the citation as a historical curiosity with no bearing on current legal standing.

Any ambiguities arising from the overlap between saved prior rights and new Accords provisions shall be mediated by Archmage Veyra. In instances where a saved right directly contradicts a new prohibition, the new prohibition shall prevail, as the Accords prioritize the collective stability of the Midlands over individual historical privileges. See § 1.5 for the overarching priority of the Accords over external and internal mandates.

body.heading: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
body.text:
For the purposes of the Autumnwood Accords, a "Seal" is defined as a legally recognized mark of authorization, either physical or metaphysical, applied by a certified officer of the Accords Desk or an authorized representative of the Aegis Magi. Only such marks may be used to certify the legality of restricted research, the issuance of Provisional Guild Passes, or the verification of official cartography. Any mark, sigil, or emblem that does not originate from a recognized authority is deemed a "False Seal" and is subject to immediate seizure and the prosecution of the bearer.

It is expressly clarified that common culinary markings, symbols of personal preference, or incidental markings of no official capacity do not constitute seals. Specifically, the presence of garlic bread markings or any related culinary iconography upon a map, scroll, or artifact shall not be interpreted as a seal of authenticity or a mark of Guild approval. The Accords Desk will not recognize such marks as evidence of legal status, nor shall their presence be used as a basis for any regulatory exemption.

Furthermore, the physical or mental state of a person does not determine their capacity to hold a seal. A concussed, unconscious, or otherwise incapacitated unnamed pilot, regardless of their previous rank or standing, is not a certifying officer and cannot provide valid authorization for the movement of goods, the activation of rifts, or the crossing of restricted zones. Any "authorization" purportedly granted by a person in such a state is null and void. The Accords Desk requires a conscious, voluntary act of certification by a recognized official to validate any official action.

Practitioners are cautioned against the use of "pseudo-seals"—magical constructs that mimic the appearance of Guild authority without the underlying legal weight. The use of a pseudo-seal to bypass the Innovator's permission requirements or to circumvent Conservator restrictions shall be treated as a high-level violation of the Accords. See § 1.6 for the full list of certified authorities.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
The inclusion of reserved catchlines within this Codex is a fundamental structural necessity of the Autumnwood Accords. A reserved catchline signifies a designated location within the legal framework that is currently vacant of specific statutes but remains a permanent fixture of the book’s architecture. These sections are not "empty" in the sense of being ignored; rather, they are placeholders for future legislative expansion, amendments, or the insertion of specific emergency decrees as dictated by the Archmage Sovereign.

By maintaining these reserved spaces, the Accords Desk ensures that the legal framework can be updated and expanded without necessitating a complete re-indexing of the Codex. When a new law is drafted to address a novel magical phenomenon, a new rift, or a shift in the political landscape between the Conservators and the Innovators, it may be inserted into a corresponding reserved section. This allows for a modular approach to governance, where the foundational structure remains constant while the specific applications of the law can evolve.

The existence of a reserved catchline does not imply that the law is "under construction" in a way that delays its current validity. A blank section remains a place in the book, and its presence does not grant any temporary immunity from the laws already codified in preceding sections.
