Practitioners should not assume that a lack of specific text in a reserved section constitutes a "gray area" or a lack of regulation; rather, it signifies that the Accords Desk has not yet deemed a specific sub-topic worthy of a permanent, standalone statute.

Any request to occupy a reserved catchline with a specific decree must be submitted to the Accords Desk for review. Such a decree must be vetted by both the Conservator and Innovator factions to ensure it does not violate the core tenets of the Accords. Once approved, the new statute will be permanently bound to the Codex under its respective reserved heading, becoming a functional part of the law. See § 1.2 for the enacting authority regarding these additions.

sections.title: Effective Date; Savings
sections.brief: Prior Accords remain. Dead citations in Part XIV do not revive repealed schemes.

body.heading: Effective Date; Savings
body.text:
The provisions contained within this Codex shall be deemed to take effect immediately upon the final ratification of the Autumnwood Accords by the Archmage Sovereign. This legal instrument serves as the primary governing authority for all thaumaturgical practice within the Midlands and all territories under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords. Any actions taken by mages, practitioners, or affiliated entities prior to the date of enactment shall be judged based on the prevailing laws of that time, unless such actions fall under the specific transitional provisions outlined in the Sovereign’s Decree of Continuity.

Prior Accords, treaties, and local ordinances that are not explicitly repealed by the text of this Codex shall remain in full force and effect. The existence of the Autumnwood Accords does not constitute a wholesale dissolution of historical agreements, provided those agreements do not directly conflict with the fundamental mandates of the Accords. Where a conflict arises between a prior agreement and a current provision of this Codex, the Accords shall prevail as the superior authority. Practitioners seeking to maintain the validity of historical pacts must ensure such pacts are registered with the Autumnwood Accords Desk for reconciliation.

Notwithstanding the preservation of prior agreements, the legal status of repealed sections is strictly defined. The invocation of a repealed section as a justification for current conduct is strictly prohibited. Pursuant to the principles of legal finality, the repeal of a statutory provision renders it null and void for all future purposes. See § 1401.2 for further clarification on the status of dead citations. No practitioner may argue that a repealed scheme, despite its historical significance or its former utility, holds any residual weight or provides a permit for contemporary action.

Furthermore, the repeal of a scheme does not grant the right to "revive" the law through mere citation or persistent practice. A section that has been struck from the Codex is legally deceased; it cannot be resurrected by the actions of the Innovators, the dictates of the Conservators, or the demands of external powers such as the Regal Empire. The Accords Desk shall not recognize any "ghost laws" or "shadow precedents" derived from defunct titles. This ensures that the legal landscape remains navigable and that the sovereign authority of Archmage Veyra remains absolute and unambiguous. For matters regarding the preservation of specific historical rights, see § 1.8.

body.heading: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
body.text:
The authority of the Autumnwood Accords is manifested through the official application of Seals and Stamps. A Seal is a legally recognized mark of authentication, issued by the Accords Desk or a designated high-ranking official, signifying that a document, research permit, or magical artifact has been vetted and approved for use. Such seals carry the weight of the Sovereign’s mediation and the collective oversight of the Conservators and the Innovators. A stamp, being a secondary mark of administrative processing, may be used to indicate the status of a filing or the completion of a bureaucratic requirement, but it does not carry the same weight of sovereign sanction as a Seal.

The Guild maintains a strict distinction between legitimate marks of authority and mundane, artistic, or coincidental markings. For the purposes of this Codex, a Seal must be a deliberate act of magical or administrative certification. It is expressly stated that a non-official mark, even one that mimics the aesthetic of a Guild Seal, shall not be recognized as a valid instrument of authority. This distinction is critical in the prevention of forgery and the unauthorized exercise of magical rights. See § 1.6 for definitions regarding authorized agents.

To ensure clarity in the face of common misconceptions or absurdities, the Accords Desk hereby establishes specific exclusions. It is expressly decreed that garlic bread depicted upon a map—regardless of its size, placement, or perceived importance—does not constitute a Seal. The presence of culinary imagery or any other non-magical, non-administrative notation on a map does not grant the bearer of said map any special privileges, licenses, or exemptions from the laws of the Midlands. Furthermore, the presence of a map does not serve as a raid license; see § 1.6.

Equally, the Accords Desk clarifies the status of personnel. A concussed unnamed pilot, or any individual suffering from physical or mental impairment who lacks the requisite certification and clarity of mind, is not a certifying officer. The authority to issue Seals or Stamps requires a clear mandate from the Sovereign or the designated faction leaders. Any "certification" obtained from an individual who is not a recognized official of the Accords, or who is currently incapacitated, shall be considered null and void. Such actions may be grounds for a Paradox Trial. No individual may claim that a mark of authority was "validly" issued by a source that the Accords do not recognize as a legitimate seat of power.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
The Accords Desk maintains the right to reserve specific sections within this Codex for future expansion, amendment, or the inclusion of specialized regulations. A reserved catchline serves as a placeholder within the legal architecture of the Autumnwood Accords, ensuring that the structure of the law remains intact even when specific provisions are yet to be drafted. The existence of a reserved catchline signifies that the law is a living document, capable of evolving to meet new thaumaturgical challenges, political shifts, or the emergence of new magical phenomena.

A reserved section is not a "blank" space in the sense of being legally empty; rather, it is a designated area of potentiality. While a reserved catchline does not currently carry a specific mandate, the fact that it exists in the Codex means that the Guild acknowledges the necessity of future regulation regarding that topic. When a new law is eventually drafted to fill a reserved section, it shall be integrated into the Codex while maintaining the sequential order of the existing titles. This prevents the need for retroactive renumbering and ensures that the hierarchy of the Accords remains stable.

Practitioners should be aware that the presence of a reserved catchline does not imply that the conduct associated with that topic is currently unregulated. In the absence of a specific provision within a reserved section, the general principles of the Accords—specifically those regarding the balance between Conservator stability and Innovator research—shall apply. However, the Accords Desk reserves the right to enact emergency measures or temporary directives that may address matters currently held in reserved sections until a permanent statute is codified.

The Accords Desk shall not be held liable for the perceived ambiguity of a reserved section. It is the duty of the mages to seek clarification from the Archmage Sovereign or the relevant faction leaders (Archmage Theron for stability-based queries, or Janna Brightspark for research-based inquiries) should they require guidance on matters not yet fully detailed in the Codex. The preservation of these placeholders is a fundamental requirement of the Accords, ensuring that the legal body of the Autumnwood Accords remains comprehensive and prepared for the complexities of the arcane future. See § 1.3 for instructions on the interpretation of these provisions.

sections.title: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
sections.brief: Garlic bread on a map is not a seal. A concussed unnamed pilot is not a certifying officer.

body.heading: Seals, Stamps, and What Is Not a Seal
body.text:
All official instruments, mandates, and permissions issued under the authority of the Autumnwood Accords shall bear a certified seal of the Guild. A seal is defined as a distinct, magically-reactive impression or sigil that validates the authenticity of a document, the intent of the signatory, and the legal standing of the contents therein. For the purposes of this Codex, a seal must be verifiable by the Aegis Magi through standard resonance testing. Any document bearing a mark that lacks the requisite arcane signature, or any mark that has been mimicked through mundane forgery or low-level illusion, shall be deemed null and void. The absence of a proper seal shall render any instruction, regardless of the status of the individual providing it, non-binding upon the members of the Guild.

To ensure clarity in administrative proceedings and to prevent the misappropriation of authority, the Guild hereby establishes a list of specific non-validating markings. Specifically, the presence of food items, culinary notations, or mundane geographic markings—including, but not limited to, garlic bread on a map—shall not constitute a seal. Furthermore, the physical presence of an individual, regardless of their perceived expertise or current state of consciousness, does not constitute a certification of legal authority. A concussed unnamed pilot, or any individual lacking a verified identity and a designated rank within the Accords, is not a certifying officer. No verbal command or physical gesture from an uncertified individual may be interpreted as a valid issuance of a Guild mandate.

Furthermore, the Guild shall not recognize any "seal" derived from unauthorized sources. Marks associated with the Regal Empire, the Iron Legion, or the Silver Flame are strictly prohibited from being recognized as valid within the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords. Any mage found to be acting upon a seal from an opposing faction shall be subject to immediate review by the Conservators. The validity of a seal is inextricably linked to the source of its issuance; therefore, any seal that cannot be traced back to a sanctioned office of the Guild, or an authorized representative of the Innovators or Conservators, is to be treated as a decorative element without legal weight. Mages are cautioned that relying upon an unverified mark for the execution of high-level thaumaturgy may result in the immediate revocation of their provisional status. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
This section serves as a formal reservation of space within the Autumnwood Accords Codex. The inclusion of reserved catchlines is a structural necessity of the Accords, ensuring that the legal framework remains expandable and adaptable to the evolving nature of thaumaturgy. A reserved catchline constitutes a designated placeholder for future legislation, amendments, or specific regulations that have been identified as necessary but have not yet been ratified by the Archmage Sovereign or the presiding council of the Conservators and Innovators. The existence of a reserved section does not imply a current lack of law, but rather provides a designated locus for the insertion of new mandates without necessitating a total restructuring of the Codex's numerical sequence.

A blank or reserved section within this book is still a place in the book. It represents a commitment by the Guild to maintain an organized and systematic approach to governance. When a new law is ratified, it shall be inserted into the nearest available reserved section that corresponds to its subject matter. This prevents the "crowding" of existing statutes and ensures that the legal progression of the Guild remains coherent. Any mage seeking to reference a section that appears currently blank should be aware that the section is legally active in its capacity as a placeholder; however, no rights, permissions, or prohibitions are currently enforceable until such time as the section is populated with ratified prose.

The preservation of these placeholders is essential for the administrative integrity of the Autumnwood Accords. It allows the Guild to anticipate the growth of the "Unsanctioned Arts" regulations and the potential expansion of the "Restricted Research" permits. By maintaining these reserved spaces, the Guild ensures that the legal architecture of the Midlands remains robust enough to house the complexities of future magical breakthroughs. Any attempt to interpret a reserved catchline as containing "implied" law is strictly prohibited. If a section is reserved, it is silent. The silence of a reserved section is the silence of the law itself, until the Archmage Sovereign deigns to speak through the formal recording of new text. See § 1.7.

sections.title: Reserved Catchlines
sections.brief: How reserved sections work. A blank is still a place in the book.

body.heading: § 1.10 Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
The structure of this Codex is predicated upon the principle of continuity and the preservation of the legal vacuum. It is hereby established that the physical and metaphysical architecture of the Autumnwood Accords requires a fixed sequence of articles, regardless of whether said articles contain active mandates, prohibitions, or specific regulatory procedures. A reserved catchline, denoted by a numerical designation without corresponding prose, shall not be interpreted as a clerical error, a lapse in transcription, or a void in the sovereign’s authority. Rather, such a designation serves as a permanent placeholder within the sacred geometry of the Accords. It signifies a designated space for future legislative expansion, a "silent seat" at the table of law that remains available for the insertion of new statutes as the magical landscape of the Midlands evolves.

The preservation of these reserved sections is essential to maintain the integrity of the Codex’s internal referencing system. Should a section be omitted entirely from the numerical sequence, all subsequent citations would shift, thereby rendering the cross-references of the existing Accords null and void. To prevent such a catastrophic collapse of legal coherence, any section designated as reserved must remain in the registry in perpetuity. The Archivists of the Autumnwood Accords Desk are strictly prohibited from renumbering the Codex to "close the gap." If a new law is drafted that pertains to a matter previously unaddressed, the Archmage Sovereign may, at her discretion, authorize the insertion of the text into a reserved catchline, provided that the new text does not conflict with the existing primary mandates.

Furthermore, the existence of a reserved catchline constitutes a "latent authority." While a blank section does not currently impose a specific burden, duty, or privilege upon the mages of the Guild, it serves as a formal recognition by the Sovereign that the law is a living organism. It acknowledges that the current scope of the Accords may be insufficient to address future paradoxes, technological leaps by the Innovators, or traditionalist mandates from the Conservators. By maintaining these vacancies, the Guild ensures that the legal framework is prepared for the unpredictable nature of arcane progression. Any attempt by an outside entity, such as the Regal Empire or the Silver Flame, to claim that a reserved section implies a lack of jurisdiction is hereby rejected; the silence of a catchline is the silence of the Sovereign’s deliberate restraint, not a surrender of power.

In the event of a dispute regarding the application of a reserved catchline, the presiding magistrate shall refer to § 1.3 How to Read This Codex to ensure the standard of interpretation is upheld. If a mage seeks to argue that a lack of text in a specific section grants them immunity from the broader spirit of the Accords, such an argument shall be dismissed as a violation of the principle of Aggregation of Conduct as defined in § 1.7. The Codex is a complete and unified body of law; the presence of a reserved catchline does not create a "lawless zone" within the statutes. It is merely a placeholder for a future truth, a silent vessel awaiting the ink of the Sovereign’s decree. All mages shall proceed under the understanding that the Codex is a finished structure of intent, where even the empty spaces are bound by the weight of the Archmage’s authority.

body.heading: Reserved Catchlines
body.text:
The structure of this Codex is designed to accommodate the fluid and often volatile nature of arcane jurisprudence. Pursuant to the administrative guidelines established by the Archmage Sovereign, certain sections of this book are designated as Reserved Catchlines. A Reserved Catchline represents a formal placeholder within the legislative sequence, signifying that a specific topic is recognized by the Guild as a matter of potential future regulation, even in the absence of currently enacted prose. The existence of a blank space or a catchline without accompanying descriptive text does not imply a vacuum of authority; rather, it constitutes a "latent provision." These sections are preserved to ensure that the internal numbering of the Accords remains contiguous and that no subsequent legislative additions can disrupt the structural integrity of the primary legal framework.

The preservation of these spaces serves a dual purpose of administrative continuity and preemptive governance. By reserving a catchline, the Guild acknowledges that certain behaviors, magical phenomena, or jurisdictional disputes are currently under observation or deliberation by the relevant factional councils. For instance, a blank section under the oversight of the Conservators may represent a pending prohibition on a burgeoning school of magic, while a reserved space under the Innovators may signify a pending authorization for restricted research. Until such time as the Archmage Sovereign issues a formal decree to populate the catchline with specific mandates, the space remains a "silent sentinel." Any attempt by a practitioner to argue that a lack of text equates to a lack of oversight shall be summarily rejected by the Aegis Magi.

Furthermore, the doctrine of Reserved Catchlines prevents "legislative drift." Without these designated placeholders, the insertion of new laws regarding emerging magical threats—such as unauthorized rift activity or the discovery of new Heartstones—would require the renumbering of the entire Codex. Such a process would create significant confusion among the signatories of the Autumnwood Accords and potentially lead to the misapplication of existing statutes. Therefore, the Accords maintain that a Reserved Catchline is a fixed point in the legal geography of the Midlands. It is a binding commitment by the Guild to address the topic eventually, and its presence in the book serves as a notice to all mages that the Guild is cognizant of the matter, even if the specific penalties or permissions are not yet codified.

In matters of litigation or the determination of intent during a Paradox Trial, the presence of a Reserved Catchline shall be interpreted as an indication of the Guild's intent to regulate. If a dispute arises over a practice that falls under a Reserved Catchline, the presiding council may invoke the principle of "Provisional Precaution." This allows the council to impose temporary restrictions or demands for cessation on a practice until the formal text is ratified. Practitioners are advised to consult with their respective faction leaders—be they of the Conservators or the Innovators—to determine if a specific arcane endeavor currently occupies a reserved space. Failure to adhere to the spirit of a Reserved Catchline while awaiting its formal codification may result in a finding of "Willful Negligence of Governance," punishable under the standard protocols of the Paradox Trial. See § 1.8 for the overarching authority regarding the commencement of these provisions.

sections.title: Guild Offices Named
sections.brief: Accords Desk, Clerk, Conservator chair, Innovator chair. No new characters.

body.heading: Guild Offices Named
body.text:
The administrative structure of the Mages' Guild, as recognized under the Autumnwood Accords, shall be confined to the designated seats of authority and functional offices established by the Sovereign. These offices are hereby codified to prevent the emergence of unauthorized administrative bodies or the fabrication of titles by independent practitioners. The primary seat of governance is the Accords Desk, which serves as the central repository for the legal codification of thaumaturgy. The Clerk of the Accords Desk shall be the primary custodian of the bound codes, responsible for the preservation, filing, and maintenance of all legislative records. The Clerk serves as the gatekeeper of the Accords, ensuring that every transcription adheres to the stylistic and structural requirements of the Guild.

The legislative oversight of the Guild is divided between two primary chairs, which represent the fundamental ideological schism of the body. The Conservator Chair shall represent the interests of stability, the preservation of ancestral methods, and the strict prohibition of forbidden schools. The Innovator Chair shall represent the interests of progress, the expansion of arcane boundaries, and the regulated exploration of new methodologies. These two chairs, while often in opposition, are the only recognized legislative seats for the purpose of establishing new Accords or amending existing ones. No other titles, chairs, or offices shall be recognized as having legislative power.

Any individual claiming a title of authority not explicitly listed within this section, or any individual attempting to establish an "Office of Research," "Hall of Secrets," or any other self-appointed administrative seat, shall be deemed an unauthorized entity. The Guild shall not recognize the existence of any characters, personalities, or fictional personas as legitimate administrative agents. The Accords Desk does not recognize the authority of "shadow cabinets," "secret councils," or "informal committees" unless they are formally ratified and recorded by the Sovereign. All actions taken by individuals outside these named offices are considered personal acts and do not carry the weight of Guild mandate. For matters regarding the definitions of these roles, see § 1.6.

body.heading: Who May Speak for the Guild
body.text:
The authority to represent the Mages' Guild in external negotiations, diplomatic treaties, or public declarations is strictly limited to those individuals explicitly granted "Voice" by the Sovereign or the presiding Quorum. A primary principle of this section is the expiration of temporary mouths; any individual granted the right to speak for the Guild for a specific duration, purpose, or event shall have their authority automatically revoked upon the conclusion of said event. The Guild shall not be bound by the statements of an envoy whose mandate has lapsed, nor shall such statements be considered a binding commitment of the Accords Desk.

Furthermore, the Guild clarifies that the presence of a familiar, spirit, or magical construct does not constitute a legal speech or a binding agreement. A familiar’s nod, gesture, or telepathic confirmation is not a speech unless that specific familiar has been formally listed in the Guild’s Register of Authorized Mouths. The Guild shall not be held liable for the actions or "agreements" made by a familiar acting on its master's behalf, as the familiar lacks the legal capacity to bind the Guild to any contract, treaty, or Accord. Only a conscious, sentient agent with a valid, non-expired mandate may bind the Guild to a legal obligation.

In the event of a dispute regarding a statement made by a representative, the Clerk shall review the duration of the mandate. If the representative spoke outside the temporal or thematic boundaries of their granted "mouth," the statement shall be stricken from the record as a mere personal opinion. Any attempt to use a familiar’s communication as a basis for a legal claim against the Guild shall be dismissed summarily. The Guild maintains that the sanctity of the Accords requires a deliberate, human-centric (or sentient-sentient) declaration of intent. See § 1.2 for the source of this authority.

body.heading: Quorum of the Desk
body.text:
The legislative power of the Accords Desk is activated only when a valid Quorum is present. The standard Quorum for the deliberation and passage of any new Accord, amendment, or regulatory decree shall consist of exactly one Conservator and one Innovator. This requirement is designed to ensure that no single faction can unilaterally alter the laws of magic without the consent of the opposing ideology. If the Conservator Chair and the Innovator Chair are both present, their agreement constitutes a binding mandate. If only one chair is present, no legislative action may be taken, and the matter must be tabled until a representative of the opposing faction can be convened.

In instances where a chair is unavailable, a secondary Quorum may be established by a Clerk of the Accords Desk and a recognized member of the Guild who possesses a "Headache" designation. A "Headache" is defined as a mage who has been formally recognized by the Sovereign as possessing a sufficiently complex, persistent, and legally-recognized grievance or cognitive burden that qualifies them for emergency consultation. This secondary Quorum is intended for the processing of administrative backlog and minor regulatory clarifications rather than the drafting of new laws. A Clerk and a Headache may authorize the filing of records and the stamping of existing permits, but they lack the authority to alter the fundamental Accords.

Should a situation arise where neither a chair nor a secondary Quorum is available, the Accords Desk shall enter a state of administrative suspension. During such a suspension, no new laws may be enacted, and all pending applications must remain in a state of "Pending Review." The Sovereign, Archmage Veyra, may issue a temporary decree to bypass a Quorum impasse, but such decrees are subject to immediate ratification by the next convened Quorum. All procedures regarding the seating of the Desk and the recognition of chairs are governed by the foundational agreements. See § 1.5 for the priority of these rules over external mandates.

body.heading: Records of Speech
body.text:
The Accords Desk maintains a strict policy regarding the documentation of legislative and administrative discourse. Any spoken vote, decree, or formal declaration made during a session of the Accords Desk that is not subsequently filed with the Clerk shall be deemed a rumor and possess no legal standing. The Guild recognizes that the spoken word is ephemeral and susceptible to corruption; therefore, the act of filing is the only mechanism by which a statement becomes law. Mages who participate in the deliberation of the Accords are strictly prohibited from bragging about, quoting, or enforcing any "agreed-upon" points that have not been formally transcribed and stamped by the Clerk.

The Clerk shall maintain the Official Record of Speech. Upon the conclusion of a session, the Clerk shall summarize the votes and resolutions. Any member of the Guild who attempts to cite a "previous agreement" that does not appear in the bound code shall be subject to a citation for misinformation. This rule serves to prevent the "Shadow Accord" phenomenon, where informal promises made in private chambers are used to circumvent the public laws of the Autumnwood Accords. If a mage claims a vote was taken, the burden of proof lies with the mage to produce the filed record. If no record exists, the vote is legally non-existent.

Furthermore, the act of bragging or publicizing unfiled votes is considered a breach of administrative decorum. While the Guild encourages vigorous debate between the Conservators and the Innovators, the finality of that debate must be anchored in the written word. Any mage who attempts to influence the Guild’s actions based on "what was said in the hall" shall be directed to the Clerk to find the proper filing. This ensures that the Accords remain a stable, navigable body of law rather than a shifting collection of verbal promises. See § 1.7 for the treatment of aggregated conduct in these matters.

body.heading: Conflict of Interest in Casting
body.text:
To preserve the integrity of the Guild’s regulatory oversight, a strict prohibition against self-certification is enforced. A member of the Guild, including those holding chairs or administrative offices, may not stamp, certify, or authorize their own transfiguration of inventory, research, or magical artifacts. This prohibition is intended to prevent the "Circular Validation" loop, wherein a mage uses their authority to grant themselves permission to perform a task that would otherwise require oversight. For example, an Innovator may not use their status to grant themselves permission to research a restricted school of magic without an independent review by the Clerk or a secondary chair.

This rule extends to the physical manipulation of the Guild’s assets. A mage who has performed a transfiguration on a batch of inventory cannot be the individual who certifies that the inventory meets the safety standards of the Accords. Such a certification must be performed by a third party who was not involved in the original casting. This is particularly vital in the handling of materials related to the Heartstone or other rift-adjacent substances, where the risk of magical instability is high. Any transfiguration performed on Guild property without a secondary stamp shall be considered an unauthorized act and may result in a Paradox Trial.

If a member finds themselves in a position where they must oversee a project involving their own previous work, they must recuse themselves from the stamping process. They may provide the initial research and casting, but the final certification must be delegated to a peer or a subordinate who is not bound by the same personal interest. Failure to comply with this prohibition constitutes a conflict of interest and shall be treated as a formal violation of the Accords. All such instances of self-certification are grounds for immediate review by the Sovereign. See § 1.9 for the validity of stamps.

body.heading: Delegation to Clerks
body.text:
The Clerk of the Accords Desk is empowered with the authority to act as a gatekeeper for the Guild’s administrative functions. Specifically, Clerks may refuse to provide a stamp of authorization for any application, permit, or research proposal if it is found to be incomplete, poorly formatted, or lacking the necessary signatures. This refusal of a stamp is a procedural right and does not constitute a legal challenge to the merit of the request. A mage who is denied a stamp due to incompleteness is not entitled to a duel or a formal hearing; they are simply required to rectify the documentation and resubmit it for review.

The Clerk’s role is to ensure that the records of the Accords remain clean and consistent. Therefore, a Clerk may refuse a stamp if the application contains contradictory information, lacks the required fee of mana or coin (where applicable), or fails to cite the relevant sections of the Accords. Because this is a matter of administrative completeness rather than a dispute over magical legality, the Clerk's decision is final regarding the *filing* of the document. The mage may still appeal the *content* of the law to the Chairs, but they cannot bypass the Clerk’s requirement for a complete file.

This delegation of power serves to protect the Chairs from being overwhelmed by trivial administrative errors. By allowing the Clerk to reject incomplete work without the need for a formal dispute, the Guild maintains its efficiency. However, the Clerk may not refuse a stamp based on personal animosity or ideological disagreement with the contents of the research. If a Clerks refuses a stamp and the mage believes the application is complete, the matter may be escalated to the Sovereign for a determination of "Administrative Sufficiency." See § 1.10 for reserved catchlines.

body.heading: Foreign Halls and Courtesy
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords recognize that mages may interact with other halls of learning, temples, and sovereign entities outside the Midlands jurisdiction. However, a stamp or seal of authorization from a foreign hall is considered evidence of a transaction, not a law of the Guild. If a mage presents a certificate of mastery or a license of research from a foreign entity, the Accords Desk shall record the document as "External Evidence" but shall not grant it the force of law within the Midlands until it has been formally recorded and reviewed by the Sovereign or the Quorum.

For example, a license granted by a foreign hall may allow a mage to perform certain tasks in that foreign territory, but it does not automatically exempt them from the restrictions of the Autumnwood Accords. A mage who relies on a foreign seal to bypass a Guild prohibition on forbidden schools shall be found in violation of the Accords. The Guild may, at its discretion, choose to recognize certain foreign seals as equivalent to Guild stamps, but this must be done through a formal treaty and recorded in the bound code. Until such a treaty is signed, the foreign seal is merely a courtesy and holds no weight in a Paradox Trial.

Furthermore, any mage who wishes to have a foreign seal recognized must submit a "Petition for Equivalence." This petition must be reviewed by both the Conservator and Innovator chairs to ensure that the foreign standards do not compromise the stability of the Midlands. The Guild maintains a policy of high caution regarding foreign magic, particularly that which originates from the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion. The Accords Desk shall maintain a ledger of all such foreign seals to ensure that no mage is attempting to use the same foreign license to bypass multiple Guild restrictions. See § 1.5 for the priority of local law.

body.heading: Emergency Sitting
body.text:
The Accords Desk is a body of deliberative law, and its sessions are typically scheduled to allow for proper consultation and record-keeping. It is a fundamental principle of the Accords that "unscheduled weather is not by itself an emergency sitting." The occurrence of a storm, a localized blizzard, a sudden mana-surge, or any other environmental anomaly does not automatically grant the Accords Desk the authority to convene an emergency session without a formal declaration of crisis by the Sovereign. The Guild rejects the notion that nature’s whims dictate the timing of legislative action.

An emergency sitting may only be convened if a specific, immediate threat to the Midlands or the Guild’s existence is identified and verified by the Sovereign. Such a threat must be of a magnitude that requires immediate legislative intervention—for instance, a rift opening in a populated center or an invasion by a recognized opponent like the Silver Flame. In such cases, a "Decree of Emergency" must be issued, which provides the legal basis for an unscheduled sitting. This decree must specify the duration of the emergency and the specific powers granted to the Quorum for the duration of the sitting.

The purpose of this rule is to prevent the "Crisis Exploitation" tactic, where mages might attempt to manufacture or exaggerate environmental hazards to force the Guild into making hasty, poorly-vetted decisions. By requiring a Sovereign declaration, the Accords ensure that emergency powers are used only when truly necessary. If a mage attempts to call for an emergency sitting based solely on poor weather or a minor magical mishap, the Clerk shall deny the request and the mage shall be directed to wait for the next scheduled session. All actions taken during an authorized emergency sitting remain subject to the standard rules of the Accords, unless specifically waived by the Sovereign's decree.

sections.title: Who May Speak for the Guild
sections.brief: Temporary mouths expire. A familiar's nod is not a speech unless the familiar is listed.

body.heading: Who May Speak for the Guild
body.text:
The authority to represent the Mages' Guild, and specifically the intent of the Autumnwood Accords, is strictly reserved for those individuals explicitly vested with the right of speech by Archmage Veyra or the presiding council. While many entities may operate under the Guild’s aegis, the legal weight of a declaration, a treaty, or a binding oath rests solely upon the vocalization of an authorized representative. Any individual whose status as a spokesperson is derived from a temporary mandate, a seasonal commission, or a localized administrative grant shall be subject to the expiration of such authority upon the conclusion of the designated timeframe. These temporary mouths expire exactly as the clock strikes the appointed hour; any declarations made beyond this window are legally void and do not bind the Guild to any external obligations or internal mandates.

Furthermore, the Guild acknowledges the pervasive presence of familiar spirits and bound entities within its halls, yet it is strictly codified that a familiar’s nod, gesture, or telepathic resonance does not constitute a formal speech of the Guild. Unless a familiar has been explicitly listed in the official registry of authorized conduits—a process requiring a petition to the Conservators and a review by the Innovators—their actions shall be viewed as mere instinct or subordinate reflex. No binding agreement may be entered into, nor any official decree issued, based upon the non-verbal cues of a familiar. The Guild shall not be held liable for any commitments perceived to have been made by a familiar, nor shall any familiar be granted the status of a legal persona for the purposes of these Accords.

To ensure the integrity of the Guild's diplomatic and internal standing, any entity claiming to speak for the Guild must present a valid Seal of Voice, issued in accordance with the protocols established in § 1.9. If a representative’s credentials are in dispute, the matter shall be referred to the Aegis Magi for verification of the individual's current standing. See § 1.4 for the scope of persons bound by these regulations. Any unauthorized speech that results in a breach of the Accords may result in the immediate revocation of the speaker's status and a referral to the Paradox Trial for the determination of appropriate sanctions.

body.heading: Quorum of the Desk
body.text:
The administrative functions of the Autumnwood Accords Desk, including the certification of research permits, the filing of restricted school licenses, and the mediation of jurisdictional disputes, require the presence of a formal quorum to ensure a balance of interests. The Guild recognizes the inherent friction between the traditionalist philosophies of the Conservators and the progressive ambitions of the Innovators. Therefore, to prevent the stagnation of the law or the reckless acceleration of magical practice, every binding decision made by the Desk must be ratified by a quorum consisting of at least one Conservator and one Innovator. This duality is intended to ensure that every action taken under the Accords is weighed against the requirements of stability and the permissions of restricted research.

In instances where the primary factions are unavailable, a secondary quorum may be established for the purpose of maintaining the flow of bureaucracy. Such a quorum may consist of two senior Clerks of the Accords Desk, provided they have served at least five years in continuous service. However, this secondary quorum is restricted to matters of clerical maintenance, record keeping, and the processing of standard petitions. They may not override the fundamental tenets of the Accords or authorize the exploration of forbidden schools. If a matter of significant magical magnitude or political sensitivity arises and the primary factions are absent, the Desk shall remain in a state of suspension until the required representatives can be convened.

Should a quorum fail to reach a consensus due to irreconcilable ideological differences, the matter shall be elevated to Archmage Veyra for mediation. The Archmage Sovereign retains the ultimate authority to break a deadlock, though she shall endeavor to find a path that satisfies the requirements of both the Conservators and the Innovators. If a quorum is reached but the deliberation becomes unproductive or circular, the Clerk of the Desk may declare a "Headache of Procedure," at which point the session is adjourned without prejudice. No binding action shall be taken under a "Headache" status, and the petition shall be returned to the petitioner for re-submission at a later date. See § 1.6 for relevant definitions.

body.heading: Records of Speech
body.text:
The integrity of the Mages' Guild relies upon the permanence of its records. It is a fundamental principle of the Autumnwood Accords that any spoken vote, decree, or formal declaration that is not subsequently filed with the Accords Desk is considered a mere rumor and carries no legal weight. While the oral tradition of the Guild is respected in social settings, the legal reality of the Guild is written. Mages who participate in council meetings, factional deliberations, or public hearings are strictly enjoined from bragging about the outcomes of such sessions until the official transcript has been reviewed, stamped, and entered into the permanent archive.

The act of filing is the transition from a private sentiment to a public law. Once a vote is recorded in the archives, it becomes a matter of record that can be cited in future disputes, used as a basis for the Paradox Trial, or served as a precedent for the Innovators’ research requests. Conversely, any agreement made in a tavern, a private study, or a field camp that is not filed with the Clerk of the Desk is unenforceable against the Guild. If a mage claims a right based on a "spoken agreement" with a faction leader, they must produce the corresponding filing; failure to do so shall result in the claim being dismissed as hearsay.

Clerks are tasked with the immediate transcription of all authorized speech. Any mage who fails to ensure their speech is filed may find themselves excluded from future deliberations until their records are brought into compliance. This rule serves to prevent the "shadow governance" of the Guild, where informal agreements might undermine the stability sought by the Conservators or the regulated progress sought by the Innovators. All filings must be submitted within three standard lunar cycles of the speech being uttered. See § 1.9 regarding the necessity of seals on all filed records.

body.heading: Conflict of Interest in Casting
body.text:
To maintain the impartiality of the Guild’s regulatory body, a strict prohibition exists regarding the intersection of personal magical practice and administrative authority. No member of the Guild, including Clerks, Archivists, and Aegis Magi, may use their official position to facilitate, authorize, or certify their own private magical endeavors. Specifically, a member may not stamp their own transfiguration of inventory, nor may they authorize the expansion of their own private laboratory or the acquisition of restricted materials for personal use. Such actions constitute a fundamental breach of the Accords and are viewed as a corruption of the Guild’s mandate.

This prohibition extends to all forms of "self-certification." If a mage seeks to have a new spell structure registered or a research project approved, they must submit the application to a different department or a different member of the Desk who has no personal or professional stake in the outcome. For example, an Innovator seeking permission for restricted research must have their application reviewed by a member of the Conservator faction or a neutral Clerk. Any attempt to bypass this process by seeking a "friendly" stamp from a colleague of the same faction shall be flagged for investigation by the Aegis Magi.

Violations of this policy are treated as grave offenses of integrity. If a member is found to have stamped their own transfiguration of inventory or any other personal magical act, the stamp shall be declared null and void, and the individual shall be subject to an immediate review for removal from the Desk. Furthermore, any inventory transfigured under such a fraudulent stamp is subject to immediate seizure or destruction. The Guild maintains that the authority to regulate magic must remain separate from the desire to wield it, ensuring that the Accords remain a tool of the public good rather than a shield for private ambition.

body.heading: Delegation to Clerks
body.text:
The Clerks of the Accords Desk are the primary conduits of the Guild’s administrative will. To ensure the efficiency of the Guild, the Archmage Sovereign has granted Clerks the authority to act as the first line of defense against procedural errors. Under this provision, Clerks may refuse a stamp for any petition, license, or record that is found to be incomplete, improperly formatted, or lacking the necessary signatures. This refusal is a procedural right and does not constitute a final judgment on the merit of the magic involved; it is a requirement of the record.

Crucially, a Clerk’s refusal to stamp a document for incompleteness does not grant the petitioner the right to a duel. While the Paradox Trial is the mechanism for resolving disputes over the interpretation of the Accords, it is not the appropriate venue for correcting a missing signature or a misspelled reagent list. If a petitioner attempts to demand a stamp through intimidation or by threatening a duel over a clerical error, the Clerk may immediately cease all interaction and refer the matter to the Aegis Magi for a breach of decorum. The Clerk’s role is to ensure the perfection of the archive, not to arbitrate the mysteries of the arcane.

However, the Clerk’s authority is not absolute. If a petitioner believes that a Clerk is unfairly withholding a stamp for a complete and correct document, the petitioner may appeal to the Quorum of the Desk. The Clerk must provide a written explanation for the refusal, citing the specific subsection of the Accords that was not met. This ensures that while the Clerks have the power to maintain order, they cannot use that power to arbitrarily obstruct the work of the Innovators or the interests of the Conservators. See § 100.3 for Quorum requirements.

body.heading: Foreign Halls and Courtesy
body.text:
The Mages' Guild recognizes that the Midlands is home to various entities with their own unique legal structures and magical traditions. However, the Autumnwood Accords are the sovereign law of this jurisdiction. When a mage presents a stamp or a decree from another hall—be it a regional collective, a private academy, or a foreign sovereign body—it shall be treated as evidence of an external fact, but it does not carry the force of law within the Autumnwood jurisdiction until it has been formally recorded and integrated into the Guild's archives.

For instance, a certificate of magical proficiency from a foreign hall may be used as evidence that a mage possesses certain skills, but it does not grant that mage the right to perform those skills in violation of the Accords. Similarly, a decree from a foreign sovereign body regarding the use of magic in their lands has no standing here. To move a foreign law into the sphere of Guild recognition, the petitioner must submit a "Petition for Integration." This process involves a review by the Conservators to ensure the foreign law does not conflict with the stability of the Midlands, and a review by the Innovators to ensure it does not stifle permissible research.

Courtesy is extended to all such halls, and the Guild shall not arbitrarily invalidate foreign credentials. However, the Guild shall not be bound by the debts, treaties, or penalties of another hall unless a formal "Accord of Reciprocity" has been signed by Archmage Veyra. Without such an Accord, the Guild remains a sovereign body, and the actions of foreign mages are subject to the same scrutiny as those of any other entity within the Midlands. This ensures that while the Guild is a participant in the wider world, it is not a vassal to the laws of others.

body.heading: Emergency Sitting
body.text:
The Guild recognizes that the unpredictable nature of magic can necessitate rapid responses to crises. However, to prevent the erosion of standard procedure, the Guild maintains a strict definition of what constitutes an emergency. Unscheduled weather, including but not limited to arcane storms, localized blizzards, or atmospheric mana fluctuations, does not by itself constitute an emergency sitting of the Accords Desk. Such events are considered environmental hazards to be managed by the Aegis Magi or through standard emergency protocols, rather than grounds for a suspension of the Guild’s deliberative processes.

An emergency sitting may only be convened when there is a direct and immediate threat to the integrity of the Autumnwood Accords, the safety of the Midlands, or the existence of the Guild itself. This includes, but is not limited to, a rift in the fabric of reality, a large-scale breach of the forbidden schools, or an imminent invasion by a recognized hostile force such as the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion. To convene an emergency sitting, a petition must be signed by at least three members of the Quorum and presented to Archmage Veyra for immediate ratification.

Once an emergency sitting is ratified, the usual requirements for quorum and deliberation may be expedited, but the actions taken during such a sitting remain subject to post-facto review by the Conservators. This prevents the use of "emergency" status as a pretext for the Innovators to bypass research restrictions or for the Conservators to enact reactionary laws without proper debate. All decisions made during an emergency sitting must be recorded with the same rigor as standard sessions, and a summary of the emergency must be filed within one lunar cycle of the session’s conclusion. See § 1.5 for the relation to other laws.

sections.title: Quorum of the Desk
sections.brief: One Conservator and one Innovator, or a clerk and a headache.

body.heading: Quorum of the Desk
body.text:
The administrative functions of the Accords Desk, as recognized under the foundational agreements of the Autumnwood Accords, shall only be deemed valid and binding when conducted by a quorum of sufficient authority. To ensure the delicate equilibrium between the traditionalist mandates of the Conservators and the progressive inquiries of the Innovators, the primary quorum for the issuance of official stamps, the validation of research permits, and the adjudication of minor grievances shall consist of at least one representative from the Conservator faction and one representative from the Innovator faction. This dual-representation requirement is designed to prevent the unilateral monopolization of magical oversight by either side of the ideological divide. By requiring the presence of both a Conservator and an Innovator, the Accords ensure that every administrative action is scrutinized for both its potential for stability and its feasibility of advancement.

In instances where the primary quorum cannot be met due to travel, illness, or the sequestering of high-ranking mages, a secondary quorum may be established. Under the provisions of § 1.2, the Accords Desk may authorize a quorum consisting of a designated Guild Clerk and an individual of sufficient mental fortitude to endure the administrative burden, colloquially referred to in internal memoranda as a "headache." However, the Desk shall endeavor to maintain the primary quorum for all matters involving the Paradox Trial or the classification of Restricted Research. Any action taken by a Clerk in the absence of a proper quorum shall be considered "provisional" and shall require retroactive ratification by the Archmage Sovereign or a formal session of the full Hall.

Furthermore, the presence of an Aegis Mage at the Desk does not constitute a quorum. The Aegis Magi are the enforcement arm of the dominant faction and are prohibited from casting votes on the interpretation of the Accords. Their role is strictly limited to the physical security of the Hall and the execution of sanctioned seals. Should a dispute arise regarding the composition of a quorum, the Archmage Veyra shall serve as the ultimate arbiter. If the Archmage is unavailable, the Desk shall remain in recess until a valid quorum is assembled. No stamp issued during a period of insufficient quorum shall be recognized as tender or valid under the Accords, and any mage attempting to utilize such a stamp shall be subject to a formal inquiry. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Records of Speech
body.text:
All spoken votes, declarations, and verbal adjudications rendered within the Hall of Autumn Wood that are not formally entered into the official ledger shall be deemed mere rumors and possess no legal weight under the Autumnwood Accords. The sanctity of the written record is the cornerstone of the Guild’s stability; therefore, any mage who wishes to see a policy enacted, a fine levied, or a research permit granted must ensure that the proceedings are transcribed and filed before any public proclamation or bragging is permitted. A mage who brags of a victory or a granted privilege before the Clerk has finalized the entry in the Codex shall be liable for a "Littering of the Air" fine, as such behavior undermines the solemnity of the Guild’s legal processes.

The Clerk of the Accords Desk is the sole custodian of the official record. Upon the conclusion of any session, the presiding mages shall present their verbal findings to the Clerk for immediate transcription. Once a vote is filed, it becomes a permanent part of the Accords' history and may be cited in future disputes. Conversely, any statement made by a member of the Guild in a tavern, a marketplace, or a private residence that is not subsequently filed with the Desk is considered "extemporaneous speech" and carries no authority. This rule is specifically intended to prevent the spread of misinformation and to ensure that the Innovators and Conservators remain bound to their documented agreements rather than the shifting winds of public opinion.

Mages who habitually speak of "agreed-upon" matters without verifying the records shall be cautioned. In cases where a mage claims a right based on a verbal agreement made by a high-ranking official, such as Archmage Theron or Janna Brightspark, the burden of proof lies with the claimant to produce a filed record. If no such record exists, the agreement shall be treated as non-binding. This practice serves to insulate the Guild from the "shadow-agreements" that often plague high-level magical politics. To ensure compliance, the Desk shall maintain a "Rumor Log" to track common misconceptions, which may be used as evidence of a mage's negligence in following proper filing procedures. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Conflict of Interest in Casting
body.text:
To preserve the integrity of the Guild's regulatory framework, a strict prohibition is placed upon the self-validation of magical alterations. A member of the Guild, regardless of their rank or factional affiliation, may not apply an official stamp to their own transfiguration of inventory, the expansion of personal laboratories, or the modification of any enchanted item they personally commissioned. This prohibition extends to any "self-service" magical adjustments that would otherwise require the oversight of the Accords Desk. The purpose of this rule is to prevent the accumulation of unregulated magical power and to ensure that the transmutation of materials remains consistent with the safety standards established by the Conservators and the research guidelines of the Innovators.

Any mage who attempts to bypass the Desk by using their own authority to validate their works shall be flagged for a Conflict of Interest review. This is particularly relevant for high-level Innovators who may possess the raw power to alter significant quantities of inventory without external assistance. While such mages may possess the capability, they lack the legal standing to provide the necessary certification for the Guild’s public records. If an Innovator seeks to expand their workshop, they must petition a different member of the Desk who has no vested interest in the specific project. The presiding Clerk shall be responsible for identifying such conflicts and may void any stamp that appears to be issued by a party with a personal stake in the outcome.

Furthermore, this rule applies to the "Goodstyle Artisans" and any affiliated contractors. While the Guild maintains a cooperative relationship with the Artisans, no Artisan may use a Guild stamp to certify their own products without a neutral third-party inspection. Any inventory found to have been "self-stamped" or "self-certified" by a Guild member shall be subject to immediate seizure and may be confiscated as evidence of a breach of the Accords. Violations of this rule may result in a referral to the Paradox Trial for the purpose of determining whether the mage intended to circumvent the safety protocols of the Hall. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Delegation to Clerks
body.text:
The Clerks of the Accords Desk are granted specific administrative powers to ensure the smooth operation of the Hall’s bureaucratic functions. Among these powers is the right of refusal; a Clerk may refuse to apply a stamp or issue a certificate for any petition found to be incomplete, improperly formatted, or lacking the required signatures. This refusal is an administrative action, not a judicial one, and therefore does not constitute a legal finding of guilt or a denial of rights. A Clerk's refusal based on incompleteness is a matter of procedure; if a mage wishes to challenge the specific requirements of the Clerk, they must first complete the paperwork as requested and then appeal to the Archmage Sovereign for a ruling on the necessity of those requirements.

Crucially, the Clerk’s refusal to stamp an incomplete document does not, in itself, authorize a duel. The Guild prohibits the use of the Paradox Trial or any form of arcane duel to settle matters of clerical procedure. A mage who attempts to initiate a duel because a Clerk has demanded additional documentation shall be cited for "Hostile Procedural Escalation." The Clerk is empowered to hold a petition in a state of "Pending Review" indefinitely until the petitioner provides the missing data or signatures. This ensures that the Desk remains a place of orderly administration rather than a theater for magical combat.

The Clerk shall also be responsible for ensuring that all petitions meet the standards of both the Conservators and the Innovators. If a petition is technically complete but fails to meet the safety standards of the Conservators, or the research potential of the Innovators, the Clerk may return it with a "Notice of Insufficiency." The petitioner may then revise the document to address the specific concerns raised. By granting Clerks the power to refuse stamps without the risk of immediate combat, the Accords allow for a more nuanced and thorough vetting of magical activities. This bureaucratic buffer is essential for protecting the Hall from the volatile impulses of the radical factions. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Foreign Halls and Courtesy
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords recognize that mages may occasionally interact with external magical entities and governing bodies. However, a stamp, seal, or certificate issued by a foreign hall is considered evidence of a transaction or a statement of fact, but it does not carry the force of law within the Midlands or under the jurisdiction of the Archmage Sovereign. For a foreign document to be recognized as a binding legal instrument within the Guild, it must be formally recorded and transcribed into the Accords' ledger by the Desk. Until such recording occurs, the document is treated as a "Foreign Courtesy," and the Guild assumes no responsibility for the actions, promises, or magical outputs associated with it.

This rule is particularly important when dealing with the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion, whose legal codes (such as the Iron Mandate) are fundamentally at odds with the Accords. A mage who presents a permit from an Iron Legion outpost as a license to operate within the Autumnwood must be informed that such a permit holds no weight here. The Guild will not honor the "legal" requirements of hostile powers, and any mage who attempts to use foreign law to circumvent the Accords shall be subject to immediate expulsion. The Desk shall maintain a "Foreign Registry" to track which external seals have been recorded, providing a clear distinction between recognized international cooperation and unauthorized foreign interference.

Furthermore, the Guild shall extend "Courtesy of Recognition" to the Goodstyle Artisans, whose marks of quality are respected but are not legally equivalent to a Guild stamp. If an Artisan provides a certificate of craftsmanship, the Clerk may record it as a secondary verification, but it cannot replace the primary oversight of the Accords. Mages are cautioned against relying on the "good faith" of foreign mages; the only security lies in the formal recording of the Accord. Any mage who acts upon a foreign seal that has not been recorded by the Desk does so at their own peril, and the Guild shall not be held liable for any resulting rifts, paradoxes, or diplomatic incidents. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Emergency Sitting
body.text:
The Accords Desk is a body of deliberate and measured action. Therefore, the occurrence of unscheduled weather—including but not limited to blizzards, localized storms, or atmospheric distortions—does not, by itself, constitute an "Emergency Sitting." The Guild maintains that true emergencies are defined by threats to the structural integrity of the Accords, the safety of the Hall, or the presence of a breach in the veil, rather than mere environmental inconveniences. A weather event only triggers an Emergency Sitting if it is accompanied by a direct threat to the sovereign's mandate or the physical security of the Autumn Wood.

Mages who attempt to declare an Emergency Sitting simply to bypass the standard quorum requirements or to fast-track a controversial research permit shall be sanctioned for "Procedural Manipulation." The Archmage Veyra alone holds the authority to declare a state of emergency that necessitates an unscheduled sitting. During a legitimate emergency, the quorum requirements may be suspended, and the Aegis Magi may be granted temporary authority to enact protective measures. However, the burden of proof for such a declaration is high; the petitioner must demonstrate that the situation poses an immediate and existential risk to the Guild's stability or the surrounding Midlands.

Standard procedures for the filing of records, the verification of stamps, and the adjudication of disputes shall remain in effect during all non-emergency weather events. The Clerk of the Desk is instructed to maintain the regular schedule of operations regardless of the conditions outside the Hall, provided the Hall remains structurally sound. This ensures that the bureaucracy of the Accords remains a constant and reliable force, un swayed by the temporary whims of nature. Any mage who seeks to use a storm as a pretext for clandestine activity will find their petitions ignored until the weather clears and the proper quorum is met. See § 1.6.

sections.title: Records of Speech
sections.brief: Spoken votes that are not filed are rumors. File before bragging.

body.heading: Records of Speech
body.text:
§ 100.4 Records of Speech

All deliberations, verbal votes, and oral testimonies produced within the halls of the Autumnwood Accords are considered ephemeral and non-binding in their primary state. It is the express policy of the Accords Desk that any spoken vote that is not formally filed within the central registry shall be categorized as mere rumor and shall carry no weight in the adjudication of magical rights, factional standing, or the distribution of sanctioned reagents. The transition from "rumor" to "record" is achieved only upon the physical or magical filing of a transcribed scroll or a witnessed verbal deposition into the archive. Mages who engage in the public dissemination of internal votes prior to such filing commit a breach of administrative decorum.

The principle of "File Before Bragging" serves as both a procedural requirement and a punitive deterrent against the premature inflation of political capital. A member who claims a victory in a council vote, a decree of the Conservators, or a research grant from the Innovators without having secured a filed record shall be subject to a formal reprimand. The Accords Desk does not recognize the "he-said, she-said" of the Midlands as a basis for legal action. If a mage seeks to use a past vote to justify a current requisition of restricted materials, they must produce the corresponding filing. Failure to do so renders the claim null, and the member may be cited for attempting to codify rumor as law.

Furthermore, the propagation of unfiled votes in taverns, public squares, or private residences is strictly discouraged to prevent the destabilization of the Guild’s internal harmony. While the Archivists of the Autumnwood Accords do not police every whisper in the Midlands, they shall refuse to acknowledge any petition that cites an unfiled oral agreement. This ensures that the administrative integrity of the Guild remains insulated from the fickle nature of spoken word. See § 100.3 for requirements regarding the validity of the Desk’s administrative functions. Any record submitted after the fact must be accompanied by a notarized seal of the presiding officer to be accepted into the primary ledger.

body.heading: Conflict of Interest in Casting
body.text:
§ 100.5 Conflict of Interest in Casting

To preserve the impartiality of the Guild’s regulatory oversight, a member of the Mages' Guild, regardless of their factional affiliation—be they Conservator, Innovator, or Aegis Mage—is strictly prohibited from certifying or stamping their own magical transfigurations of inventory. This prohibition is designed to prevent the illicit conversion of mundane materials into restricted reagents or the clandestine alteration of Guild-owned assets for personal gain. Any mage who performs a transfiguration on a bulk item of inventory must submit said item to a neutral third party for inspection and subsequent stamping by a clerk of the Accords Desk who holds no direct interest in the transaction.

This rule applies with equal force to the Innovators’ research materials and the Conservators’ restricted stores. A researcher may not utilize their own signature to validate the safety of a high-potency reagent they have synthesized, nor may a Conservator use their authority to stamp a transfigured artifact that they personally crafted. Such actions constitute a fundamental breach of the Accords, as they circumvent the necessary oversight intended to maintain the stability of the Midlands’ magical environment. Violations of this provision shall be viewed as an attempt to bypass the safety protocols established to prevent magical leakage or unauthorized research.

Where a conflict of interest is identified, the offending mage shall be required to surrender the item in question for a mandatory audit by the Aegis Magi. If it is determined that the transfiguration was performed with the intent to deceive the Guild or to circumvent the Iron Mandate's external pressures, the individual may be referred for a Paradox Trial. See § 1.6 for definitions of restricted reagents and inventory classifications. All stamps of approval must be applied by a clerk whose name does not appear on the manifest of the originating laboratory or the private estate of the requesting mage.

body.heading: Delegation to Clerks
body.text:
§ 100.6 Delegation to Clerks

The administrative clerks of the Accords Desk are granted the delegated authority to act as the first line of defense against procedural irregularities. As such, a clerk may refuse to apply a stamp of approval to any scroll, petition, or manifest deemed incomplete, insufficient, or technically deficient without the necessity of initiating a formal duel. This administrative prerogative is intended to streamline the flow of documentation and ensure that only legally sound requests reach the higher authorities of the Archmage Sovereign or the faction leaders. A clerk’s refusal is a matter of bureaucratic fact, not a personal affront or a challenge to the mage’s power.

While the Guild recognizes the inherent power of its members, the Accords Desk is a space of civil administration where the "might makes right" philosophy of the Aegis Magi is tempered by the "rule of law" of the Autumnwood Accords. A mage may not demand a stamp through the threat of arcane force; any attempt to coerce a clerk through intimidation or magical pressure shall be reported as a violation of the Guild’s internal peace. The clerk shall provide a written notice of deficiency, detailing the specific requirements—such as missing seals, incorrect dates, or lack of required signatures—that must be addressed before the stamp may be granted.

This delegation of power ensures that the Archmage Veyra and the faction leaders are not burdened with the minutiae of clerical errors. By allowing clerks to act as gatekeepers, the Guild maintains a high standard of documentation. If a mage disputes a clerk's refusal, they may appeal to the presiding officer of the Desk, but they may not bypass the clerk to seek a stamp from a peer. See § 100.3 for the conditions under which these administrative functions are deemed binding. Clerks are instructed to remain neutral and objective, adhering strictly to the criteria laid out in the Codex.

body.heading: Foreign Halls and Courtesy
body.text:
§ 100.7 Foreign Halls and Courtesy

The Autumnwood Accords recognize the existence of other magical bodies and regional authorities, yet it remains the firm stance of the Guild that a stamp or seal issued by a foreign hall is considered evidence of an action, not a source of law. While the Guild may acknowledge the legitimacy of a foreign mage’s credentials for the purpose of transit or basic commerce, no foreign decree shall have binding authority within the Midlands unless it is formally recorded and ratified by the Accords Desk. This principle prevents the encroachment of external legal systems—such as the Iron Mandate or the Edicts of the Flame—upon the sovereign magical jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords.

When a mage presents a document bearing the seal of a foreign entity, the clerk shall record the entry as a "Foreign Certification." This certification may be used to verify the identity of a traveler or the origin of a shipment, but it does not grant the holder any rights, privileges, or exemptions from the laws of the Accords. For instance, a permit of passage from the Regal Empire does not exempt a mage from the restrictions on necromancy or the requirements for a Paradox Trial. The Guild maintains a policy of "cordial distance," acknowledging the existence of neighbors without surrendering the autonomy of its own legal framework.

Should a mage seek to incorporate a foreign agreement into Guild law, they must petition the Archmage Sovereign for a formal recording. Once recorded, the agreement may be granted limited standing within specific circumstances, but it shall always remain subordinate to the primary Accords. Mages are cautioned against relying on foreign stamps to circumvent local regulations, as the Guild will not recognize "reciprocal" permissions that violate the stability of the Midlands. See § 1.5 for the relation to other laws and the status of external mandates. All foreign seals are to be filed in the "External Correspondence" ledger for archival purposes only.

body.heading: Emergency Sitting
body.text:
§ 100.8 Emergency Sitting

The administrative functions of the Accords Desk are designed to operate on a predictable schedule to ensure the orderly governance of the Midlands. It is hereby codified that unscheduled weather events—including but not limited to localized thunderstorms, blizzards, or magical fog—do not, by themselves, constitute a legal basis for an emergency sitting of the Council or the Desk. While the Guild acknowledges the logistical difficulties posed by the volatile climate of the Autumnwood, the disruption of routine proceedings for mere weather inconveniences is deemed an inefficient use of the Guild’s resources and a violation of standard operating procedure.

An emergency sitting may only be convened upon the presentation of a "Threat to the Accords" notice, which must detail a specific, immediate danger to the magical stability of the region, the safety of the Guild members, or the integrity of the Heartstone. Examples of such threats include a confirmed rift opening, a large-scale breach of the Quiet List, or a direct assault by the Iron Legion or the Silver Flame. Weather-related delays shall be handled through standard rescheduling protocols, and no mage shall be penalized for missing a session due to impassable roads, provided they filed a notice of absence in a timely manner.

The purpose of this regulation is to prevent the factional leaders—specifically the Innovators and the Conservators—from using minor environmental hazards as a pretext to stall legislation or avoid inconvenient votes. By requiring a specific threat to be identified, the Accords ensure that the Desk remains focused on the preservation of the Midlands. If a mage claims that a storm has rendered a meeting impossible, the Desk shall require proof of a "Magical Hazard" as defined in the restricted schools section of the Accords. See § 100.3 for the quorum requirements that must be met during any valid sitting, whether scheduled or emergency.

sections.title: Conflict of Interest in Casting
sections.brief: A member may not stamp their own transfiguration of inventory.

body.heading: Conflict of Interest in Casting
body.text:
A member may not stamp their own transfiguration of inventory. Any mage, whether of the Conservator or Innovator faction, is strictly prohibited from issuing, validating, or providing the official Guild Seal of Authenticity for any magical transmutation of personal or corporate inventory in which they hold a primary interest. This prohibition serves to prevent the illicit expansion of magical assets and ensures that the integrity of the Autumnwood Accords is not compromised by self-serving arcane manipulation. When a mage performs a transfiguration—be it the expansion of storage dimensions, the alteration of raw materials into finished goods, or the transmutation of currency—the resulting object must be subjected to an independent review by a neutral third party. This third party shall be a clerk or a licensed auditor of the Accords Desk who bears no kinship, financial ties, or magical resonance with the caster.

The purpose of this regulation is to maintain the stability of the local market and the metaphysical equilibrium of the Midlands. If a mage attempts to bypass this restriction by employing a proxy, such as a familiar or a low-level apprentice, to perform the stamping on their behalf, the act shall be deemed a direct violation of the Accords. See § 100.2 for the limitations on familiar speech and representation. Any inventory found to have been stamped by the primary caster shall be subject to immediate seizure by the Aegis Magi. Furthermore, any goods produced under such circumstances are declared "Arcane Nullities" and may not be traded with Goodstyle Artisans or any other recognized merchant body.

In instances where a large-scale industrial transfiguration is required for the public good, such as the construction of communal infrastructure in the Autumn Wood, the mage in question must petition for a Special Waiver from Archmage Veyra. This waiver shall require a deposit of mana-crystals and a sworn oath of non-profit intent. Without such a waiver, all self-stamped inventory is considered contraband. This provision stands in direct opposition to the Iron Mandate of the Regal Empire, which does not recognize the Guild's authority over private property; however, within the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords, the Guild’s seal remains the sole arbiter of magical legitimacy. Violations of this clause may result in a referral to the Paradox Trial for the assessment of magical sealing or pocket-prisonment.

body.heading: Delegation to Clerks
body.text:
Clerks may refuse a stamp for incompleteness without a duel. The administrative staff of the Accords Desk, acting under the authority of the Archmage Sovereign, are granted the discretionary power to withhold the Guild Seal from any application, scroll, or artifact that fails to meet the rigorous standards of completeness. A "complete" filing is defined as one that contains all requisite signatures, clearly delineated school-of-magic designations, and a full inventory of reagents used in the casting process. Should a clerk find a filing to be deficient, they are empowered to return the document to the petitioner for correction. This refusal is an administrative action and does not constitute a legal challenge to the mage’s competency or the validity of their research.

Under no circumstances shall a clerk be compelled to engage in a Paradox Trial or any form of arcane duel simply because a filing was rejected. The role of the clerk is one of verification, not adjudication. If a mage feels that a clerk is acting with undue bias or malice, they are encouraged to file a formal grievance with the Desk Quorum as per § 100.3. However, the clerk's right to refuse a stamp due to missing information, illegible script, or lack of proper factional headers is absolute. This ensures that the flow of magic through the Autumnwood Accords remains orderly and that the Aegis Magi are not burdened with processing incomplete or hazardous data.

Furthermore, clerks are instructed to remain impartial in their assessment of the content. While the Conservators may favor traditionalist structures and the Innovators may push for more expansive permissions, the clerk’s duty is to the letter of the law. If a filing is incomplete, it is incomplete, regardless of the prestige of the mage submitting it.
