Pursuant to the overarching mandates established in § 300.1 Schedules of Arts, the practice of Necromancy is hereby designated as a Class-A Forbidden Art. Any practitioner found engaging in the animation of necrotic tissue, the communion with the deceased for the purpose of servitude, or the manipulation of the veil between life and death without express, written authorization from the Archmage Sovereign shall be subject to immediate summary detention. The Accords recognize that while the manipulation of life essences presents a fundamental risk to the stability of the Midlands, the preservation of the natural order remains the primary directive of the Conservators. Consequently, the use of blood magic, soul-binding, and any methodology that facilitates the permanent extraction of vital essence from a sentient being is strictly prohibited under all circumstances, regardless of the stated intent of the caster.

Notwithstanding the general prohibition, the Innovators may submit formal petitions for "Restricted Research" permits concerning the study of necrotic energies. Such permits shall be scrutinized by the Accords Desk to ensure that any experimental application does not breach the fundamental safety threshold of the Autumnwood Accords. However, the mere possession of a permit for research purposes does not grant the holder the right to perform public demonstrations or large-scale applications of the art. All research conducted under such a permit must be contained within a sanctioned laboratory and reported to the Aegis Magi for periodic inspection. Failure to adhere to the containment protocols specified in the permit shall result in the immediate revocation of the permit and a referral to the Paradox Trial for the maximum penalty of magic sealing.

It is further stipulated that any mage found in possession of unauthorized necromantic reagents, including but not limited to bone-dust of the marked, grave-soil from consecrated sites, or fluids of the deceased, shall be deemed in violation of the Accords. The acquisition of such materials is considered prima facie evidence of intent to engage in Unsanctioned Arts. See § 1.6 for definitions of prohibited reagents. Any individual who knowingly assists in the smuggling or distribution of these materials shall be prosecuted as an accomplice to a high-tier felony. The Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding the unauthorized use of the "Quiet List" for the purpose of concealing necromantic activities; any attempt to mask a forbidden art under a lesser classification shall be met with the full weight of the Accord's penal statutes.

body.heading: Quiet List Procedure
body.text:
The Quiet List serves as a confidential repository of magical methodologies, artifacts, and phenomena that, while not strictly forbidden by the primary Schedules, possess a level of volatility or inherent danger that necessitates restricted awareness. Unlike the public catalogues of sanctioned arts, the Quiet List is not a public document and may not be recited, transcribed, or disseminated in any public forum, including but not limited to taverns, marketplaces, or common halls. The procedure for listing an art upon the Quiet List is initiated by a petition from a member of the Conservator or Innovator factions, supported by a comprehensive risk assessment. Once the Archmage Sovereign approves the petition, the art is entered into the private registry. The purpose of this procedure is to ensure that high-risk magics remain under the purview of the Guild's oversight without causing unnecessary public alarm or providing a roadmap for illicit exploitation by outside entities such as the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion.

A mage who becomes aware of a Quiet List entry through the course of their duties or research is bound by a permanent oath of non-disclosure. Any breach of this confidentiality, whether intentional or through negligence, shall be considered a breach of the Accords and may lead to the revocation of the caster's Guild standing. The Accords Desk shall maintain the physical and metaphysical security of the Quiet List, ensuring that it remains inaccessible to those without the requisite clearance levels. No mage, regardless of rank, may demand access to the Quiet List for the purpose of personal study unless they can demonstrate that such study is essential to the defense of the Midlands or the preservation of the Accords.

Furthermore, the naming of a Quiet List entry in a public setting is strictly prohibited. If a mage is questioned regarding an art that is known to be on the Quiet List, they must provide a generalized description that does not reveal the specific classification or the unique properties of the art. The Aegis Magi are authorized to monitor for such breaches and may impose fines or temporary suspensions on those who fail to uphold the secrecy of the List. The Quiet List is a tool of preservation, not a secret of shame; it is the mechanism by which the Guild manages the most delicate threads of reality. By ensuring that these arts are not publicized, the Guild prevents the destabilization of the common populace and maintains the delicate equilibrium of the Autumnwood Accords. See § 1.6 for further clarification on confidentiality.

body.heading: Reclassification
body.text:
The classification of magical arts within the Autumnwood Accords is subject to periodic review by the Accords Desk to ensure that the Schedules of Arts remain relevant to the evolving nature of magical discovery. However, the process of reclassification is governed by strict procedural hurdles to prevent the politicization of magical safety. Specifically, moving an art from a restricted category, such as Schedule B (Restricted Research), to a more permissive category, such as Schedule A (Sanctioned Arts), is not a matter of simple majority vote or partisan preference. Such a transition requires a "Consensus of Stability," necessitating approval from both the Conservator and Innovator chairs, as well as a formal endorsement from the Archmage Sovereign. The Guild recognizes that the Innovators may frequently advocate for the expansion of sanctioned arts, while the Conservators seek to maintain the current boundaries; therefore, the Desk shall not permit a reclassification to occur solely based on the desires of one faction.

Any petition for reclassification must be accompanied by a "Stability Impact Report," detailing the history of the art's use, any recorded incidents of magical fallout, and a proposed framework for its safe integration into the general magical landscape. If a proposed reclassification is deemed by the Accords Desk to pose a significant risk to the Midlands or to violate the core tenets of the Autumnwood Accords, it shall be denied regardless of the factional support. The Desk shall maintain a record of all such petitions, and any mage found attempting to bypass the formal reclassification process by practicing a Schedule B art as if it were Schedule A shall be subject to the Paradox Trial. This rule ensures that the evolution of magic remains a deliberate, measured process rather than a reactive one.

Furthermore, the reclassification of an art does not retroactively change the legal status of previous violations. Any mage who engaged in the unauthorized practice of an art before its formal reclassification remains liable for the infractions committed during the period of its restricted status. The Accords Desk reserves the right to freeze the status of any art currently under review if new evidence of catastrophic risk emerges. This procedural safeguard is designed to prevent the rapid "normalization" of dangerous magics that could lead to systemic collapse. The integrity of the Schedules of Arts is the foundation of the Guild's authority, and its preservation is paramount. See § 300.1 for the primary categorizations.

body.heading: Research Copies of Quiet Items
body.text:
The Guild acknowledges the necessity of research and the creation of pedagogical materials for the advancement of the arcane sciences. However, the status of an item or art as a "Quiet" entity under the Accords implies a permanent restriction on its public profile. It is a fundamental principle of the Accords that any copy, derivative, or transcription of a Quiet List item remains a Quiet item. If a mage is granted permission to create a research copy of a Quiet art—such as a transcribed scroll, a physical model, or a localized magical echo—that copy must be treated with the same level of security and confidentiality as the original. The act of creating a copy does not "dilute" the restricted nature of the art, nor does it authorize the caster to speak of the copy’s contents in public spaces. The restriction is tied to the nature of the magic itself, not merely the specific instance of the medium.

While the physical possession of a research copy is permissible for authorized scholars, the dissemination of information regarding that copy is strictly controlled. A scholar may discuss the *methodology* of their research or the *general goals* of their study, provided such discussion does not reveal the specific mechanics, properties, or classifications of the Quiet item. For example, a mage may state they are "studying a volatile atmospheric phenomenon," but they may not describe the specific resonance frequencies or the unique identifiers that place it on the Quiet List. Any mage who shares the specific details of a Quiet research copy with a non-cleared individual, including those who are not members of the Guild, shall be subject to immediate disciplinary action. This includes the seizure of the research materials and a potential referral to the Aegis Magi for a security audit.

It is important to distinguish between the *existence* of a copy and the *revelation* of its contents. A mage may own a library of Quiet research copies, but they must be kept in a manner consistent with the privacy requirements of the Accords. These materials must be stored in secure locations, and access must be logged. The Accords Desk does not permit the creation of "public-facing" summaries of Quiet items; any attempt to create a "sanitized" version of a Quiet art for public consumption without the express permission of the Archmage Sovereign is a violation of the confidentiality protocols. The goal of these regulations is to facilitate the pursuit of knowledge while ensuring that the most dangerous and sensitive aspects of the arcane remain shielded from those who lack the training or the temperament to handle them. See § 1.6 for related definitions.

sections.title: Quiet List Procedure
sections.brief: How an art is listed without a public catalogue.

body.heading: Quiet List Procedure
body.text:
The maintenance of the Quiet List is a matter of highest security and sovereign discretion, overseen by the Archmage Sovereign and the High Council of the Conservators. Pursuant to the mandates of the Autumnwood Accords, certain schools of magic or specific arcane methodologies are deemed so volatile, spiritually corrosive, or socially destabilizing that their existence must be shielded from the general populace. The Quiet List is not a public catalogue, nor is it a registry available for consultation by mere citizens, wandering mages, or the uninitiated. It serves as a subterranean repository of forbidden knowledge, a ledger of the "Unsanctioned Arts" that the Guild recognizes as existing but refuses to acknowledge in the public sphere. The primary objective of this procedure is the containment of metaphysical hazards that, if publicized, would invite widespread hysteria or provide a blueprint for catastrophic misuse by the Regal Empire, the Iron Legion, or the Cosmic Jesters.

An art is listed upon the Quiet List through a process of secret adjudication. When a new magical phenomenon is discovered by the Innovators or identified as a recurring threat by the Conservators, it is brought before the High Council in a closed session. If the Council determines that the art poses a risk to the structural integrity of the Midlands or violates the fundamental tenets of Mana Reverence, it shall be struck from the public Schedules of Arts. From that moment forward, the art is officially "Quiet." No public advertisement of the art, no pedagogical instruction in public academies, and no commercial sale of components related specifically to that art may occur. Any mage found to be teaching, practicing, or publicly disseminating the mechanics of a Quiet Item shall be subject to immediate investigation by the Aegis Magi.

The procedure for listing does not involve the destruction of the knowledge, but rather its sequestration. The Guild maintains a clandestine library where the methodology of these arts is archived for study by authorized personnel only. This is a distinction between "Forbidden" and "Quiet." While some arts are forbidden entirely under the Iron Mandate of external powers, the Quiet List is a Guild-specific mechanism of internal regulation. To ensure the integrity of this procedure, any clerk or official who becomes aware of a Quiet Item is bound by a perpetual oath of silence. Recitation of a Quiet Item’s name or properties in a tavern, marketplace, or any other public forum is a breach of the Accords and shall be treated as a high-level offense, potentially resulting in a Paradox Trial. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Reclassification
body.text:
The administrative movement of magical arts between categories—specifically from the restricted tiers of the Innovators to the sanctioned tiers of the Conservators—is a formal process of Reclassification. This Codex clarifies that the act of Reclassification is a bureaucratic transition of status and does not constitute a "party" to any legal agreement or a change in the underlying nature of the magic itself. When an art is moved from Category B (Restricted Research) to Category A (Sanctioned Use), the Guild is acknowledging that the risks associated with the art have been sufficiently mitigated or that the social utility of the art outweighs the perceived danger. However, the transition of a category is a unilateral administrative act by the Archmage Sovereign; it does not create a bilateral contract between the user and the Guild.

Mages seeking to petition for the Reclassification of a specific art must provide a comprehensive dossier to the Conservators, demonstrating that the art can be practiced with a high degree of stability and without violating the core tenets of the Autumnwood Accords. If the petition is granted, the art is removed from the restricted schedules and may be taught in standard academies. This change in status does not grant the user immunity from the general regulations governing magical conduct. The mere fact that an art is no longer "Quiet" or "Restricted" does not mean it is unregulated; it simply means it is no longer subject to the specific secrecy protocols outlined in § 300.3.

Furthermore, any legal disputes arising from the use of an art during the period of its Reclassification shall be judged based on the status of the art at the time of the casting. If a mage utilizes an art that is currently undergoing a transition from restricted to sanctioned, they remain bound by the restrictive permissions of the Innovators until the final seal of Reclassification is affixed by the Archmage Sovereign. The movement of an art is not a negotiation; it is a decree. Therefore, any attempt by a mage or a faction to claim that the "process" of Reclassification creates a temporary state of legality is rejected. The law is either in effect, or it is not. See § 1.6.

body.heading: Research Copies of Quiet Items
body.text:
The Guild acknowledges the necessity of scholarly pursuit and the preservation of arcane history. Consequently, the creation of research copies of Quiet Items is permitted under strict supervision, provided such copies are designated as "Static Artifacts" for the purpose of study. It is a fundamental principle of this Codex that the creation of a copy does not strip the underlying art of its "Quiet" status. If an art is listed on the Quiet List, any physical manifestation, scroll, or construct derived from that art remains subject to the secrecy protocols of § 300.3. The existence of a research copy does not authorize the user to discuss the mechanics, properties, or existence of the art in public spaces.

The distinction between the *object* and the *information* is paramount. A mage may possess a physical copy of a Quiet Item within a secured laboratory for the purpose of analysis, but they may not speak of that item in a tavern, a marketplace, or any other public venue. Talking about the item is not permitted; possessing the copy is a regulated privilege. If an Innovator seeks to study a Quiet Item, they must do so within the confines of a Guild-sanctioned research hall. Any dissemination of the knowledge contained within that copy to unauthorized parties constitutes a violation of the Accords. The Guild's stance is clear: the possession of a copy is a matter of research, but the speech regarding that copy is a matter of security.

Furthermore, research copies are not considered "tender" or "goods" in any commercial sense. They cannot be traded, sold, or gifted to individuals outside of the Guild's authorized research circles. Any attempt to use a research copy as a means of bypassing the secrecy of the Quiet List will result in the immediate seizure of the copy and the initiation of a Paradox Trial for the offending mage. The goal of the Guild is to ensure that the dangerous truths of the Quiet List remain in the shadows, accessible only to those with the clearance to handle them and the discipline to keep them hidden. See § 1.6.

sections.title: Reclassification
sections.brief: Moving B to A is not a party.

body.heading: § 300.4 Reclassification
body.text:
The administrative integrity of the Autumnwood Accords relies upon the immutable classification of magical phenomena, methodologies, and research subjects. It is the foundational principle of this Codex that the designation of a magical art, a research initiative, or a restricted substance is a matter of sovereign decree by the Guild, not a fluid state of being. Under no circumstances shall the mere alteration of a classification label—specifically the movement of a subject from Category B (Restricted Research) to Category A (Sanctioned/Public Art)—be construed as a legal transformation of the underlying nature of the act itself. The Accords Desk maintains that a change in designation is a procedural shift in oversight, not a fundamental transmutation of the magic’s inherent risk or the legal liabilities associated with its practice.

Furthermore, the doctrine of "Moving B to A is not a party" is hereby codified as a primary defense against administrative evasion. This means that if a school of magic or a specific ritual is moved from a restricted status to a sanctioned status by the Innovators or the Conservators, the legal precedents, historical prohibitions, and safety protocols associated with its previous "Category B" status remain tethered to its history. A practitioner who seeks to argue that a ritual is "safe" or "permissible" solely because it has been reclassified does so at their own peril. The Guild recognizes that while the regulatory burden may be lessened, the inherent volatility of the arcane does not diminish upon the stroke of a clerk’s quill. The reclassification is a change in the *handling* of the magic, not a change in the *essence* of the magic.

Any attempt by a faction—be it the Innovators seeking to expedite research or the Conservators seeking to isolate a threat—to use reclassification as a means to bypass the requirements of § 300.2 Necromancy; Unsanctioned Arts, shall be deemed a violation of the Accords. If a practice is inherently forbidden under § 300.2, no administrative decree may "reclassify" it into a sanctioned category to circumvent the prohibition. The Accords Desk shall view any such attempt as a bad-faith maneuver intended to undermine the stability of the Midlands. Practitioners are reminded that the Aegis Magi are tasked with enforcing the current status of the Accords; however, they are not required to ignore the historical hazards of a practice simply because its paperwork has been updated.

In the event of a dispute regarding the transition of a magical art from a restricted to a public status, the Archmage Sovereign shall mediate the determination of the "Residual Risk." This determination shall dictate what safety protocols remain in place despite the reclassification. For instance, if a blood-based transmutation is moved from Category B to Category A, the Guild may still require specific containment seals, even if the general practice is no longer subject to the Innovator's Research Permits. The Accords Desk shall not recognize any "amnesty" granted by reclassification that would exempt a practitioner from the consequences of historical violations. Legal culpability for actions taken while a magic was under Category B status remains enforceable regardless of subsequent administrative shifts.

All records of reclassification must be filed with the Autumnwood Accords Desk in triplicate. Each entry must include a "Heritage Clause" stating that the new designation does not nullify any previous safety warnings or prohibitions. Any practitioner found to be exploiting the nuance between a "Reclassified Art" and a "New Art" to evade the Paradox Trial shall be subject to immediate sanction. The Guild’s authority is derived from the preservation of the Midlands; therefore, the law shall not be treated as a labyrinth of loopholes where the mere renaming of a danger allows for its unchecked expansion. The Codex is the anchor; the labels are but the markings upon the anchor.

sections.title: Research Copies of Quiet Items
sections.brief: Copies are still Quiet. Talking about them is not.

body.heading: Research Copies of Quiet Items
body.text:
Copies are still Quiet. Talking about them is not.

The protocols governing the Quiet List are designed to ensure that certain sensitive, volatile, or socially disruptive magical phenomena remain outside the public consciousness. Under the Accords, the "Quiet" status of an item refers to its inherent nature and the Guild's determination that its public dissemination poses a risk to the stability of the Midlands or the safety of the populace. It is a fundamental principle of the Accords that the creation of a secondary representation—be it a physical manuscript, a mental projection, or a magical duplicate—does not strip the original subject of its Quiet status. A copy of a Quiet Item is, by definition, a Quiet Item.

While the physical possession of a copy is subject to the standard restrictions of the Quiet List, the act of discussing the existence of such a copy in a private, scholarly, or authorized setting does not constitute a violation of the Accords. The prohibition is against the *recitation* of the Quiet Item’s specific mechanics, incantations, or secret histories in public forums, such as taverns or marketplaces. The mere mention that a researcher possesses a "Quiet Copy" for the purpose of authorized study is permissible, provided the contents of that copy are not revealed. The law distinguishes between the *subject* of the research and the *act* of research.

Scholars affiliated with the Innovators may hold copies of Quiet Items for the purpose of restricted research, provided they have obtained the requisite permissions from Archmage Veyra or her designated deputies. These researchers may speak of their work in peer-reviewed settings, discussing the *implications* of the research without revealing the *specifics* of the Quiet Item itself. However, should a researcher describe the specificities of a Quiet Item—regardless of whether they are describing the original or a copy—they shall be subject to immediate sanction. The copy is a shadow of the original; if the shadow is cast into the light of public discourse, the prohibition is breached.

This distinction is vital for the continued advancement of the arcane arts. It allows for the progress of the Innovators to continue in the shadows of the Hall of Autumn Wood without alerting the Regal Empire or the Silver Flame to the Guild's internal methodologies. The Guild recognizes that knowledge is power, but the Accords recognize that *public* knowledge of certain powers is a liability. Therefore, while the copy remains bound by the silence of the List, the researcher is permitted to speak of the *process* of the research. See § 300.2. Any violation of this distinction by a practitioner shall be referred to the Desk for a Paradox Trial to determine the extent of the breach.

sections.title: Research Permits
sections.brief: Form, fee, who signs.

body.heading: Research Permits
body.text:
§ 400.1 Research Permits — Form, fee, who signs.

All inquiries into the manipulation of high-density mana, the exploration of restricted schools, or the creation of volatile arcane phenomena shall be subject to the rigorous oversight of the Autumnwood Accords. No mage, regardless of standing or lineage, may commence any undertaking that risks the integrity of the Midlands or the stability of the local weave without a valid Research Permit issued by the Accords Desk. The application for such a permit must be submitted on the Official Form 400-A, which requires a comprehensive description of the intended methodology, a projected duration of the research, and a detailed risk assessment of potential blowback. Failure to provide a complete risk assessment shall result in an immediate summary rejection of the application without the possibility of appeal for a period of three lunar cycles.

The fee for a Research Permit is calculated based on the magnitude of the arcane flux expected during the proceedings. This fee is non-refundable and must be deposited in the Guild’s treasury prior to the signing of the permit. For research involving high-risk categories, such as those bordering on the forbidden schools outlined in § 300.2, the fee shall be tripled to account for the increased surveillance requirements. It is strictly understood that these fees do not constitute a payment for the right to perform the magic, but rather a tax on the potential hazard posed to the public and the Guild's interests. The Accords Desk reserves the right to adjust fee structures based on the current volatility of the regional mana ley lines.

The authority to sign and validate a Research Permit rests solely with the presiding leadership of the relevant faction, as mediated by Archmage Veyra. For standard research, a signature from a Senior Conservator or a High Innovator is sufficient, provided it is countersigned by an Aegis Mage to ensure enforcement capabilities are available. In cases of extreme complexity or novelty, the Archmage Sovereign must personally review and sign the permit. No provisional permits shall be issued by lower-ranking officials, nor shall a permit granted by a Conservator be superseded by an Innovator without a formal decree from the Desk. All signed permits shall be stamped with the official seal of the Accords; see § 1.9. Any researcher found operating under an expired permit, or an altered permit, shall be subject to immediate seizure of materials and referral to the Paradox Trial for sentencing.

sections.title: Pocket Dimensions as Labs
sections.brief: Hours inside a pocket are still hours for the other party.

body.heading: Pocket Dimensions as Labs
body.text:
Pursuant to the regulatory framework established by the Autumnwood Accords and the subsequent oversight of the Conservators, all researchers seeking to utilize extra-planar spaces or artificially generated pocket dimensions for the purpose of laboratory experimentation must adhere to the temporal parity standards set forth herein. While the physical laws of a pocket dimension may be significantly altered from those of the Midlands, the temporal flow remains subject to the Guild’s primary oversight regarding labor, duration, and cognitive preservation. Specifically, any research conducted within a pocket dimension, regardless of its internal expansion or spatial distortion, shall be measured against the standard chronometry of the primary plane of existence from which the laboratory originated.

The intent of this provision is to prevent the exploitation of "dilated" time as a means to circumvent the standard duration limits imposed on restricted research permits. Under the authority of Archmage Theron, no researcher may claim that a week of experimentation occurred in a matter of seconds—or vice versa—for the purpose of reporting progress or fulfilling the temporal requirements of a permit. If a researcher enters a pocket dimension that experiences a slower temporal flow, the Guild shall recognize the duration based on the external world's clock. Conversely, if a researcher utilizes a pocket dimension where time accelerates, the Guild shall view the total duration of the experiment as being equal to the time elapsed in the external world. This ensures that the cognitive toll on the practitioner and the potential for catastrophic instability remain within the manageable parameters defined by the Conservators.

Furthermore, all logistical requirements, including the consumption of resources, the degradation of reagents, and the expiration of temporary mouths, shall be calculated based on the external time. Should a researcher be trapped or detained within a pocket dimension, the Guild’s rescue protocols shall initiate based on the external duration of the disappearance. All laboratory equipment, regardless of its location in a pocket dimension, remains subject to the maintenance schedules of the Guild. See § 1.6 for relevant definitions of "Pocket Dimension" and "Primary Plane." Failure to maintain temporal parity during research shall result in the immediate revocation of the researcher's permit and a referral to the Aegis Magi for a formal audit of the laboratory's stability.

body.heading: Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time
body.text:
The Guild hereby establishes a strict prohibition against the use of time-stop magic or any temporal stasis effects as a means of stalling, extending, or manipulating legal settlements, debt repayments, or the fulfillment of guild-mandated duties. In any instance where a mage is engaged in a legal proceeding, a debt negotiation, or a contractual dispute, the application of time-stop magic shall not be recognized as a pause in the proceedings. For the purposes of the Accords, time-stop during a settlement is still considered active time. Any party attempting to utilize such magic to "freeze" a situation to their advantage shall be deemed in violation of the Guild's integrity protocols.

The principle of "Interest in Time" dictates that if a mage uses magic to halt the flow of time for others while they proceed with a specific action—be it the completion of a task, the movement of goods, or the negotiation of a contract—the Guild shall treat the duration of the stasis as active time for the purpose of all calculations. This includes, but is not limited to, the expiration of deadlines, the accrual of interest on debts, and the expiration of temporary licenses. If a mage spends what they perceive as one hour in a time-stopped state to complete a task, the Guild shall record that hour as having elapsed in the standard flow of the Midlands. No "borrowed" time shall be granted to the practitioner; the magic used to halt the world does not grant the user a reprieve from the responsibilities of the world.

Furthermore, any attempt to use time-stop magic to evade the consequences of a Paradox Trial shall be met with the highest tier of sanction. The use of such magic to delay the arrival of an Aegis Magi enforcement team or to stall a peer review shall be considered an aggravating factor in the determination of guilt. All mages are reminded that while the mastery of time is a sophisticated pursuit, it does not exempt the practitioner from the temporal obligations of the Autumnwood Accords. See § 1.6 for definitions of "Temporal Stasis" and "Settlement."

body.heading: Specimen Custody
body.text:
All biological or inorganic entities of significant size, complexity, or magical potency that are captured, restrained, or petrified by a practitioner shall be classified as "Inventory" under the Guild’s custody regulations. This classification holds until such time as the specimen is officially released, destroyed, or permanently integrated into a controlled environment. No specimen, regardless of its current state of animation or petrification, shall be considered a "Trophy" or a "Personal Possession" for the purposes of Guild transport or public display until the proper documentation of release or destruction is filed with the Desk.

A petrified monster, for instance, remains a hazardous specimen under the jurisdiction of the Conservators. Because a petrified entity retains the potential for sudden reanimation or magical resonance, it must be handled with the same safety protocols as a living creature. Practitioners are prohibited from transporting such specimens across the Midlands without a certified containment vessel and a valid transport permit. The classification as "Inventory" ensures that the Guild maintains a record of all hazardous materials in circulation, preventing the clandestine movement of dangerous entities by rogue mages or radical Innovators.

The transition from "Inventory" to "Trophy" may only occur upon the formal "Decommissioning of Threat" by a certified Aegis Mage or the "Sanctioned Release" by a Conservator. Until such a certification is issued, the practitioner is responsible for the maintenance, containment, and safety of the specimen. Any loss of a specimen while it is still classified as Inventory shall be treated as a breach of safety protocol, potentially resulting in a Paradox Trial. Furthermore, the possession of such specimens in private residences or unauthorized laboratories is strictly forbidden under the research restrictions of the Innovators. See § 400.1 for research permit requirements.

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth
body.text:
The Guild hereby clarifies the distinction between "Controlled Research" and "Unauthorized Field Use" regarding the growth of large-scale magical structures or entities. Any instance of growth magic—including the rapid expansion of flora, the scaling of architectural constructs, or the somatic growth of biological entities—that occurs within a public street, marketplace, or any other non-sanctioned public space shall be automatically classified as "Unauthorized Field Use." This classification remains final and absolute, regardless of whether the practitioner claims the growth was a byproduct of an accident or if the practitioner intends to study the results of said growth at a later date.

The Innovators may argue that such growth provides a unique opportunity for observation and data collection; however, the Conservators maintain that the risks to public safety and structural integrity in the Midlands outweigh the benefits of such field experiments. Because the growth occurs in a public sphere, it is subject to immediate intervention by the Aegis Magi. The fact that a mage may later seek to study the growth in a laboratory does not retroactively grant the initial growth "Research" status. To be classified as research, the growth must occur within a licensed laboratory or a designated "Wilderness Study Zone" with a pre-approved permit from Janna Brightspark’s office.

Any mage found to be responsible for unauthorized titan growth in a public area shall be subject to immediate fines and a mandatory review of their licensing. If the growth poses an immediate threat to life or property, the Aegis Magi are authorized to use whatever force is necessary to neutralize the growth, with the practitioner being held liable for all damages. This law serves to protect the infrastructure of the Autumnwood Accords from the reckless expansionism often associated with radical innovation. See § 200.1 for licensure requirements and § 400.1 for research permits.

sections.title: Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time
sections.brief: Time-stop during settlement is still time.

body.heading: Borrowed Hours; Interest in Time
body.text:
Pursuant to the overarching tenets of the Autumnwood Accords, specifically regarding the temporal stability of the Midlands, any mage who employs chronomancy or time-dilation effects during the duration of a legal settlement, a debt negotiation, or a formal mediation process shall be held to the standard of continuous temporal progression. It is hereby codified that the suspension of the flow of time for the purpose of deliberation, contemplation, or the cooling oftempers does not constitute a cessation of the legal clock. For the purposes of the Guild, time-stop during settlement is still time. If a party to a dispute invokes a chronomantic stasis to prolong a negotiation, the interest accrued on any outstanding magical debts or temporal reparations shall continue to calculate at the standard rate prescribed by Archmage Veyra.

The Innovators may argue that a frozen moment is a vacuum of progression, yet the Conservators maintain that the intent of the mage is the primary driver of the Accord's jurisdiction. Therefore, any attempt to utilize "Borrowed Hours" to evade the consequences of a delayed agreement shall be viewed as a bad-faith manipulation of the arcane weave. Mages seeking to enter a period of stasis for the purpose of intensive study or meditation must first secure a research permit under § 400.1, and even such permits do not exempt the individual from the temporal taxes of the Guild. Any mage found attempting to "pause" the legalities of a contract while continuing to benefit from the status quo of that contract shall be subject to a Paradox Trial.

Furthermore, the Aegis Magi are authorized to impose a "Temporal Interest Penalty" on any individual who purposefully creates a localized time-stop to prevent the expiration of a temporary mouth or a provisional license. The Guild recognizes that time is a sacred resource, and its artificial manipulation for the sake of administrative evasion is a violation of Mana Reverence. See § 1.6 for definitions regarding temporal flux and magical debt. Any disputes arising from the calculation of interest during a period of suspended animation shall be adjudicated by the Desk, with the Archmage Sovereign holding final authority on the determination of "active" versus "passive" temporal states.

body.heading: Specimen Custody
body.text:
The possession and transport of biological entities, whether living, dormant, or petrified, are governed by strict protocols to ensure the preservation of the Midlands' ecological and magical integrity. Under the Accords, any creature of significant magical potency or size that has been rendered into a state of petrification, stasis, or permanent slumber is strictly classified as inventory, not a trophy. This classification remains in effect regardless of the owner's intent, the aesthetic value of the specimen, or the degree of martial prowess required to achieve the petrification. A petrified monster is inventory, not a trophy, until released.

Owners of such specimens are required to register the entity with the nearest Guild outpost within three lunar cycles of acquisition. This registration serves as a manifest of the specimen's origin, its current state of stasis, and the specific seals used to maintain its condition. The failure to register a petrified specimen constitutes a violation of the research safety protocols outlined in § 400.1. Furthermore, the transport of such inventory across provincial lines requires a verified transport manifest; if a specimen is seized by the Aegis Magi without proper documentation, it shall be impounded as unauthorized material and may be subject to immediate destruction if it poses a risk to the public.

The distinction between inventory and trophy is critical for the purposes of the Paradox Trial. A mage who displays a petrified creature as a mark of personal achievement in a public forum may be cited for "Ostentatious Display of Forbidden Stasis," especially if the creature belongs to a species protected by the Conservators. Conversely, a mage who treats a petrified entity as a mere object of trade without proper licensing may be charged with "Negligent Handling of High-Potency Remains." No specimen may be "released"—whether through the reversal of a petrification spell or the termination of a stasis field—without a formal release permit issued by the Desk. See § 1.6 for further clarification on the definition of "High-Potency Remains."

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth
body.text:
The Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding the manifestation of large-scale, rapid-growth magic in non-designated zones. Any instance of growth magic utilized within a public thoroughfare, residential district, or any area not specifically zoned for agricultural or botanical experimentation is strictly classified as unauthorized field use. This classification is absolute and pertains to the act of manifestation itself, rather than the subsequent academic pursuit of the perpetrator. Growth magic in a street is field use, not research, even if someone later studies it.

The Innovators frequently advocate for the "experimental freedom" of the arts, yet the Accord dictates that the safety of the populace overrides the curiosity of the individual. If a mage utilizes growth charms to manifest flora, structures, or biological masses in a street, the resulting infrastructure is considered a public hazard. Even if the practitioner subsequently submits a retrospective request for research credit or seeks to categorize the growth as a "controlled experiment," the Guild shall not grant such status retroactively. The act of casting in a public space bypasses the protections and privileges afforded by § 400.1, and the practitioner shall be liable for all damages and the costs of removal as determined by the Aegis Magi.

Furthermore, any growth that results in the obstruction of trade routes, the damage to Goodstyle Artisan products, or the endangerment of common travelers will result in immediate summary judgment. The Guild does not recognize "unintentional growth" as a valid defense if the mage failed to consult the local cartography or the one-T cartography for land-use restrictions. Because the growth occurs in a public domain, the legal status of the magic is "Field Use," which carries a higher penalty of sanction and seal than "Restricted Research." Any mage found in violation of this clause may be required to undergo a Paradox Trial to determine the extent of their negligence. See § 1.6 for the distinction between "Field Use" and "Restricted Research."

sections.title: Specimen Custody
sections.brief: A petrified monster is inventory, not a trophy, until released.

body.heading: Specimen Custody
body.text:
Pursuant to the oversight of the Autumnwood Accords, all biological or semi-biological entities that have undergone petrification, stasis, or arcane crystallization shall be classified as Guild Inventory rather than personal trophies, spoils of war, or decorative acquisitions. This classification applies to any creature, beast, or sentient being rendered immobile by high-level transmutation or temporal suspension. The Accords Desk asserts that the inherent potential for animation within a petrified specimen constitutes a lingering arcane signature that must be accounted for within the Guild's safety protocols. Any mage who secures such a specimen is strictly prohibited from displaying it in public spaces, taverns, or non-sanctioned residences without a verified containment permit issued by the Conservators.

The distinction between inventory and trophy is a legal necessity to prevent the misappropriation of hazardous magical assets. A trophy is a static object of personal vanity; a petrified monster is a dormant hazard capable of sudden, uncontrolled restoration or violent expiration. Should a specimen be released from its state of stasis—whether by intent, accident, or environmental decay—the responsibility for its containment shifts from passive inventory to active containment. Any mage found in possession of a released specimen that has not been properly neutralized or bound shall be subject to immediate seizure by the Aegis Magi. The Guild maintains that the preservation of the public's safety outweighs the individual's right to own a "curiosity" of such volatile nature.

Furthermore, the transportation of petrified specimens across the Midlands requires a manifest of transit. If a specimen is moved from a private laboratory to a public thoroughfare, it must be accompanied by a clerk or a licensed handler who possesses the knowledge to initiate a "Cold Seal" in the event of a breach. Failure to provide such documentation shall result in the immediate revocation of the owner's Research Permit and a referral to the Paradox Trial for reckless endangerment of the populace. See § 1.6 for definitions regarding "Arcane Signature" and "Cold Seal." All specimens held in private vaults must be reported to the Archmage Veyra’s office biennially for audit.

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth
body.text:
The application of growth magic within any urban center, village, or public thoroughfare is hereby defined as unauthorized field use, regardless of the caster's stated intent or the eventual academic utility of the results. This provision serves to distinguish between controlled laboratory experimentation and the reckless expansion of magical flora or fauna in civilian spheres. If a mage utilizes growth enchantments to produce oversized produce, decorative greenery, or structural reinforcements in a street or marketplace, the act is automatically classified as a violation of the Accords. The fact that a mage may subsequently attempt to study the resulting growth as part of a research project does not retroactively合法ize the initial casting. The initial act of expansion is the primary offense; the study of the consequence is a separate, and often secondary, matter of record.

The Accords Desk recognizes the Innovators' desire to push the boundaries of botanical and structural transmutation. However, the Conservators maintain that the unpredictable nature of "Titan Growth" poses an unacceptable risk to the structural integrity of the Midlands. Growth magic of this magnitude can cause unintended structural collapse, the choking of water supplies, or the creation of ecological dead zones. Therefore, any mage seeking to experiment with growth magnitudes exceeding standard horticultural limits must do so within a designated research zone or a pocket dimension as authorized under § 400.2. The use of such magic in a street is a breach of the public peace and an affront to the stability of the Accord.

Mages who engage in unauthorized field growth are liable for all costs associated with the removal of the growth and the restoration of the affected area. If the growth results in property damage or the endangerment of life, the caster shall be summoned before a council of peers for a Paradox Trial. The penalty for such violations may range from the Sanction and Seal of the caster's growth-related schools to the full sequestration of their research materials. See § 1.6 for further clarification on the "Midlands Public Thoroughfare" boundaries. No "Wario Coin" or other non-tender currency shall be accepted as restitution for damages caused by unauthorized growth. All restitution must be paid in standard Guild-approved currency or through labor-service to the Goodstyle Artisans for reconstruction.

sections.title: Unauthorized Titan Growth
sections.brief: Growth magic in a street is field use, not research, even if someone later studies it.

body.heading: Unauthorized Titan Growth and Field Use Classifications
body.text:
The Guild hereby establishes a strict distinction between sanctioned laboratory growth and unauthorized field application of expansionary arcana. Pursuant to the primary mandates of the Autumnwood Accords, all magical research conducted under the auspices of the Innovators must be confined to designated research zones, such as those permitted under § 400.2. Any application of growth magic that occurs within a public thoroughfare, residential district, or any non-sanctioned geographical coordinate shall be automatically classified as field use. This classification remains immutable regardless of the caster's stated intent, academic justification, or the subsequent analytical study of the resulting growth. The Guild recognizes that the volatility of expansionary magic is compounded by the proximity of civilian infrastructure and public transit; therefore, the mere act of manifesting such growth in a street environment constitutes a breach of the safety protocols governing the use of the Unsanctioned Arts.

Specifically, the Guild shall not entertain any defense claiming that the growth of a Titan-class entity or any related biological expansion was intended as a preliminary experiment for future scholarly review. If the growth occurs in a public street, it is, by definition, a field operation. The fact that a mage may later seek to study the biological properties, structural integrity, or magical residue of said growth does not retroactively transform the initial casting into a protected research activity. See § 400.1 for the requirements of research permits, which explicitly exclude any actions resulting in uncontrolled environmental expansion. Any mage found to have initiated growth magic in an unauthorized area shall be subject to immediate investigation by the Aegis Magi to determine the extent of the structural damage and the risk posed to the surrounding populace.

Furthermore, the Guild notes specific precedents involving unauthorized field use on the Markop region. Any growth magic utilized on Markop that results in Titan-scale expansion is deemed a violation of the Accords' stability requirements as championed by the Conservators. Such incidents shall be recorded as unauthorized field use and shall not be eligible for the protections afforded to the Innovators' restricted research permits. The Guild shall treat all such instances as reckless endangerment of the Midlands' magical equilibrium. Any mage involved in such growth shall be referred to the council for the Paradox Trial, wherein the punishment may include the sealing of the mage's arcana or permanent relocation to a pocket-prison to ensure the continued stability of the public sphere.

In cases where a mage claims that the growth was a byproduct of a different, sanctioned spell, the burden of proof lies with the caster to demonstrate that the growth was neither intended nor foreseeable. However, the Guild maintains a policy of strict liability for expansionary magic; if the growth occurs in a street, the caster is held responsible for the entirety of the resulting ecological and structural consequences. No provision exists within this Codex to excuse growth magic based on the "necessity" of the expansion or the "scientific value" of the Titan. For further clarification on the distinction between research and field use, see § 400.1 and § 400.2. All growth magic conducted without a specific permit for the specific location shall be prosecuted under the most severe penalties available to the Aegis Magi.

sections.title: Field Casting for Value
sections.brief: Public safety distance, notice to non-casters.

body.heading: Field Casting for Value
body.text:
§ 500.1 Field Casting for Value

Any practitioner of the arcane who intends to perform a manifestation of magical energy within a public or semi-public thoroughfare for the purpose of obtaining tangible, intangible, or spiritual compensation shall be deemed to be "Casting for Value." This designation applies regardless of whether the compensation is offered in the form of coin, labor, goods, or the fulfillment of a specific request by a non-magical entity. Pursuant to § 200.1, all such acts require a valid license from the Autumnwood Accords Desk. The mere act of performing a spell for a friend or family member does not exempt the caster from these regulations if the resulting outcome provides a measurable benefit to the recipient. The Guild maintains that the public sphere is not a laboratory, nor is it a theater for unregulated arcane commerce.

To mitigate the risk of collateral magical displacement and physical harm to the populace, all Field Casting for Value must adhere to strict Public Safety Distances. A minimum buffer zone of fifty paces must be maintained between the epicenter of the arcane manifestation and any non-consenting bystander. This distance is non-negotiable and must be calculated based on the projected "Arcane Radius" of the spell. If a spell’s inherent nature—such as a large-scale transmutation or a high-yield pyrotechnic enchantment—exceeds a radius of twenty paces, the caster must establish a physical barricade and provide a formal notice to all non-casters within a hundred paces. Failure to provide such notice, or the failure to maintain the safety buffer, shall constitute a violation of the Accords and may result in immediate intervention by the Aegis Magi.

Notice to non-casters must be delivered in a clear, audible manner, preferably via a minor auditory enchantment that does not infringe upon the Quiet List. The notice must state the nature of the casting, the estimated duration, and the primary risks involved. For example, a caster performing a "Frost-Touch" enchantment for the purpose of preserving local produce must announce the "localized temperature drop" and "potential for slick surfaces." If a non-caster enters the designated buffer zone after notice has been given, the caster is permitted to use minor non-lethal binding spells to ensure the safety of the bystander, provided such actions do not exceed the scope of the original casting. Any caster who proceeds with a casting for value without satisfying these proximity and notification requirements shall be subject to immediate seizure of the proceeds and a formal review by the Paradox Trial. See § 1.6 for definitions of "Public Thoroughfare."

body.heading: Unscheduled Weather
body.text:
§ 500.2 Unscheduled Weather

The atmospheric integrity of the Midlands is a shared resource, and the manipulation of meteorological phenomena for private gain is strictly regulated under the Autumnwood Accords. Any mage who deliberately invokes, alters, or sustains atmospheric conditions—including but not limited to precipitation, wind velocity, temperature fluctuations, or cloud density—for the purpose of securing an agricultural advantage shall be subject to the provisions of this section. This includes "Precision Irrigation" via localized rain, "Accelerated Maturation" through artificial warmth, and "Pest Deterrence" via sustained gale-force winds. While the Innovators may argue for the efficiency of such methods, the Conservators maintain that large-scale weather manipulation risks the stability of the local ley lines and the health of neighboring lands.

Mages seeking to utilize weather-altering magic for agricultural purposes must submit a "Meteorological Impact Study" to the Accords Desk no less than fourteen days prior to the intended casting. This study must detail the geographical boundaries of the effect, the duration of the manipulation, and the measures taken to prevent "Atmospheric Bleed," wherein the desired weather effect spills over into neighboring properties or public waterways. Only those with a "Weather-Class Permit" may proceed with such castings. If a mage performs these actions without a permit, the Guild reserves the right to neutralize the effect at the caster's expense, regardless of the damage caused to the crops or livestock during the intervention.

Furthermore, it is explicitly stated that the Guild’s insurance protocols and the Goodstyle Artisans' liability protections do not cover losses incurred from weather that has been intentionally summoned or modified by a licensed or unlicensed mage. If a farmer’s crop is destroyed by a "rogue" storm, the Guild shall not be held liable. Conversely, if a farmer’s crop is destroyed by a storm they specifically paid a mage to summon—and that storm exceeded the permitted parameters—the farmer may file a grievance with the Desk. However, the Guild shall not provide restitution for "Unscheduled Weather" events that were not filed correctly. The Accords distinguish clearly between "Act of Nature" and "Act of Arcana"; the latter carries a higher burden of proof and a stricter penalty for negligence. See § 400.1 for research permits related to atmospheric study.

body.heading: Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion
body.text:
§ 500.3 Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion

In the event of a magical discharge, structural collapse, or "Arcane Rupture" that results in the destruction of Guild hallways, common areas, or shared laboratory corridors, the following protocols for restoration shall apply. The primary objective of these rules is to ensure that the flow of commerce and study is not impeded by the debris of magical failure. The party responsible for the discharge—hereafter referred to as the "Originating Party"—is legally obligated to provide the initial assessment of the site. This assessment must determine if the explosion was a result of authorized research, a violation of the Iron Mandate (where applicable to external threats), or a lapse in personal magical containment.

The Originating Party shall be held solely responsible for the initial "Clearing Phase." This includes the removal of large-scale debris, the stabilization of any remaining magical residue, and the neutralization of lingering "Arcane Static" that may cause disorientation or minor hexing to passersby. The Originating Party must file a "Damage and Incident Report" with the Desk within twenty-four hours of the event. If the explosion occurred during a sanctioned Innovator project, the costs of the Clearing Phase may be shared with the Guild’s general fund, provided the research was approved under § 400.1. However, if the explosion was a result of a violation of the Forbidden Schools or the Quiet List, the Originating Party shall bear the entirety of the restoration costs.

Following the Clearing Phase, the "Sanitization and Sweeping" of the corridor shall be conducted. While the Originating Party is responsible for the heavy lifting, the Guild may delegate the fine sweeping and polishing to the Goodstyle Artisans or a designated cleaning construct. The Originating Party shall be billed for the labor of these third parties at the standard Guild rate. If the corridor remains unusable for more than forty-eight hours due to lingering magical instability, the Originating Party shall be subject to a "Loss of Access" fine. Furthermore, any physical damage to the architectural integrity of the Autumn Wood hall must be repaired to the original specifications as recorded in the Guild’s archives. No mage may attempt to "patch" a wall with permanent transmutation without express permission from Archmage Veyra. See § 100.6 for Delegation to Clerks regarding restoration billing.

body.heading: Healing Offered as Consideration
body.text:
§ 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration

The provision of restorative magic—including but not limited to the closing of wounds, the curing of blights, or the mending of broken bones—is a sacred duty and a regulated practice. Under the Autumnwood Accords, healing may never be sold as a primary "Contract Term" for unlicensed individuals. While a mage may accept a voluntary gift or a modest tip for a healing act, the systematic sale of healing as a commodity requires a specific "Medicinal Casting License." This distinction is vital to prevent the exploitation of the infirm and to ensure that life-saving magic is not hoarded by those with the highest capital.

Any entity, including a merchant house or a private estate, that includes "Magical Healing" as a mandatory condition of a contract—such as a labor agreement, a prisoner exchange, or a debt repayment—must ensure that the healer providing the service is currently licensed by the Accords Desk. If a contract is found to be predicated on "Unlicensed Healing," the contract shall be declared null and void by the Archmage Sovereign, and the unlicensed healer shall be subject to a "Practice Violation" penalty. This includes "Passive Healing" zones or "Restorative Fields" established in commercial spaces. Such fields must be registered with the Guild to ensure they do not interfere with the local mana flow or create "Healing Sinks" that drain the vitality of nearby non-consenting individuals.

Furthermore, healing offered as consideration for the release of a debt or as a "penalty" for a crime is strictly prohibited. The Guild views the commodification of biological integrity as a violation of Mana Reverence. If a mage is caught selling "Healing Vials" or "Restorative Potions" without a secondary manufacturing license, they shall be subject to a permanent ban from the Hall of Autumn Wood. For those who hold the proper licenses, the Desk provides a standardized fee schedule to ensure that healing costs remain equitable across the Midlands. Any deviation from these fees in a public setting must be reported to the Aegis Magi to prevent predatory pricing. See § 200.1 for Licensure Required.

body.heading: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
body.text:
§ 500.5 Love Philtre and Undue Influence

The use of enchantments to manipulate the emotional state, desires, or loyalties of another sentient being is a grave violation of the Autumnwood Accords. Specifically, the creation and distribution of "Love Philtrés," "Charisma Enhancers," or any "Affective Alteration" draughts or spells are strictly prohibited. A philtre, by its very definition in Guild law, is an instrument of undue influence; therefore, the administration of such a substance can never constitute valid consent. Any magical effect that overrides the free will of a sentient being to induce affection, obedience, or obsession shall be classified as a "Violation of Autonomy."

Mages who manufacture or possess "Love Philtrés" are subject to immediate seizure of their materials and a mandatory review by the Conservators. If such a substance is administered, the victim shall be entitled to a "Neutralization Rite" performed by the Guild at the caster's expense. The caster shall be liable for all damages arising from the duration of the undue influence, including emotional trauma, loss of property, or social standing. The Innovators may argue that "Emotional Buffs" are a form of artistic expression or psychological therapy, but the Accords are clear: any magic that bypasses the conscious choice of the subject is a breach of the peace.

Furthermore, the use of "Undue Influence" in negotiations, political maneuvering, or the acquisition of property is a felony under the Accords. Mages who utilize "Subtle Charm" or "Persuasion Weaving" to coerce others into signing agreements shall have their licenses revoked. This prohibition extends to the "Quiet List"; any spell designed to make a person "forget" their opposition to a deal is an even more severe violation. The Guild maintains that the sanctity of the mind is paramount. Those who seek to turn the hearts of others into puppets of their own design shall find themselves facing the Paradox Trial, with the potential for permanent sealing of their arcane abilities. See § 300.2 for Necromancy and Unsanctioned Arts.

sections.title: Unscheduled Weather
sections.brief: Calling weather for agricultural advantage. Insurance does not cover weather you called.

body.heading: Unscheduled Weather
body.text:
§ 500.2 Unscheduled Weather. Any practitioner of the arcane who intentionally alters, induces, or manipulates atmospheric conditions for the purpose of providing agricultural advantage—including but not limited to the stimulation of crop growth, the redirection of irrigation flows, or the mitigation of frost—shall be subject to the oversight of the Accords Desk. While the Guild recognizes the utility of such magic in the maintenance of the Midlands, it is strictly prohibited to utilize high-magnitude meteorological manipulation without a pre-approved Seasonal Adjustment Permit. The Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding the use of "Growth-Spurring Rains" or "Artificial Sun-Cycles" that bypass natural cycles to create market monopolies or ecological imbalances.

Furthermore, let it be known that the Guild’s internal insurance and indemnity protections do not extend to damages arising from self-induced meteorological events. If a mage invokes a localized storm or heatwave to benefit their own holdings or those of their patrons, and that event subsequently causes collateral damage to neighboring properties, the Guild shall hold the caster personally liable for all reparations. This includes, but is not limited to, the destruction of neighboring structures, the contamination of shared water tables, or the unintended migration of local fauna. The caster shall be required to provide a full ledger of the magical expenditure and a comprehensive damage assessment to the Accords Desk within three lunar cycles of the event.

In cases where the weather is called for the purpose of "Force Majeure" defense in civil disputes, the Accords Desk shall strike such claims from the record immediately. A mage cannot claim "Act of God" for a phenomenon they personally authored for commercial gain. Any practitioner found in violation of § 500.2 shall be subject to a fine of fifty gold marks per acre of affected land, plus a mandatory period of service in the Goodstyle Artisans' restoration wing. See § 1.6 for definitions of "Agricultural Advantage."

body.heading: Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion
body.text:
§ 500.3 Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion. In the event of a magical discharge, structural failure, or intentional detonation resulting in the debris-clogging of any common hallway, thoroughfare, or laboratory corridor, the immediate priority shall be the restoration of safe passage. The practitioner responsible for the primary arcane discharge—hereafter referred to as the "Originator"—is legally bound to file a Notice of Incident with the nearest Aegis Magi outpost within one hour of the event. This notice must include the estimated magnitude of the blast, the intended objective of the casting, and a list of any materials rendered unstable by the shockwave.

Following the filing of the Notice of Incident, the Originator shall be held solely responsible for the physical restoration of the corridor. This duty includes the removal of pulverized masonry, the neutralization of lingering arcane radiation, and the sweeping of all particulate matter. The Originator may hire authorized laborers, provided such laborers are bound by a non-disclosure agreement regarding the Guild’s internal architecture. No other Guild member, regardless of their proximity to the blast site, shall be required to perform manual labor or maintenance for the Originator. The "First-In-First-Out" rule of debris clearance applies: the Originator must clear a path of at least three feet in width before any other traffic may be permitted to pass.

Should the Originator fail to initiate sweeping and clearing within two hours of the incident, the Accords Desk may authorize an Aegis Magi cleanup crew to intervene. In such an instance, the Originator shall be billed at triple the standard labor rate, and the costs shall be deducted from their annual research stipend. Furthermore, if the explosion resulted from a violation of the Forbidden Schools as defined in § 300.2, the Originator shall be subject to immediate detention for a Paradox Trial. See § 100.6 for matters regarding the delegation of cleanup duties to junior clerks.

body.heading: Healing Offered as Consideration
body.text:
§ 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration. The provision of restorative magic, mending of flesh, or the alleviation of chronic ailment shall not be considered a mere "service" when it is integrated into a formal contract as a primary consideration for labor, goods, or land. Any practitioner who offers unlicensed healing as a contract term—specifically in the context of indentured servitude, debt repayment, or the fulfillment of commercial obligations—is in violation of the Accords. The Guild recognizes that the commodification of life-force and the use of healing as a tool of coercion creates a predatory environment that undermines the stability of the Midlands.

When healing is offered as a component of a contract, it must be performed by a licensed Medical Arcanist who has submitted a formal "Healing Clause" to the Accords Desk. This clause must specify the limits of the healing (e.g., "mending of superficial wounds only" or "alleviation of non-magical fatigue") and the duration of the treatment. If a mage uses healing to "repair" a worker who has been injured in the line of duty, this is permitted only if the worker retains full autonomy over the treatment and is not being "repaired" to continue labor against their will. Any healing performed as a "maintenance" requirement for a non-human construct or a bound entity without a specific permit is strictly prohibited.

Practitioners found engaging in the unlicensed sale of healing as a contract term shall have their licenses suspended for a period of no less than three years. Furthermore, any contracts found to contain "Life-Debt" clauses—whereby a healing spell is used to generate a debt that cannot be repaid through standard currency—shall be declared null and void by the Accords Desk. The Guild shall not recognize the Wario Coin as a valid tender for the settlement of any healing debts. See § 300.2 for restrictions on blood-based restorative arts.

body.heading: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
body.text:
§ 500.5 Love Philtre and Undue Influence. The creation, distribution, or administration of any philtre, potion, or enchantment designed to induce romantic affection, sexual desire, or profound emotional dependency—commonly referred to as "Love Philters"—is strictly prohibited under the Accords. The Guild maintains that the imposition of affection via arcane means constitutes a fundamental violation of individual autonomy and a breach of the Mana Reverence principles. No philtre, regardless of its potency or the "gentleness" of its effects, shall be considered a valid means of establishing consent.

Any individual who administers a philtre to another shall be held liable for "Undue Influence." This offense carries a heavy presumption of guilt. If a victim is found under the influence of a philtre, the administration of such a substance shall be treated as an assault on the victim's mental integrity. The perpetrator shall be subject to immediate seizure of all brewing apparatuses and a mandatory referral to the Aegis Magi for interrogation. If the philtre was administered with the intent to secure a marriage, a property transfer, or any other legal agreement, the resulting contract shall be deemed fraudulent and unenforceable by the Archmage Sovereign.

The Innovator faction may seek to study the chemical components of such substances for research purposes, but such research must be conducted within a sealed pocket-dimension lab as per § 400.2 and may never involve human subjects. Any "social lubrication" spells that do not involve the manipulation of deep-seated emotions may be permitted, provided they do not cross the threshold into involuntary suggestibility. Practitioners who knowingly sell philtres to the public—including those sold by Goodstyle Artisans—shall be permanently barred from the Hall of Autumn Wood. See § 1.6 for the legal definition of "Undue Influence."

sections.title: Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion
sections.brief: Who files first. Who sweeps.

body.heading: Corridor Courtesy After an Explosion
body.text:
Who files first. Who sweeps.

In the event of a localized structural failure resulting from high-output arcane discharge, the immediate restoration of the corridor's integrity shall be governed by the protocols of priority and maintenance established herein. While the primary responsibility for the containment of the initial breach rests with the Aegis Magi, the subsequent administrative and physical restoration of the corridor is subject to the "First-Response Filing" principle. The mage or researcher responsible for the discharge shall be required to file a formal Notice of Incident with the nearest Clerk of the Accords within one standard turn of the stabilization of the area. This filing must include the specific arcane signature of the spell, the estimated yield of the explosion, and a comprehensive list of any structural components rendered non-viable. Failure to file within the designated timeframe shall result in an automatic escalation of the fine, as per the standard penalties for administrative negligence.

Regarding the physical remediation of the corridor, the "Who Sweeps" doctrine dictates that the burden of labor is directly proportional to the magnitude of the disturbance. Should the explosion be classified as a Minor Outburst (less than three meters of debris), the responsible party shall be tasked with the manual clearing of the corridor. For Moderate Disruptions (extending to five meters or involving the shattering of masonry), the responsible party shall be required to hire a certified Goodstyle Artisan to perform the sweeping and debris removal, ensuring that the aesthetic and structural standards of the Autumn Wood are maintained. In cases of Major Catastrophes, where the corridor is rendered entirely impassable or the structural integrity of the Hall is compromised, the Guild shall appoint a restoration crew, and the costs shall be deducted from the responsible party’s research stipend or seized from their personal holdings.

Furthermore, no mage shall attempt to clear debris until the Clerk has verified that the area is free of lingering residual mana. Any individual attempting to "sweep" a corridor while active arcane residue is present risks a Paradox Trial for reckless endangerment. The Clerk of the Accords reserves the right to delay the sweeping process until a full survey of the site is completed, regardless of the urgency of the transit. See § 1.7 for matters regarding the aggregation of conduct in public spaces.

body.heading: Healing Offered as Consideration
body.text:
Unlicensed healing sold as a contract term.

The practice of offering restorative magic as a form of consideration, payment, or contractual fulfillment is strictly regulated under the Autumnwood Accords. It is hereby decreed that any act of healing performed by a mage in exchange for tangible goods, services, or the fulfillment of a legal obligation constitutes a commercial transaction of the arcane. Such transactions are strictly prohibited unless the practitioner holds a valid Licensure of Commercial Restoration issued by the Council. The Guild maintains that healing is a fundamental stabilization of the weave and should not be leveraged as a commodity in the marketplace, particularly when such healing is used to bypass the standard costs of labor or goods.

When a mage incorporates healing magic into a contract—for instance, promising to mend a laborer's wounds in exchange for a portion of their wages—this shall be deemed an unlicensed sale of a protected art. Such contracts are null and void upon the first instance of the healing being enacted. Any mage found to be engaging in such "Healing-for-Service" arrangements shall be subject to immediate investigation by the Aegis Magi. The penalty for such violations shall include a temporary suspension of research privileges and a mandatory period of service in the Hall's maintenance wing. This provision is intended to prevent the exploitation of injured parties and to ensure that the restorative arts are not used to create a secondary economy of magical dependency.

Moreover, the Guild recognizes that "healing" in a legal sense includes the restoration of vitality, the sealing of wounds, and the purging of toxins. Should a mage provide these services as part of a "Goodstyle Artisan" agreement, they must ensure that the specific terms of the healing are clearly delineated in a written addendum, signed by both parties and witnessed by a Guild Clerk. This addendum must specify the limitations of the healing, the duration of the effect, and a waiver stating that the mage is not liable for any complications arising from the patient's pre-existing conditions. See § 200.1 for requirements on general licensure.

body.heading: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
body.text:
A philtre is not consent.

The administration of any substance, liquid, or vapor designed to alter the emotional state, romantic inclinations, or cognitive priorities of a sentient being—hereafter referred to as a "Philtre"—is strictly forbidden under the Accords. The Guild recognizes that the manipulation of the heart is as grave a violation as the manipulation of the mind. A Philtre does not constitute a valid means of obtaining consent for any action, contract, or magical binding. Any agreement entered into under the influence of such a substance is considered legally void and shall be treated as a violation of the Sovereign’s peace. The use of such magic to influence the behavior of a peer, a subordinate, or a member of the public is grounds for immediate expulsion from the Guild.

Any mage found in possession of a Philtre without a specific, approved Research Permit for the study of emotional resonance shall have their belongings seized and their license revoked. This prohibition extends to the "Soft Influence" of magic, where a mage may not use subtle charms to make a target more "receptive" to a proposal. The Accords demand that all interactions between mages and the public be conducted with clarity of mind. If a mage utilizes a Philtre to influence an individual, they shall be held liable for any damages caused by the influenced party, including physical harm, property destruction, or the unauthorized use of the victim's magical signature.

Furthermore, the production and distribution of Philtres are categorized as the Unsanctioned Arts. Any clandestine laboratory found producing such substances will be dismantled by the Aegis Magi, and the occupants will be subject to the Paradox Trial. The Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding the erosion of individual autonomy through arcane chemistry or enchantment. No amount of "research" by the Innovators shall justify the creation of substances that bypass the natural volition of the citizenry. See § 300.2 for the definition of Unsanctioned Arts.

sections.title: Healing Offered as Consideration
sections.brief: Unlicensed healing sold as a contract term.

body.heading: Healing Offered as Consideration
body.text:
§ 500.4 Healing Offered as Consideration. All practitioners of the healing arts, whether licensed by the Autumnwood Accords or otherwise, are strictly prohibited from offering restorative magic as a primary consideration in a commercial, civil, or penal contract.
