The Guild maintains that the restoration of life and the mending of physical integrity are fundamental rights of the sentient being and cannot be commodified as a debt-repayment mechanism or a bargaining chip in the negotiation of services. Any mage who enters into a contract where the provision of healing—whether through potion, incantation, or transmutation—is listed as a specific deliverable in exchange for labor, land, gold, or political favor shall be deemed in violation of the Accords. This prohibition extends to "conditional healing," wherein a victim is granted life-saving treatment on the condition of a subsequent, undisclosed, or disproportionate obligation. Such acts are viewed as predatory and undermine the stability of the Midlands, creating a class of "debt-slaves" whose physical health is leveraged against their personal liberty.

Furthermore, the Aegis Magi are authorized to seize any assets derived from such illicit contracts, and the offending caster shall be subject to the Paradox Trial for the exploitation of vulnerable populations. See § 1.2 for the enacting authority of the Accords Desk. While the Innovators may argue that such exchanges are a matter of personal liberty between consenting adults, the Conservators maintain that the inherent power imbalance of a dying individual precludes true consent, thus rendering any such contract void ab initio. The Guild shall not recognize the validity of any "healing debt" recorded in a ledger or bound by a magical oath. Any mage found to be operating a "healing clinic" that functions as a debt-collection agency shall have their license revoked immediately and may be remanded to a pocket-prison for the duration of the investigation. This law serves to protect the sanctity of the body from the avarice of the arcane.

body.heading: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
body.text:
§ 500.5 Love Philtre and Undue Influence. The administration of any magical substance, enchantment, or ritual intended to alter the emotional state, romantic inclination, or loyalties of a sentient being—commonly referred to as "Love Philtrés"—is strictly prohibited under the Autumnwood Accords. The Guild declares that a philtre is not consent; rather, it is a violation of the cognitive sovereignty of the individual. Any mage who knowingly brews, distributes, or administers such a substance shall be held liable for "Undue Influence," a high offense against the mental integrity of the citizenry. This prohibition is absolute and does not vary based on the perceived "benign" intent of the caster. The use of such magic to bypass the natural process of emotional development or to secure a contract, marriage, or political alliance is considered a fundamental breach of the Accords and may result in the immediate sealing of the caster's magic.

In the event that a victim of a Love Philtre seeks redress, the Accords Desk shall provide a pathway for the restoration of mental autonomy, provided the victim is not currently under the influence of a more complex, multi-layered enchantment. The Aegis Magi are tasked with identifying and neutralizing active "Influence Fields" in public spaces such as taverns or marketplaces. Any mage found in possession of "Love Philtrés" without a specific research permit from Janna Brightspark—and even then, only for the purpose of studying emotional resonance in controlled, isolated environments—shall be subject to the Paradox Trial. The Guild recognizes that the manipulation of the heart is as much a violation of the law as the manipulation of the earth. Those who seek to manufacture affection through the laboratory are to be remembered as transgressors against the very essence of free will. See § 300.2 for related restrictions on the Unsanctioned Arts.

sections.title: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
sections.brief: A philtre is not consent.

body.heading: Love Philtre and Undue Influence
body.text:
Pursuant to the overarching mandates of the Autumnwood Accords and the prevailing doctrine of Mana Reverence, the Guild hereby establishes a definitive legal distinction between the voluntary exchange of affection and the chemical or magical imposition of desire. It is a foundational principle of the Accords that the sanctity of the individual will is paramount to the stability of the magical weave. Consequently, any substance, enchantment, or ritualistic brew designed to induce, amplify, or manufacture romantic attraction—hereafter referred to as a "Philtre"—shall be categorized as a primary instrument of Undue Influence. The Guild maintains that a Philtre is not consent; the presence of a Philtre does not constitute a waiver of the victim's right to self-determination, nor does it grant the caster any legal standing to claim a consensual union, contract, or physical proximity.

Any mage found to be in possession of a Philtre without a verified Research Permit issued by the Innovators, for the sole purpose of pharmacological study, shall be subject to immediate seizure of the materials. If the Philtre is found to have been deployed upon a sentient being, the offense shall be elevated from a regulatory violation to a criminal act of Arcane Assault. The Aegis Magi are authorized to intervene in any instance where a Philtre is suspected of being in active use. In such cases, the victim shall be granted immediate sanctuary, and the perpetrator shall be detained for a formal hearing. The Guild recognizes that the manipulation of the heart is as perilous as the manipulation of the elements; to bypass the internal defenses of a peer through the use of a Philtre is to violate the core tenets of the Accords and the dignity of the magical community.

Furthermore, the use of a Philtre to secure favors, information, or labor shall be treated as a form of magical coercion. Any agreement entered into under the influence of a Philtre is null and void ab initio. This includes, but is not limited to, the signing of apprenticeship contracts, the relinquishing of magical artifacts, or the granting of access to restricted research sites. If a mage attempts to enforce such an agreement, they shall be held liable for all damages caused to the victim and may face severe penalties under the Paradox Trial for the subversion of free will. The Guild shall not recognize the "Right of Pursuit" in any instance where the pursuit is predicated upon the effects of a Philtre.

The Conservators maintain that the production of Philtres borders on the Unsanctioned Arts due to its inherent violation of the natural order of emotion. Conversely, while the Innovators may study the mechanics of such substances, they are strictly prohibited from testing these substances on any sentient being, including those within the Guild's own ranks. Any research involving the "Love Philtre" must be conducted within a sealed laboratory environment, as defined in § 400.2, and must be accompanied by a certified observer from the Aegis Magi. Failure to comply with these restrictions shall result in the immediate revocation of research privileges and a mandatory period of magical sealing. The Guild's stance is absolute: the magic of the heart is a sacred domain, and its violation through artificial means is a breach of the peace that the Autumnwood Accords were designed to uphold.

sections.title: Contracts with Non-Casters
sections.brief: Plain language. Illusion of a signature is not a signature. Illusion of a fee is still a fee.

body.heading: Contracts with Non-Casters
body.text:
The legal standing of a contract entered into by a non-caster—defined herein as any sentient being lacking the innate ability to weave, channel, or manipulate the weave of magic—shall be governed by the principles of plain language and tangible consideration. While the Mages' Guild recognizes the necessity of trade with the lay populace, specifically with the Goodstyle Artisans and other non-magical entities, the Guild maintains that magical obfuscation shall not be used to circumvent the fundamental requirements of a binding agreement. Any contract wherein the intent is obscured by glamours, mental suggestion, or linguistic manipulation shall be rendered null and void at the first instance of discovery by a presiding Arbiter. The Guild holds that a contract must be understood by the signatory in the common tongue; if a mage employs complex arcane terminology to mask a predatory clause, such a contract is deemed a violation of the Accords.

Furthermore, the Guild establishes a strict doctrine regarding the illusion of authority. An illusion of a signature is not a signature. If a mage utilizes a visual glamour to mimic the appearance of a physical mark, or a psychic impression to simulate the act of signing, the resulting document carries no weight in a court of the Accords. The physical act of marking, whether by ink, blood, or seal, must be performed by the conscious will of the non-caster. Conversely, the Guild maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding the illusion of consideration. An illusion of a fee is still a fee. If a non-caster provides a service or asset based on the belief that they are being compensated in a specific currency—even if that currency is a magical construct or a fleeting hallucination—the obligation of the mage to provide the actual, tangible value remains absolute. The Guild shall not permit mages to claim that a "spiritual" or "metaphorical" payment satisfies a material debt. See § 100.2.

In matters of dispute, the Aegis Magi shall oversee the verification of non-caster contracts. If a non-caster claims they were deceived by a "magical" contract, the Guild shall appoint a neutral observer to determine if the language used was intentionally deceptive. Should a mage be found to have used their superior understanding of the arcane to trap a layperson in a labyrinthine legal web, the mage shall be subject to a fine of three hundred gold marks and a mandatory period of community service in the Autumn Wood. This ensures that the Guild remains a pillar of stability rather than a predatory monopoly. All contracts involving the transfer of artifacts or the granting of land rights must be filed with the Clerk of the Accords for verification of plain-language compliance. Any contract that fails this audit shall be flagged as "Unconscionable" and may be struck down by the Sovereign.

body.heading: Familiars as Agents
body.text:
The legal status of a familiar—defined as a non-human entity bound to a caster via a permanent or semi-permanent symbiotic bond—is one of delegated agency. Under the Autumnwood Accords, a familiar is not a legal person but is considered an extension of the caster’s will. Consequently, any action taken by a familiar, whether intentional or incidental, shall be attributed directly to the primary caster. This principle of vicarious casting holds that the caster is responsible for the magical output, physical damage, and social transgressions committed by their familiar. If a familiar strikes a bystander or a rival mage, the caster shall be held liable for all damages as if they had performed the act themselves with their own hands. This is to prevent the common defense of "the beast acted on its own," which the Guild recognizes as a fundamental breach of the responsibility inherent in familiar bonding.

The doctrine of vicarious casting extends to the unauthorized use of magic by a familiar. If a familiar possesses the capacity to channel mana—whether through innate ability or the "leaking" of its master's power—the master is strictly liable for any such discharge. Should a familiar cause a rift, a localized weather event, or any form of environmental degradation, the caster must undergo a formal audit by the Conservators. Failure to restrain a familiar from engaging in unauthorized casting may result in the mandatory severing of the bond or the sequestration of the familiar until the caster can demonstrate improved control measures. The Guild emphasizes that the bond is a tool of the caster, and like any tool, its use must be governed by the caster's discipline. A familiar is never a legal shield; it is a conduit of responsibility.

Furthermore, the Guild recognizes the "Strike by Familiar" clause in matters of physical altercation. In a scheduled Paradox Trial, a familiar may be used as a combatant, but its actions are governed by the same regulations as a summoned construct or a trained familiar. However, in unscheduled disputes, the use of a familiar as a primary aggressor shall be viewed as an escalation of force. If a familiar initiates a physical strike against a non-caster or a peer, the caster shall be deemed to have initiated the conflict. This prevents mages from using their companions as "proxy" aggressors to avoid the repercussions of a direct duel. All familiar training must be documented in the Guild's registry, and any familiar that shows signs of "rogue agency"—the ability to act independently of the master's intent—must be reported to Archmage Theron’s office for evaluation. See § 200.2.

body.heading: Geas as an Unconscionable Term
body.text:
The Guild acknowledges that the Geas—a magical binding of a sentient being to a specific course of action or a prohibition—is a powerful and often dangerous instrument of law and personal agreement. However, the Accords state clearly that a Geas to be reasonable is not a defined term. Because "reasonableness" is subjective and varies wildly between the radical philosophies of the Innovators and the rigid doctrines of the Conservators, the Guild refuses to recognize "reasonableness" as a valid magical constraint in a binding Geas. A Geas that demands a mage act "reasonably" in the face of a threat is legally unenforceable because it lacks a specific, measurable objective. Instead, any Geas placed upon a mage by a third party must be articulated with absolute specificity. A mage may be bound to "not strike a child," but they cannot be bound to "act with wisdom" or "behave justly," as these are moral qualities, not magical parameters.

The Guild views the use of "reasonable" Geases as a method of magical entrapment, often used by the Regal Empire or the Silver Flame to exert influence over Guild members without committing to specific demands. If a mage enters into a contract containing a Geas that relies on vague, subjective descriptors, the Guild shall treat the Geas as "Void for Vagueness." In such instances, the mage is not bound by the Geas, but they may be penalized for the attempted imposition of an unconscionable magical burden. The Aegis Magi are instructed to strike such clauses from any contract presented for filing. If a Geas is found to be unconscionable—meaning it requires the mage to perform an act of self-harm, a violation of the Accords, or a task that is physically impossible—the caster who imposed the Geas shall be subject to immediate investigation for "Arcane Coercion."

To ensure the integrity of the Accords, any Geas involving the manipulation of a non-caster's will must be approved by the Archmage Sovereign. The Guild maintains that while mages may use Geases to ensure the fulfillment of contracts, they cannot use them to override the fundamental rights of the person. A Geas that forces a non-caster to act against their own interests in a way that is not explicitly defined in a plain-language contract is a violation of § 600.1. The Guild seeks to prevent the "Geas-Loop," where a mage is forced to perform a series of "reasonable" actions that lead to a catastrophic outcome. By requiring specificity, the Accords ensure that the power of the Geas remains a tool of clear intent, rather than a weapon of ambiguity. See § 300.2.

body.heading: Construct Labor; Minimum Ward
body.text:
The use of constructs—be they golems, animated armatures, or magically sustained homunculi—as a labor force is permitted under the Autumnwood Accords, provided that the rights of the creator and the safety of the public are maintained. Every construct employed in a commercial or public capacity must be equipped with a Minimum Ward. This ward is a constant, low-level magical signature that serves two purposes: it prevents the construct from acting outside its primary directive and ensures it does not "leak" mana into the surrounding environment. A construct without a Minimum Ward is considered an "Unbound Entity" and is subject to immediate seizure by the Aegis Magi. The ward must be sufficient to prevent the construct from interacting with the weave in a way that could cause localized instability or unauthorized research.

Furthermore, the Guild establishes the principle of "Construct Compensation." While a construct is not a person and thus does not require a wage in the sense of the Goodstyle Artisans, the owner of the construct is responsible for the "Rest" of the construct. This refers to the periodic recharging of the mana core or the ritualistic maintenance of the binding circles. A construct that is worked beyond its capacity, leading to "Mana Burn" or structural collapse, is a violation of Guild safety standards. Owners must provide a documented schedule of maintenance and energy replenishment. If a construct is found to be operating in a state of exhaustion—evidenced by erratic movements or erratic magical discharge—the owner shall be fined for "Negligent Maintenance." This ensures that constructs do not become hazards to the public or the Guild's stability.

In the event of a construct's malfunction, the owner is strictly liable for all damages, regardless of whether the malfunction was "unforeseen." The Guild rejects the defense of "Construct Autonomy" in cases of property damage or bodily harm. If a construct strikes a person, it is treated as a violation of the owner's license, similar to a familiar's actions. Construct labor must also be registered with the Desk; any construct capable of lifting more than five hundred pounds or casting a spell of third-circle magnitude or higher must be granted a "Heavy Labor Permit." This permit requires a monthly inspection by a Conservator to ensure the Minimum Ward remains intact. Constructs used for "Restricted Research" must be held in a designated laboratory, as per § 400.2, and may not be deployed in public spaces without an express waiver from Janna Brightspark's Innovator council.

body.heading: Summoned Notary
body.text:
The Guild recognizes the necessity of high-level verification for contracts involving the transfer of significant arcane assets, the granting of land rights in the Midlands, or the formation of new magical covenants. For such high-stakes transactions, the parties may employ a Summoned Notary—a sentient being from another plane or a high-level spirit summoned specifically to witness and stamp the agreement. However, the use of a Summoned Notary is strictly regulated to prevent "Planar Evasion," where a mage attempts to have a contract validated by a being that does not recognize the laws of the Autumnwood Accords. A Summoned Notary must be capable of understanding the common tongue and must be bound by a "Truth-Binding" oath for the duration of the notarization process.

The requirements for a Summoned Notary are rigorous. The notary must be summoned into a "Neutral Zone," such as a Guild-sanctioned chamber, to ensure that their presence does not cause environmental instability. The notary must provide a "Planar Signature"—a unique magical mark that is distinct from the caster's own magic. This signature must be applied to the document in the presence of a Guild Clerk. If a Summoned Notary vanishes mid-stamp, the contract is considered "Incomplete" and holds no legal weight. The Guild maintains that a vanishing notary is a sign of an unstable summoning or a deliberate attempt to create a legal loophole where the "witness" is no longer present to be held accountable for the truth of the proceedings. In such cases, the parties must restart the notarization process with a new entity.

Furthermore, the Guild prohibits the use of Notaries from the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion, as their legal codes are in direct conflict with the Accords. Any contract notarized by a foreign entity's spirit is considered "Adverse" and will be rejected by the Desk. The Guild also mandates that the summoning of a Notary must be disclosed in the contract itself. If a mage attempts to hide the fact that a supernatural entity was used to witness a deal, the contract is voided, and the mage may face a "Paradox Trial" for unauthorized planar interaction. The goal of these regulations is to ensure that the Guild's records are immutable and that every high-level agreement is witnessed by an entity whose testimony can be verified against the Guild's own standards of truth. See § 100.4.

sections.title: Familiars as Agents
sections.brief: Vicarious casting. Strike by familiar.

body.heading: Familiars as Agents
body.text:
The legal standing of a familiar as an agent of a licensed practitioner is established under the principle of vicarious weaving. Pursuant to the Autumnwood Accords, a familiar is defined as a sentient or semi-sentient entity bound to a master through a formal tether of intent and mana. While the familiar may possess independent locomotion and minor autonomous actions, any magical manifestation originating from the familiar’s essence is legally attributed to the primary caster. This doctrine of vicarious casting ensures that the responsibility for arcane fluctuations, environmental shifts, or unintended collateral damage remains with the primary licensee. If a familiar executes a spell—whether by direct command or by instinctual reaction—the master shall be held liable for any breach of the Accords, regardless of the master's stated intent at the moment of casting.

Furthermore, the doctrine of "Strike by Familiar" governs physical and metaphysical interactions between a familiar and a third party. Should a familiar strike, bite, or otherwise physically assault a non-combatant or a Guild-protected citizen, the master is deemed to have authorized the use of force. The master may not claim "loss of control" as a defense for familiar aggression, as the tether itself constitutes a continuous delegation of agency. To mitigate liability, masters are encouraged to maintain clear behavioral boundaries; however, the legal burden remains heavy. Any familiar that displays persistent hostility toward the public may be subject to immediate seizure by the Aegis Magi for "re-education" or permanent binding. See § 600.1 for the primary definitions of non-caster contracts, as a familiar's actions may occasionally intersect with the rights of those who cannot weave.

Any familiar acting under a direct command to perform a task that results in the destruction of property or the violation of a local ordinance shall be treated as a direct extension of the master's hand. This means that a "rogue" familiar is, in the eyes of the Accords Desk, a malfunctioning tool of the master, much like a malfunctioning wand or a cracked focus. Therefore, the master must ensure that all familiars are properly attuned to the restrictive protocols of the Midlands. Failure to restrain a familiar during a public demonstration or a sanctioned research session shall result in a formal citation and potential suspension of the master's license. The Guild acknowledges that familiars are not mere pets but are arcane proxies; as such, the master is the ultimate guarantor of the familiar's conduct within the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: Geas as an Unconscionable Term
body.text:
A geas, defined as a magical compulsion or a binding oath enforced by arcane weight, is subject to the same standards of equity as any written contract entered into by the Guild's members. Under the Accords, a geas is considered an unconscionable term if it imposes a burden that is fundamentally disproportionate to the consideration provided, or if it seeks to strip the subject of their fundamental agency in a manner that violates the stability of the Midlands. However, the Guild explicitly notes that "a geas to be reasonable" is not a defined term within this Codex. Because the subjective experience of "reasonableness" varies between the traditionalist Conservators and the radical Innovators, the Accords Desk shall not adjudicate based on the internal feelings of the parties involved. Instead, the Desk shall look to the objective impact of the geas on the individual's ability to function as a productive member of society.

If a geas is found to be unconscionable—for instance, requiring a mage to perform acts of self-harm, treason against the Guild, or the deliberate violation of the Forbidden Schools—it shall be deemed voidable at the request of the bound party. The petitioner must present a formal grievance to the Archmage Sovereign, who shall mediate the dispute. If the geas was established without the clear, informed consent of the bound individual, the Accords Desk may move to have the binding magically dissolved by the Aegis Magi. The Guild warns that attempting to bypass these protections by using "subtle" geases—those that do not appear overtly coercive but slowly erode the subject's will—is a grave violation of the Accords and may lead to a Paradox Trial.

The Innovators may argue for a wider latitude in the application of geases for the purpose of research, while the Conservators will insist on the strictest limitations to prevent the creation of "arcane thralls." In the absence of a specific ruling from the Sovereign, the Desk will default to the principle of least restrictive means. A geas that prevents a mage from casting certain spells is generally permissible; a geas that prevents a mage from speaking, eating, or sleeping without cause is likely to be struck down as unconscionable. Any practitioner who knowingly imposes an unconscionable geas upon another may be subject to the penalties outlined in § 300.2. Furthermore, any contract involving a geas must be filed with the Accords Desk to ensure it does not conflict with existing Guild mandates.

body.heading: Construct Labor; Minimum Ward
body.text:
All constructs created for the purpose of labor—including but not limited to golems, clockwork automatons, and animated sculptures—are subject to the regulations regarding artificial sentience and magical maintenance. To ensure the safety of the public and the stability of the local mana field, all constructs utilized in commercial or industrial capacities must be equipped with a Minimum Ward. This ward is a baseline magical seal that prevents the construct from acting with independent malice or exceeding its programmed parameters. A construct lacking a Minimum Ward is considered an "unbound entity" and its operation within the Midlands is strictly prohibited. The Aegis Magi are authorized to dismantle any construct found to be operating without a visible or palpable ward.

The maintenance of a Minimum Ward is the sole responsibility of the construct’s owner or the master who summoned it. This includes the periodic recharging of the ward's essence and the repair of any structural fractures that might allow for "magical leakage." Furthermore, the Accords Desk stipulates that constructs used for heavy labor must be periodically "rested." This does not mean the construct must sleep in a biological sense, but rather that its primary mana-circuitry must be decoupled from its labor-functions for a period of one hour for every eight hours of operation. This prevents the accumulation of "arcane fatigue," which can lead to erratic behavior or spontaneous combustion of the construct's core.

Regarding compensation, a construct is not a person and therefore cannot be "paid" in the legal sense of the Accords. However, the owner of the construct is responsible for the "cost of maintenance," which includes the mana expended to maintain the Minimum Ward and any materials required for repairs. If a construct is hired by a non-caster for a specific task, the non-caster must provide the owner with a "Labor Agreement" as defined in § 600.1. If the construct malfunctions and causes damage, the owner is liable for all costs, provided the construct was properly warded and rested. Failure to provide adequate maintenance or to enforce rest periods shall result in the immediate revocation of the owner's right to operate constructs within the Hall of Autumn Wood.

body.heading: Summoned Notary
body.text:
In instances where a legal agreement must be witnessed or verified by a being of significant arcane standing who is not currently present, the use of a Summoned Notary is permitted. A Summoned Notary is an entity—be it a spirit, a minor elemental, or a displaced consciousness—brought into the physical plane specifically to observe and validate the signing of a contract or the completion of a Guild filing. For such a notary to be recognized by the Accords Desk, it must be bound by a "Temporary Mouth" agreement (see § 200.3) and must possess the requisite level of arcane resonance to ensure the integrity of the seal. The summoning must be performed in a controlled environment, and the notary must remain stationary for the duration of the proceedings.

The form requirements for a Summoned Notary are rigorous. The master performing the summoning must provide a "Script of Intent," detailing exactly what the notary is to witness and the specific magical signature it is required to apply. The notary must be clearly identified in the documentation, including its origin, its duration of presence, and the specific nature of its binding. Once the seal is applied, the notary must be released immediately. Any attempt to hold a Summoned Notary in the Midlands for longer than the duration of the signing is a violation of the Accords and may be prosecuted as unauthorized summoning. The notary's signature must be distinct from the master's own signature to ensure a clear chain of custody for the document.

A unique and problematic scenario arises in the event of a "Vanishing Notary"—a situation where a summoned entity disappears mid-stamp or before the seal is fully set. If a Summoned Notary vanishes before the document is finalized, the document is considered null and void. The master is then required to re-summon a notary and re-execute the entire filing process. In cases where the notary's disappearance causes physical damage or magical instability, the master shall be held liable for the "interruption of proceedings" and may face a fine. The Accords Desk will not accept any document where the seal is partial, smudged, or incomplete due to the notary's departure. Practitioners are advised to ensure their summoning circles are stable and their binding words are clear to prevent such logistical failures.

sections.title: Geas as an Unconscionable Term
sections.brief: A geas to be reasonable is not a defined term.

body.heading: Geas as an Unconscionable Term
body.text:
Pursuant to the overarching mandates of the Autumnwood Accords, all contracts involving the imposition of a geas—a magically binding oath or compulsion—must be reviewed for the presence of unconscionable terms. While the Guild recognizes the necessity of binding agreements to ensure the fulfillment of arcane duties, the imposition of a geas that serves to strip a caster of their fundamental agency or physical safety is strictly prohibited. Under the jurisdiction of the Accords Desk, a geas is deemed unconscionable if it requires the subject to perform an act of self-harm, commit a felony against a non-consenting party, or surrender their primary magical essence as collateral for a debt of negligible value. Any contract containing such clauses shall be rendered null and void by the Archmage Sovereign upon notice. See § 100.5.

Furthermore, it is explicitly stated within this Codex that a geas to be reasonable is not a defined term. The Guild refuses to provide a subjective metric for "reasonableness," as the interpretation of such a standard varies wildly between the traditionalist doctrine of the Conservators and the experimental methodologies of the Innovators. Therefore, the burden of proof lies with the petitioner. If a party seeks to strike a geas from a contract on the grounds of it being "unreasonable," they must provide specific evidence of physical impossibility, extreme magical exhaustion, or a direct violation of the forbidden schools as defined in § 300.2. The Guild shall not adjudicate based on the personal feelings of the bound party, but rather on the objective violation of the Accord's safety protocols.

In instances where a geas has already been enacted and is found to be unconscionable, the Aegis Magi may be deployed to facilitate a supervised dissolution. The cost of such a dissolution shall be borne entirely by the party who originally imposed the geas. No party shall attempt to bypass a geas through unauthorized ritualistic interference; such actions are considered a breach of the Accords and may result in a Paradox Trial. See § 1.2. Any contract involving the "Goodstyle Artisans" shall be treated with standard scrutiny, but shall be granted a rebuttable presumption of fairness provided the geas does not involve the permanent surrender of a Heartstone or similar rift-adjacent artifact.

body.heading: Construct Labor; Minimum Ward
body.text:
The utilization of constructs as laborers within the Midlands and surrounding territories is permitted, provided that the entity is clearly distinguished from sentient magical beings. To maintain the sanctity of the Guild’s standing, all constructs employed for industrial, domestic, or logistical purposes must be equipped with a Minimum Ward. This ward serves as a magical signature, ensuring that the construct remains a tool of the employer and cannot be hijacked by rogue casters or influenced by external telepathic pressures. A construct lacking a Minimum Ward is considered "wild" and may be dismantled by any Aegis Mage found in the vicinity without fear of civil liability. See § 200.6.

Regarding the compensation of constructs, the Accords Desk maintains that while a construct is not a "person" under the law, its primary battery or mana-source must be maintained at a standard of "adequate rest." This is defined as a period of non-active operation sufficient to prevent mana-drain fatigue, which can lead to erratic behavior or catastrophic discharge. An employer who fails to provide the requisite rest for a construct is liable for any damages caused by the construct's malfunction. While a construct is not "paid" in the sense of currency—as the Wario Coin is not a recognized tender of the Guild—the employer is required to provide a dedicated mana-conduit or a stable recharge station. Failure to do so constitutes a violation of labor safety standards and may result in a fine levied against the employer’s research permit.

Any construct performing high-risk labor, such as the transportation of volatile reagents or the construction of restricted research facilities, must be overseen by a licensed caster. The presence of a construct does not exempt a human caster from the responsibilities of § 400.1. If a construct is damaged during the performance of its duties, the owner is responsible for the repairs, provided the damage was not caused by the construct's deliberate defiance of its Minimum Ward. Conversely, if a construct is seized by a rival faction such as the Iron Legion, the Guild will not intervene unless the construct is carrying a state-sanctioned relic or a restricted research copy. See § 300.5.

body.heading: Summoned Notary
body.text:
The use of summoned entities to serve as notaries for the authentication of magical contracts is permitted, provided the entity is bound by a "Stability Clause" of no less than three lunar cycles. A summoned notary must be of a sufficiently intelligent species to comprehend the nuances of the Autumnwood Accords. Before the seal is applied, the notary must be presented with a clear, verbal recitation of the contract's primary terms to ensure the entity is not acting under a hallucination or a magical glamour. This procedure ensures that the signatures of all parties—be they human, elf, or other sentient races—are recognized by the Guild’s archives. See § 100.6.

A significant legal complication arises in the event of a "vanishing notary." If a summoned notary vanishes mid-stamp or disappears before the seal is fully set, the contract is considered "Incomplete and Voidable." The Guild does not recognize the authority of a half-formed seal. In such cases, the parties involved must return to the Accords Desk to re-verify the terms and summon a new notary. If the vanishing was caused by a breach of the contract by one of the signatories—such as a sudden surge of hostile magic—the offending party may be subject to a Paradox Trial. See § 1.2.

Furthermore, no notary may be summoned from the Quiet List, nor may a notary be used to certify any transaction involving the trade of forbidden schools. The Guild maintains a strict prohibition on the use of "ghost-notaries" or spirits of the deceased without a direct decree from Archmage Veyra. If a notary is summoned and subsequently becomes hostile, the caster who summoned said notary is held strictly liable for any magical fallout. The Guild provides no protection for casters who attempt to use "convenience summons" to bypass the standard verification processes of the Desk. All notaries must be registered in the temporary log of the presiding Clerk for the duration of the signing ceremony. See § 100.4.

sections.title: Construct Labor; Minimum Ward
sections.brief: Wards, rest, who is paid.

body.heading: Construct Labor; Minimum Ward
body.text:
All constructs, regardless of their method of manufacture—be they woven from clay and sigil, forged of iron and steam, or birthed from the ethereal essence of the Weave—are subject to the labor protections of the Autumnwood Accords. It is the decree of the Accords that no construct shall be utilized for the purpose of manual labor, transport, or administrative duties without a Minimum Ward of protection. This Ward serves as a legal and metaphysical tether, ensuring that the construct remains bound to its designated purpose and does not suffer from "arcane drift," a phenomenon wherein a construct’s lack of a soul-anchor causes it to develop erratic, self-directed behaviors that may endanger the surrounding population or the integrity of the Guild’s property. A construct operating without such a Ward is considered a rogue entity and may be dismantled by any Aegis Mage on sight without prior notice of intent.

Furthermore, the Accords dictate the specific requirements for the maintenance of these constructs. Every construct engaged in labor for a Guild-affiliated entity or a licensed private caster must be granted a period of "Restorative Stasis" at the conclusion of every lunar cycle. During this period, the construct is to be deactivated and its internal mana-conduits allowed to cool or replenish. Failure to provide adequate Restorative Stasis constitutes a violation of the Labor Stability Act. If a construct is forced to labor through its designated rest period, the owner of said construct shall be liable for double the standard labor tax, and the construct shall be subject to a mandatory recalibration by the Conservators.

The payment of wages for constructs is a matter of bureaucratic record but not of spiritual necessity. While a construct does not possess a personal bank account or the capacity for greed, the "payment" it receives is accounted for as a maintenance stipend. This stipend is to be held in a trust by the employer and used exclusively for the repair of the construct’s physical shell, the recharging of its primary core, and the renewal of its Minimum Ward. Any diversion of these funds for personal gain by the employer is a felony under the Accords. See § 600.1 for matters regarding contracts with non-casters. See § 200.6 for the specific limitations on constructs that hold a quill.

body.heading: Summoned Notary
body.text:
The authentication of high-level arcane contracts often necessitates the presence of a Summoned Notary, a specialized entity of neutral legal standing capable of witnessing the binding of complex oaths. These notaries are typically summoned from the Neutral Planes or designated pocket-dimensions to ensure that the signatures of the involved parties are untainted by terrestrial bias. To be valid under the Autumnwood Accords, a Summoned Notary must be presented with a valid Writ of Summoning, issued by a Guild Clerk or an appointed mediator such as Archmage Veyra. The notary must be capable of speaking the common tongue and the primary arcane dialect of the region in which the contract is to be executed.

The form requirements for a Summoned Notary are stringent to prevent the forging of legal intent. A notary must present a Seal of Verity, which is a magically-reactive stamp that changes color or shape based on the truthfulness of the statements being recorded. All contracts witnessed by a Summoned Notary must be written on vellum of a specific weight and treated with a non-reactive anti-magic wash to ensure that the notary’s seal does not degrade or become obscured by ambient mana. If a notary fails to present a Seal of Verity, or if the Seal is found to be a mere physical imitation, the contract is null and void, and the parties involved may be subject to a Paradox Trial for attempted fraud.

A unique and perilous legal complication arises in the event of a Notary’s Vanishing. Because summoned entities are bound by the laws of their own planes as much as the Accords, a notary who vanishes mid-stamp creates a "Limping Oath." If a notary disappears while the seal is being pressed into the wax or the parchment, the legal status of the contract enters a state of flux. In such instances, the contract is considered "Unsealed" and carries no weight until a secondary notary of equal rank can be summoned to perform a "Completion of Intent." If a notary vanishes and the parties involved flee the scene, the contract is declared a Breach of Presence, and the parties may be pursued by the Aegis Magi. Any notary who vanishes mid-stamp due to a lack of sufficient mana-binding on the part of the caster shall be held liable for the costs of the secondary summoning. See § 100.2 for limitations on who may speak for the Guild.

sections.title: Summoned Notary
sections.brief: Form requirements. A summoned notary who vanishes mid-stamp.

body.heading: Summoned Notary
body.text:
Pursuant to the overarching mandates of the Autumnwood Accords, all legal instruments, contracts, and metaphysical bindings executed within the jurisdiction of the Midlands shall be subject to verification by a recognized notary of the Guild. In instances where a physical notary cannot be produced due to geographical isolation, hostile territory, or the immediate expiration of a temporal window, a Summoned Notary may be invoked. This procedure requires a formal petition to the local Aegis Magi oversight, ensuring that the entity being summoned possesses the requisite magical aptitude to perceive the true nature of the ink and the weight of the intent. The petitioner shall be responsible for providing the necessary mana-conduits to sustain the notary’s presence for the duration of the signing. Furthermore, the petitioner must guarantee that the summoned notary is not a construct of the Iron Mandate, as the Accords do not recognize the legality of Imperial seals within our sovereign halls.

The form requirements for a Summoned Notary are strictly delineated to prevent the subversion of the Guild's authority. Every invocation must be accompanied by a Writ of Intent, clearly stating the parties involved, the nature of the agreement, and the specific magical signatures to be verified. The notary must be bound by a temporary geas, ensuring they remain neutral and objective throughout the proceedings. This geas shall be nullified immediately upon the completion of the final seal, at which point the notary is to be returned to their point of origin or dissolved into the ether, as per the standard dissolution clauses. No Summoned Notary shall be permitted to witness the drafting of the contract; their role is strictly limited to the verification and stamping of the completed document. Failure to provide a Writ of Intent shall result in the immediate forfeiture of the summoning fee and a potential citation for unauthorized arcane conjuration.

A critical exception exists regarding the phenomenon of the Vanishing Notary. Should a Summoned Notary vanish mid-stamp—defined as the moment the notary's physical or ethereal form ceases to exist while the seal is partially applied—the resulting document shall be deemed "Null and Voidable" under § 600.1. The petitioner is required to report such an occurrence to the nearest Aegis Magi station within one lunar cycle. The Guild shall then determine if the vanishing was a result of external interference, a failure of the petitioner's mana-conduits, or a breach of the notary’s own internal stability. If the vanishing is deemed an act of external sabotage by the Silver Flame or the Cosmic Jesters, the petitioner may be granted a waiver on the summoning fee. However, if the notary vanished due to the petitioner's inability to maintain the summoning circle, a fine shall be levied to cover the cost of the wasted arcane energy.

In cases where a vanished stamp leaves a lingering magical residue that threatens the stability of the surrounding area, the petitioner shall be held liable for any subsequent remediation costs. This is particularly relevant when dealing with high-level bindings that involve the restricted research permitted under the Innovator faction's oversight. See § 400.1 for the requirements regarding research permits and the limitations on high-energy signatures. Furthermore, any Summoned Notary who is found to have intentionally vanished to evade a contract they deemed "unconscionable" shall be struck from the Guild’s registry of recognized entities. Such entities will be placed on the Quiet List, and any mage who knowingly summons a known "Vanishing Notary" shall be subject to a Paradox Trial for negligence or collusion with rogue elements. All disputes regarding the validity of a mid-stamp disappearance shall be mediated by Archmage Veyra’s appointed tribunal.

sections.title: Evidence Generally
sections.brief: What a filing must contain.

body.heading: Evidence Generally
body.text:
§ 700.1 Evidence Generally — What a filing must contain.

All evidentiary submissions presented before the High Court of Autumnwood or any sub-committee of the Accords Desk shall be deemed null and void unless they conform strictly to the standards of clarity, provenance, and magical integrity established herein. A filing is not merely a statement of fact but a formal anchoring of reality within the Guild’s legal framework. To ensure that the truth of a proceeding is not distorted by the very nature of the arcane, every piece of evidence—be it a written scroll, a physical artifact, a recorded memory, or a summoned testimony—must be accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity signed by a licensed Clerk or a recognized Aegis Mage. This certificate must verify that the evidence has not been subjected to unauthorized alteration, transmutation, or temporal shifting since its initial collection.

The filing must contain a comprehensive description of the evidence’s origin, including the geographic coordinates of its discovery, the date of its acquisition, and the identities of all individuals involved in its handling. In cases involving items of significant magical potency, such as those involving the Heartstone or other rift-adjacent materials, the filing must also include a detailed survey of the item’s current mana signature to prevent the accidental triggering of environmental hazards during the hearing. Furthermore, any evidence that is inherently volatile, ephemeral, or capable of self-replication must be housed in a stabilized containment vessel as approved by the Conservators. Failure to provide a sufficient description of the evidence's nature shall result in the immediate dismissal of the filing and a potential citation for negligence under the oversight of Archmage Veyra.

Furthermore, the filing must explicitly state any known associations with the Quiet List. While the contents of the Quiet List are not to be recited in public venues, any evidence derived from such sources must be flagged for restricted viewing. The Clerk shall ensure that such evidence is only accessible to the presiding judges and the immediate parties involved, under a seal of non-disclosure. Any attempt to circumvent these restrictions or to present "hidden" evidence in a public forum shall be treated as a violation of the Accords. The Accords Desk reserves the right to reject any filing that utilizes "Wario Coin" as a form of collateral or tender, as such currency holds no recognized value within the Guild's legal system. For matters regarding the specific requirements of physical artifacts, see § 400.4. For matters regarding the handling of unauthorized research materials, see § 400.1.

body.heading: Scrying of Closed Books
body.text:
§ 700.2 Scrying of Closed Books — Warrant. Spoliation even if nothing was taken.

The sanctity of a private library or a closed grimoire is a cornerstone of the Autumnwood Accords, yet the Guild acknowledges that the pursuit of stability may necessitate the inspection of restricted materials. No mage, regardless of their standing among the Innovators or the Conservators, shall engage in the unauthorized scrying, mental probing, or ethereal peering into a closed book or a sealed repository. Such actions are strictly prohibited unless the individual possesses a valid Writ of Inspection issued by the Sovereign Archmage or a designated Aegis Magistrate. This writ must specify the scope of the scrying, the duration of the access, and the specific reasons for the inquiry. Any scrying conducted without such a warrant shall be deemed a criminal trespass of the mind and a violation of the privacy protections afforded to all registered mages.

Crucially, the Accords establish a strict doctrine of spoliation regarding the act of scrying. The mere act of peering into a closed book via arcane means constitutes a "metaphysical breach" of the object's integrity. Even if the scrying process is successful and no physical pages are removed, no secrets are stolen, and no ink is blurred, the act itself is sufficient to constitute spoliation. The Guild holds that the "observation of the arcane" is often an "alteration of the arcane"; therefore, a book that has been scried is no longer in its original state. In any legal proceeding where a book has been subjected to unauthorized scrying, the contents of that book may be ruled inadmissible as evidence, as its reliability can no longer be guaranteed by the Conservators.

The penalty for such spoliation shall be determined by the presiding council, but it shall typically involve a formal reprimand and a temporary suspension of the offender's research privileges. If the scrying was performed on a volume containing Quiet List materials, the penalties shall be significantly escalated, potentially leading to a Paradox Trial. Mages who find their libraries subjected to such unauthorized scrying are entitled to seek restitution for the "spiritual wear" caused to their collections. For procedures regarding the issuance of Writs of Inspection, see § 400.1. For the consequences of severe magical breaches, see § 300.1.

body.heading: Memory Charm as Spoliation
body.text:
§ 700.3 Memory Charm as Spoliation — Forgetting is not a defense if you paid for the forgetting.

In the pursuit of justice, the Guild recognizes that the human—and demi-human—mind is a fragile vessel, easily manipulated by the very arts it seeks to master. However, the use of memory charms, amnesia spells, or any form of cognitive erasure to avoid the consequences of a legal proceeding is strictly forbidden. Under the Accords, a mage who undergoes a memory erasure to "purge" their knowledge of a crime or a breach of contract does not receive a legal reprieve. The law shall look past the veil of the missing memory to the actions that necessitated the erasure. If it can be demonstrated that a mage purposefully induced a state of forgetting to evade testimony or to shield themselves from the repercussions of their actions, the court shall treat the erasure as a deliberate act of spoliation of evidence.

The legal principle of "Constructive Knowledge" shall apply in these instances. If a mage was aware of a violation at the time of the act, the fact that they no longer possess that memory is irrelevant to their liability. Furthermore, the Guild explicitly prohibits the use of memory charms as a method of "cleansing" one's record. A mage who pays a third party, or utilizes their own magic, to forget a specific event shall be held to the same standard of accountability as if the memory were perfectly intact. The Guild maintains that "forgetting is not a defense," particularly when the act of forgetting is a calculated maneuver to obstruct the truth. Any mage found to have utilized such charms to obstruct a Paradox Trial shall face immediate escalation of their sentencing.

Furthermore, the use of memory charms on witnesses or victims is considered a severe felony under the Accords. Such actions shall result in the immediate sealing of the offender's magic and a mandatory period of isolation. The Accords Desk shall not recognize any plea of ignorance based on self-induced amnesia. If a mage claims they cannot testify because they have "purged" the event, the court may compel them to provide evidence of the charm's usage, which shall serve as prima facie evidence of guilt or obstruction. For matters concerning the sealing of magic, see § 300.1. For the management of restricted research that might involve cognitive manipulation, see § 400.1.

body.heading: Simulacrum Testimony
body.text:
§ 700.4 Simulacrum Testimony — A copy may not swear for the original.

The integrity of the High Court relies upon the presence of the living, sentient being before whom the oath is sworn. Consequently, the use of a simulacrum, illusion, or any magically-constructed duplicate to provide testimony in a legal proceeding is strictly prohibited. A simulacrum, by its very nature as a "copy," lacks the inherent soul-binding or consciousness required to enter into a binding legal oath. While a simulacrum may be used to demonstrate a visual reconstruction of a past event—provided it is clearly labeled as a "Visual Reconstruction" and not "Testimony"—it may never be permitted to speak on behalf of the original entity or to provide subjective accounts of events.

Any attempt to present a simulacrum as a valid witness shall be met with an immediate stay of proceedings and a formal investigation into the authenticity of the claimant's actions. The law distinguishes clearly between a "Visual Reconstruction," which is a tool of education and evidence, and "Simulacrum Testimony," which is a fraudulent attempt to bypass the requirements of the Accords. If a mage seeks to provide a visual reconstruction of a crime scene or a historical event, they must obtain a permit from the Conservators to ensure the reconstruction does not contain unauthorized magical effects or "hallucinations" that could mislead the court. The original entity must be present to oversee the reconstruction and must be available to answer clarifying questions in real-time.

Should a party attempt to substitute a simulacrum for an absent witness, the court may rule that the party is in "Contempt of the Accords." In such cases, the evidence provided by the simulacrum shall be struck from the record, and the party may be subject to a Paradox Trial for attempting to subvert the judicial process. This rule ensures that the "human element"—the weight of personal responsibility—remains at the center of the Guild's legal framework. For matters regarding the use of constructs in legal settings, see § 600.4. For the definition of forbidden schools that might involve the creation of sentient duplicates, see § 300.2.

body.heading: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
body.text:
§ 700.5 Clone as Duplicate Claimant — One claim. The later body files an amendment.

In instances where a mage has undergone the process of cloning—whether for research, labor, or survival—the legal status of the resulting bodies must be clearly defined to prevent the "Multiplicity of Claims" paradox. Under the Autumnwood Accords, a single magical signature or "Identity Essence" may only hold one primary legal standing at any given time. If a mage possesses multiple bodies through cloning, they are considered a single legal person with multiple physical manifestations. Therefore, only one body may act as the primary claimant in a legal suit, hold property, or enter into contracts. The "Original" body is typically designated as the primary claimant by default, unless a formal "Transfer of Primacy" is filed with the Accords Desk.

If a mage wishes to pursue a legal claim using a secondary body, they must first file a "Notice of Intent to Claim" with the Clerk. Once the intent is filed, the secondary body may act as the representative for the legal proceedings. However, should a dispute arise between the bodies regarding the direction of the claim, the Accords dictate that the primary body's wishes shall prevail. If the primary body is incapacitated or destroyed, the secondary body must file a "Petition for Amendment of Primacy" to become the sole legal claimant. This ensures that the Guild's records remain clean and that no single mage can use their clones to "double-file" claims or circumvent the limits of the Paradox Trial.

Furthermore, any property or assets acquired by a clone during a period of "Secondary Status" are considered the property of the primary identity. Should a clone be destroyed, the assets do not revert to the public but remain with the primary body. This prevents the "fragmentation of wealth" that often plagues the Innovators' more radical experiments with biological and magical replication. Any mage who attempts to file a claim with a clone without first filing the required amendment or notice shall have their claim dismissed as a "Duplicate Filing." For matters regarding the use of clones as labor, see § 600.4. For the overarching rules on research permits involving such replication, see § 400.1.

sections.title: Scrying of Closed Books
sections.brief: Warrant. Spoliation even if nothing was taken.

body.heading: Scrying of Closed Books
body.text:
The act of scrying, whether through a crystal lens, a scrying pool, or a direct mental projection, into a volume that has been formally sealed by the Archmage Sovereign or the presiding High Conservator is strictly prohibited under the Autumnwood Accords. A closed book is not merely a physical object of bound paper and ink; it is a legal state of existence wherein the information contained therein has been sequestered from the public and private spheres for reasons of stability, security, or the preservation of the Quiet List. Any attempt to bypass these seals via divination, ethereal peering, or any other arcane method of observation constitutes a breach of the sanctity of the Archive. Such actions are treated as a prima facie violation of the privacy of the Guild's internal records and the personal property rights of the authors.

To initiate a legal inquiry into a closed volume, a caster must first obtain a formal Warrant of Inspection from the Accords Desk. This warrant must specify the exact nature of the information sought, the necessity of the inquiry for the preservation of the Guild or the safety of the Midlands, and the specific limitations of the scrying duration. Without a warrant, any scrying of a closed book shall be met with immediate seizure of the scrying apparatus and a mandatory period of magical silence for the offending caster. The mere intent to observe is sufficient for prosecution, as the volatile nature of forbidden knowledge means that even a glance can cause irreparable ripples in the local weave.

Furthermore, the law of Spoliation applies to all scrying attempts regardless of the outcome. If a caster successfully scries into a closed book without a warrant, the contents of that book are deemed "spoliated" in the eyes of the Accords. This means that even if the caster takes no physical notes, reveals no secrets to third parties, and admits no knowledge of the contents, the integrity of the text is considered compromised. The Guild shall treat the book as if its contents were leaked, and the original author or the presiding Conservator may demand that the volume be moved to a more secure, high-containment vault. The caster shall be liable for the costs of re-sealing and the administrative fees associated with the relocation of the text. See § 700.1.

body.heading: Memory Charm as Spoliation
body.text:
The use of memory charms, cognitive erasure, or any mnemonic suppression spell intended to remove knowledge of a Guild-related offense or a restricted research violation is strictly prohibited as a method of evading justice. The Accords Desk holds the firm position that "forgetting is not a defense if you paid for the forgetting." If a caster utilizes a charm to erase their own memory of a crime, or if they employ a charm on a witness to suppress their testimony, the act of erasure is itself considered a secondary offense of Spoliation. The law recognizes that the voluntary removal of a memory creates a void in the legal record that can be exploited to obstruct the Paradox Trial. Therefore, the existence of a memory charm is sufficient evidence of a desire to obstruct, regardless of whether the caster can currently recall the specific details of the act.

In any proceeding before a council of peers, the presence of a memory charm—whether active or recently expired—shall be treated as a confession of the underlying act. If a caster is found to have sought out a memory charm to "cleanse" their mind of a specific event, the Guild shall presume that the event occurred as described in the initial accusation. The caster shall not be permitted to argue a lack of intent or a lack of memory as a mitigating factor; rather, the proactive seeking of oblivion shall be viewed as an admission of guilt. This prevents the "clean slate" defense where a rogue mage might attempt to render themselves legally incapable of understanding their own crimes.

Furthermore, any caster who provides a memory charm to a third party for the purpose of concealing evidence or silencing a victim shall be subject to immediate arrest by the Aegis Magi. Such actions are viewed as a direct assault on the transparency of the Accords. The Guild maintains that the truth of the past is a communal responsibility, and the artificial deletion of that truth to protect an individual's reputation or freedom is a violation of the collective security of the Midlands. See § 700.1.

body.heading: Simulacrum Testimony
body.text:
A simulacrum, whether it be a physical construct of flesh and bone, a magical duplicate, or a lingering psychic echo, may not swear testimony or provide evidence in any formal hearing before the Accords Desk. The law of Identity requires that only a sentient being of recognized legal standing—specifically a living mage, a non-magical citizen of the Midlands, or a sanctioned Goodstyle Artisan—may participate in the testimony of a Paradox Trial. A copy may not swear for the original, as the nature of magic allows for the creation of perfect mimics that lack the moral weight and soul-binding oaths required by the Guild's judicial processes.

If a party to a legal dispute seeks to present the testimony of a simulacrum, they must first prove that the original entity is deceased and that the simulacrum is a "Living Record" of the original's intent, which is a standard rarely granted. Even in such cases, the simulacrum may only be used to provide historical context and cannot be used to swear an oath or provide "new" testimony. The use of a simulacrum to testify as if it were the original person is strictly forbidden and shall be considered a form of identity theft and a violation of the Sanctity of the Self. Any attempt to do so will result in the immediate dismissal of the evidence and a heavy fine against the presenting party.

The Accords Desk further stipulates that a simulacrum may not be used to bypass the "Quiet List" restrictions. If a simulacrum were allowed to speak, it could potentially recite forbidden knowledge without the caster facing the direct consequences of such a violation. Therefore, any simulacrum that speaks during a legal proceeding must be bound by a permanent silence ward unless specifically authorized by Archmage Veyra. The preservation of the distinction between the "Original" and the "Copy" is fundamental to the prevention of magical fraud within the Guild's jurisdiction.

body.heading: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
body.text:
In matters of property, intellectual research, or magical rights, a clone shall be considered a Duplicate Claimant rather than a separate legal entity. Under the Autumnwood Accords, the existence of a clone does not grant the secondary body a separate right to claim ownership, nor does it allow for the doubling of resources. One claim is permitted per original identity. If a mage creates a clone to claim a share of a research grant or a portion of a physical estate, the Guild shall recognize only the primary body as the legal owner. The clone is viewed as an extension of the original's reach, not a new person.

Should a situation arise where a clone is granted its own Provisional Guild Pass or seeks to establish independent research permits, the Guild shall treat this as a violation of the Unsanctioned Arts. The clone is legally tethered to the original. If the original body is incapacitated, the clone may act as a temporary proxy, but it cannot hold property in its own name. In cases where a clone attempts to file for independent status, the Guild shall require a "Severance of Identity" hearing, which is notoriously difficult to achieve and requires the express permission of the Conservators.

In the event of a dispute between a primary body and its clone regarding the use of shared resources—such as a laboratory or a specific mana source—the primary body shall always hold the dominant legal right. The later body, or the clone, must file an amendment to the original's charter to request specific hours of usage. This ensures that the creation of clones cannot be used as a tactic to dilute the authority of a single mage or to circumvent the limits on research copies of Quiet Items. The law is clear: the soul (or the primary arcane signature) owns the claim; the body is merely the vessel. See § 400.5.

sections.title: Memory Charm as Spoliation
sections.brief: Forgetting is not a defense if you paid for the forgetting.

body.heading: Memory Charm as Spoliation
body.text:
The Guild hereby establishes that the intentional erasure of cognitive data via magical means does not constitute a valid defense against the withholding of evidence, nor does it grant the practitioner immunity from the consequences of their prior actions. Under the Autumnwood Accords, a mage who undergoes a Memory Charm to obfuscate their knowledge of a transgression is deemed to have committed an act of Spoliation. The legal principle of "Cognitive Integrity" dictates that the burden of memory remains with the individual regardless of the method by which that memory is suppressed. If a mage is summoned to provide testimony or evidence regarding a breach of the Accords and claims ignorance due to a self-inflicted Memory Charm, such a claim shall be dismissed by the presiding council.

Furthermore, the Guild recognizes that the act of paying for, commissioning, or self-administering a Memory Charm constitutes a willful attempt to subvert the judicial process. In all proceedings, the court shall treat the existence of a Memory Charm as a prima facie admission of guilt regarding the underlying matter being suppressed. The mere fact of forgetting is not a shield; rather, the methodology of forgetting serves as a confession of the existence of the fact. Practitioners who seek to utilize such charms to evade the Paradox Trial shall find their magic subject to immediate Sealment under the authority of the Conservators. Any individual found to have induced a state of amnesia to avoid the disclosure of illicit research or unauthorized field casting shall be prosecuted as if the original information were still held in clear and present mind.

See § 700.1 for general evidence standards. See § 700.2 regarding the limitations of scrying. The Guild maintains that the preservation of the truth is paramount to the stability of the Midlands. Any attempt to treat a blank mind as a clean slate in the eyes of the law is a violation of the sanctity of the Accords. The cost of the charm, whether paid in gold, mana, or personal sacrifice, is irrelevant to the determination of spoliation. The law focuses on the result: the deliberate removal of evidence from the sphere of human consciousness to hinder the Guild's ability to maintain order.

body.heading: Simulacrum Testimony
body.text:
A simulacrum, whether created through high-level illusion, somatic projection, or complex material transmutation, lacks the legal standing to provide sworn testimony or enter into binding contracts on behalf of its progenitor. The Guild recognizes that while a simulacrum may possess the appearance, voice, and perceived personality of a specific mage, it lacks the "Arcane Signature of Intent" required for legal recognition. Therefore, a copy may not swear for the original. Any attempt to utilize a simulacrum to bypass the requirements of the Paradox Trial or to provide false testimony in a dispute of the Accords shall be treated as a felony of Deceptive Casting.

When a mage is summoned to appear before the High Council or an Aegis Magi tribunal, they must present their own physical form. The use of a simulacrum as a proxy is strictly prohibited, as the Guild cannot verify the internal state of a magical construct. If a simulacrum is presented in place of a mage, the proceedings shall be suspended, and the mage in question shall be subject to a summary citation for evasion. This rule ensures that the nuances of the mage's conscience and the weight of their personal oaths are properly weighed by the peers of the Guild. A copy is a reflection of a truth, not the truth itself; it cannot bear the weight of a vow, nor can it be held liable for the consequences of its words.

Furthermore, any contract signed by a simulacrum is null and void ab initio. If a mage seeks to conduct business with the Goodstyle Artisans or other entities, they must ensure that their own hand—not a magical duplicate—affixes the seal. Failure to adhere to this requirement may result in the immediate revocation of research permits under § 400.1. The Guild's stance is clear: the law governs the soul and the intent of the caster, neither of which can be replicated by the mere mastery of form. For those who believe their simulacrums are sufficiently "real" to stand in court, the Guild reminds them that the Accords are bound by the essence of the individual, not the shadow they cast.

body.heading: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
body.text:
In instances where a mage undergoes biological or magical replication resulting in the creation of a clone, the Guild recognizes a singular legal identity for the purpose of claims, debts, and privileges. The doctrine of "Unitary Essence" dictates that while two bodies may exist, only one legal entity may hold the primary standing. The first body to register with the Accords shall be recognized as the Primary Claimant. Any subsequent body produced via cloning shall be designated as a Duplicate Claimant. The Duplicate Claimant possesses no independent rights to Guild assets, research privileges, or the right to vote within the factions of the Conservators or Innovators.

To resolve conflicts of interest between a Primary and a Duplicate Claimant, the law requires that the later body files a formal amendment to the original registration. This amendment must explicitly state the intended role of the Duplicate Claimant—whether it be as a servant, a research vessel, or a secondary laborer—and must be approved by the presiding Archmage. If a Duplicate Claimant attempts to assert independent ownership of a laboratory, a research permit, or a position within the Guild, such claims shall be summarily struck down. The law does not recognize the "right of replication" as a right of "multiplication" of legal status. One mage, regardless of the number of physical vessels they may inhabit, may only hold one seat of power or one license of practice.

Should a dispute arise regarding the distribution of resources between a Primary and a Duplicate Claimant, the Guild shall default to the Primary Claimant's rights unless a prior written agreement, notarized by a Summoned Notary under § 600.5, states otherwise. The Duplicate Claimant may be utilized for the purposes of research or field work, provided that the Primary Claimant remains the sole bearer of legal responsibility for any violations of the Accords. Any attempt to split the ownership of a licensed artifact or a restricted research copy between two bodies shall be viewed as an unauthorized division of the Guild's interests. The Accords are designed to prevent the dilution of responsibility; therefore, the clone must follow the lead of the original, and the law shall treat them as a single thread in the tapestry of the Midlands.

sections.title: Simulacrum Testimony
sections.brief: A copy may not swear for the original.

body.heading: Simulacrum Testimony
body.text:
A copy may not swear for the original. Any entity produced via the method of arcane duplication, illusion, or somatic mirroring—collectively referred to as a "Simulacrum"—is strictly prohibited from providing testimony, depositions, or sworn statements before a tribunal of the Autumnwood Accords. The legal fiction of the Guild maintains that a Simulacrum possesses the likeness and, in some instances, the memories of the progenitor, yet it lacks the metaphysical "weight" required to bind a soul to a truth. Consequently, any statement extracted from a Simulacrum is deemed inadmissible as primary evidence. This restriction applies regardless of the degree of fidelity achieved by the caster. Even if a Simulacrum is indistinguishable from the original to the naked eye, or if it possesses the ability to replicate the vocal nuances and mannerisms of the source, it remains a mere echo. Under the Accords, only a living, sentient body of the original caster may be held accountable for the truth of their actions.

Furthermore, the use of a Simulacrum to obstruct justice by providing a "false" testimony that mirrors a "true" one is considered a grave offense. If a party seeks to utilize a Simulacrum for the purpose of information retrieval, they must first petition the Aegis Magi for a Research Permit to ensure the process does not violate the sanctity of the original's cognitive privacy. See § 400.1. Any attempt to bypass these restrictions by weaving complex "truth-binding" spells onto a duplicate shall be viewed as an attempt to circumvent the inherent limitations of the Accords and may result in a Paradox Trial. The Guild recognizes that while a copy may hold data, it cannot hold the "burden of conscience." Therefore, any legal proceeding involving a Simulacrum shall require the physical presence of the original caster to verify the authenticity of the information provided. Failure to produce the original caster for verification shall result in the immediate dismissal of the testimony and a formal warning against the use of unauthorized arcane proxies.

In cases where the original caster is deceased, a Simulacrum may be used solely for the purpose of "archival visualization" to assist the tribunal in understanding the context of past events, provided that such visualization is not presented as evidence of fact. The Clerk of the Accords shall ensure that all such visualizations are clearly marked as "Non-Testimonial Visualizations" in the court record. Any party found to be attempting to pass off a Simulacrum’s speech as the original's sworn word shall be subject to immediate sanctions, including potential sealing of their casting abilities. This law serves to protect the integrity of the Accords against the manipulation of reality by those who would seek to manufacture witnesses from the ether. See § 700.2.

body.heading: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
body.text:
One claim. The later body files an amendment. In the event that a single magical consciousness inhabits multiple biological vessels—specifically through the process of cloning or somatic splitting—the Guild recognizes the "Doctrine of Primacy." This doctrine dictates that the first viable body to manifest or exist in a state of independent consciousness shall be the primary claimant for all legal, financial, and contractual obligations. The Guild does not recognize the existence of "multiple" citizens when the underlying magical signature is identical. Therefore, should a mage or artisan create a clone, the clone is viewed as a legal extension of the original, rather than a separate entity capable of independent litigation or contract formation. This prevents the "doubling" of assets or the "dilution" of liability within the Midlands.

When a second body is produced, it is considered a "Subordinate Vessel." If the Subordinate Vessel seeks to engage in independent commerce, property ownership, or the signing of Accords, it must first file a Formal Amendment of Status with the Accords Desk. This amendment requires the Primary Claimant to explicitly delegate specific rights to the Subordinate Vessel. Without such a filing, any contract signed by the clone is legally voidable at the whim of the Primary Claimant, as the Guild views the clone as a mere tool or "construct" of the original's will. This mirrors the protections found in § 600.4 regarding construct labor, as the Guild refuses to grant full personhood to bodies that are manufactured by the intent of another. The Primary Claimant retains all core rights, including the right to the original's Guild license and the responsibility for any debts incurred by the Subordinate Vessel.

If a dispute arises between two bodies of the same consciousness regarding the ownership of a specific artifact or land, the Guild shall default to the Primary Claimant's claim unless a prior "Splitting of Essence" decree has been filed. Such a decree is a rare and difficult-to-obtain legal maneuver, requiring a high-level mediation by Archmage Veyra herself. In the absence of such a decree, the "later body" is legally subordinate. Any attempt by a clone to file a separate claim of ownership without the Primary Claimant's signature shall be treated as an unauthorized expansion of magical influence and may be subject to a Paradox Trial. This ensures that the radical Innovators cannot use cloning to circumvent the limitations of the Accords or to multiply their influence within the Autumn Wood. See § 200.1.

sections.title: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
sections.brief: One claim. The later body files an amendment.

body.heading: Clone as Duplicate Claimant
body.text:
