In the event that a legal claimant presents a physical duplicate of their person—whether through the use of high-fidelity transmutation, sophisticated illusionary weaving, or the biological replication of cellular matter—the Guild shall recognize only the primary biological entity as the rightful holder of any and all legal claims, properties, or titles. The existence of a secondary body does not constitute a secondary right of ownership, nor does it grant the duplicate the standing to act as a joint tenant or a co-claimant in any matter before the Accords. Any attempt to utilize a duplicate body to circumvent debt, evade the Paradox Trial, or assert multiple interests in a single asset shall be deemed an act ofarcane fraud and a violation of the foundational principles of the Autumnwood Accords.

The Guild’s stance on replication is predicated on the principle of singular identity. When a mage or a layperson produces a clone, that clone is viewed by the Accords as an extension of the original's will, not as an independent legal persona. Consequently, if a claimant possesses a duplicate, the Guild shall treat all actions taken by the duplicate as if they were taken by the primary body. If the duplicate is used to acquire property, that property belongs to the primary; if the duplicate is used to incur debt, the primary is liable. This prevents the "doubling" of rights which would otherwise destabilize the economic and social fabric of the Midlands.

Should a legal dispute arise involving both the primary body and a duplicate, the Guild shall permit the later-manifested body to file a formal amendment to the primary's status. This amendment may be used to define the specific operational boundaries of the duplicate—for instance, designating it as a "Laborer Entity" or a "Research Proxy"—but it cannot be used to sever the link of ownership. The filing of such an amendment serves to clarify the intent of the primary claimant and to ensure that the Guild’s records reflect the intended use of the replication. Failure to file an amendment within three lunar cycles of the duplicate’s manifestation shall result in the Guild assuming a default "Proxy Status," wherein the duplicate is granted no rights beyond those of a common construct, as defined in § 600.4.

Furthermore, any attempt to claim that a duplicate is a separate legal "person" for the purpose of splitting a single inheritance or a single license shall be summarily dismissed. The Guild acknowledges the complexities of replication, yet it maintains that a soul—or the arcane signature associated with a legal identity—cannot be partitioned without a specific, high-level decree from Archmage Veyra. See § 700.1 for general evidence requirements regarding identity. Any mage found attempting to use a duplicate to bypass the restrictions of § 200.1 or to manufacture "new" claimants for the purpose of illicit trade shall be subject to immediate referral for a Paradox Trial. The Aegis Magi are authorized to seize all assets of a duplicate that are not explicitly bonded to the primary body in a filed amendment.

sections.title: Discipline; Range of Sanctions
sections.brief: From fee to seal to pocket-prison. Paradox Trial named.

body.heading: Discipline; Range of Sanctions
body.text:
The disciplinary framework of the Autumnwood Accords is predicated upon the principle of proportional restoration, wherein the severity of the sanction shall be directly correlated to the magnitude of the arcane transgression and the potential risk posed to the stability of the Midlands. All punitive measures are overseen by the Accords Desk, with the Archmage Sovereign maintaining final appellate authority. For minor infractions, such as the unauthorized use of common cantrips in residential zones or the failure to register a minor familiar, the Guild shall levy a standard administrative fee. These fees are non-negotiable and are to be paid in recognized currency; notably, the Wario Coin is strictly prohibited as a medium of tender for any Guild transaction, per the standing prohibitions on non-standardized currency.

For more significant violations, specifically those involving the reckless manipulation of mana or the infringement upon the privacy of other mages, the Guild may impose a Seal of Silence or a magical Seal of Binding. A Seal of Binding is a permanent or semi-permanent restriction placed upon a practitioner’s ability to channel the weave, effectively neutralizing their threat to the public and the Guild's interests. The application of such a Seal requires a formal finding of negligence or malice by a tribunal of the Aegis Magi. In cases where a mage’s actions threaten the very fabric of reality—such as the creation of a rift or the unauthorized growth of a Titan—the sanction shall escalate to the ultimate punitive measure: the Pocket-Prison.

The Pocket-Prison serves as a localized, extra-dimensional incarceration designed to isolate dangerous individuals from the material plane indefinitely. Entry into the Pocket-Prison is the final recourse of the Accords, reserved for those whose presence in the Midlands constitutes an existential risk. All disciplinary actions, regardless of scale, are recorded in the central registry to ensure that the history of the Accords remains transparent to the Conservators and the Innovators alike. See § 1.6 for definitions of "Transgression" and "Arcane Magnitude." See § 800.1 for the naming of the Paradox Trial as the primary judicial mechanism for these sanctions.

body.heading: Paradox Trial Procedure
body.text:
The Paradox Trial is the official judicial mechanism of the Autumnwood Accords, designed to adjudicate complex disputes and criminal charges through a system of peer review. It is mandated that all high-level disputes involving the use of restricted magic, the violation of the Quiet List, or the breach of the Unsanctioned Arts be brought before a council of peers. These peers shall be selected from a pool of qualified mages who are not directly involved in the litigation, ensuring a semblance of impartiality between the traditionalist Conservators and the radical Innovators. The trial shall be conducted in a designated neutral hall within the Autumn Wood, where the Aegis Magi are tasked with maintaining the integrity of the magical perimeter.

During the Paradox Trial, all evidence must be presented in a structured format, and every testimony shall be recorded by a Summoned Notary to ensure a permanent legal record. The proceedings may involve the demonstration of magical theory, the presentation of seized artifacts, or the recitation of historical precedents. The objective of the trial is to determine the truth of the violation and to assign the appropriate sanction as outlined in § 800.1. The council shall deliberate in private, and their verdict shall be binding upon all signatories of the Accords.

Strict prohibition is placed upon the conduct of unscheduled street duels. While the Guild recognizes the historical prevalence of magical combat, the Accords decree that no duel shall be considered a legal method of dispute resolution unless it has been formally scheduled, registered, and sanctioned by the Accords Desk. Any mage who engages in an unscheduled duel in a public space shall be subject to immediate arrest by the Aegis Magi and shall be liable for the costs of the intervention. Only through the formal Paradox Trial may a mage seek to vindicate their honor or reclaim stolen property. See § 700.1 for evidence standards.

body.heading: Seal of Silence; Duration and Review
body.text:
The Seal of Silence is a specific disciplinary measure employed when a mage’s speech—whether spoken, telepathic, or inscribed—poses a risk to the stability of the magical order or involves the unauthorized dissemination of information regarding the Quiet List. Upon the imposition of the Seal, the affected individual is rendered incapable of producing any linguistic output that can be perceived by others. The duration of this Seal is determined by the presiding council during the Paradox Trial, based on the severity of the breach. A standard Seal of Silence for minor informational leaks shall last for a period of no less than one lunar cycle and no more than three years, depending on the frequency of the offender's previous infractions.

While a Seal of Silence is active, the individual may still engage in non-verbal activities, such as the study of theory or the maintenance of mundane tasks, provided these actions do not involve the manipulation of the weave in a manner that could be interpreted as coded communication. The Seal is not a total removal of agency but a targeted restriction on the medium of speech. The Accords Desk shall monitor the effectiveness of the Seal to ensure it does not cause unintended physiological harm to the caster, as the preservation of the caster's health is a secondary priority to the preservation of the Guild's secrets.

A mage under the Seal of Silence may petition for a review of their sentence after the passage of one-half of the designated duration. Such a petition must be submitted in writing, using a pre-approved method of non-verbal transcription, and must be presented to the Archmage Sovereign for mediation. The review shall consider the mage's conduct during the period of silence, their cooperation with the Aegis Magi, and the current threat level posed by the information they were originally seeking to disseminate. If the petition is granted, the Seal may be lifted, shortened, or modified. If the petition is denied, the remaining duration of the Seal shall stand. See § 300.3 for Quiet List Procedure.

body.heading: Duel Stakes Converted to Fees
body.text:
In instances where a mage insists upon a formal Trial by Arcane Duel as the primary method of adjudication—specifically when the legal merits of a case are deemed too nuanced for a standard peer review—the Accords Desk shall intervene to ensure the preservation of public safety and the Guild's resources. While the Guild acknowledges the cultural significance of the duel, it shall not permit the destruction of infrastructure or the collateral damage inherent in high-level magical combat. Therefore, the Accords Desk shall mandate that the "stakes" of the duel be converted into administrative fees and restorative penalties.

The conversion process requires the parties to agree upon a pre-determined valuation of the dispute. For example, if a mage seeks to reclaim a stolen artifact, the "win" condition of the duel shall be the legal transfer of the item, while the "loss" condition shall be the payment of a substantial fine to the Guild’s treasury. The Aegis Magi shall oversee the duel, and should either participant exceed the permitted output of mana or target non-combatants, the duel shall be immediately terminated. The losing party shall be held liable for the full cost of the Aegis Magi's intervention, as well as a punitive surcharge for the unsanctioned escalation of magical force.

This conversion of stakes ensures that the Paradox Trial remains the primary judicial framework while still allowing for the resolution of disputes through active magical demonstration. The Accords Desk shall maintain a schedule of these converted duels, ensuring that they occur in designated "duel-pits" where the magical fallout can be safely dissipated. No duel shall be permitted to proceed if the projected cost of the collateral damage exceeds the valuation of the stakes. This policy serves to prevent the "scorched earth" tactics often favored by the Innovator faction in their pursuit of radical results. See § 800.2 for Paradox Trial Procedure.

body.heading: Pocket-Prison Procedure
body.text:
The Pocket-Prison is the ultimate site of incarceration for those deemed too dangerous to remain within the Midlands or those whose magic has become fundamentally erratic. The procedure for commitment to a Pocket-Prison is strictly regulated to prevent the arbitrary disappearance of Guild members. A mage may only be committed to a Pocket-Prison following a final verdict of the Paradox Trial, where the council determines that sealing the mage's magic (as per § 800.1) is insufficient to protect the public. The commitment must be signed off by both the Archmage Sovereign and the head of the Conservators, ensuring that the decision is made with the full weight of the Guild's authority.

The "key" to a Pocket-Prison is not a physical object but a complex, multi-layered arcane lock maintained by the Aegis Magi. Only the Archmage Sovereign and the designated High Conservator may authorize the opening of a cell. The prison itself is a pocket dimension, isolated from the flow of standard time and the reach of external scrying. This isolation is necessary to prevent the "leakage" of dangerous magic into the surrounding environment. Once a mage is committed, their presence is struck from the active census of the Midlands, though their records remain accessible to the Accords Desk for historical and legal purposes.

Regarding the conditions of confinement, the Accords are silent on the specifics of daily life within the Pocket-Prison, as these are considered internal security matters. However, it is a common misconception among the populace that "visiting hours" exist for those incarcerated in a Pocket-Prison. The Accords Desk officially denies the existence of such a practice, as the very nature of the pocket dimension precludes safe external access. Any attempt to scry into the Pocket-Prison or to bypass the Aegis Magi's wards to reach an inmate shall be treated as a high-level felony, punishable by immediate and permanent Seal of Binding. See § 400.2 for details on Pocket Dimensions as Labs.

sections.title: Paradox Trial Procedure
sections.brief: Peers, record, no street duel unless scheduled.

body.heading: Paradox Trial Procedure
body.text:
The Paradox Trial shall serve as the primary judicial mechanism for the resolution of high-level arcane disputes and the adjudication of severe violations of the Autumnwood Accords. Per § 800.1, all trials must be overseen by a council of peers, defined as mages of equivalent or greater established rank who possess no direct familial or commercial ties to the accused or the complainant. The presence of these peers ensures that the delicate balance between the Conservator and Innovator philosophies is maintained, preventing any single faction from weaponizing the judiciary to achieve absolute hegemony over the Midlands. The primary objective of the Paradox Trial is the preservation of the Weave and the safety of the citizenry; consequently, the council shall prioritize the containment of volatile magic over the immediate satisfaction of personal grievances.

All proceedings of the Paradox Trial shall be entered into the permanent record of the Accords Desk. Each testimony, magical manifestation, and evidentiary artifact presented during the trial must be transcribed by a bonded Notary or a construct authorized under § 600.5. These records are to be kept in a secure, magically-warded archive, accessible only to the Archmage Sovereign and the presiding Council. The records serve not only as a historical ledger but as a binding precedent for future adjudications. Any mage found to have willfully falsified a trial record or attempted to redact testimony shall be subject to immediate sentencing under the maximum severity tier of § 800.1.

Furthermore, the Paradox Trial expressly prohibits the conduct of street duels as a means of settling legal disputes. While the history of magic is replete with spontaneous arcane combat, the Accords Decree that all such conflicts must be moved into a formal, magically-regulated environment. If a complainant and a defendant insist upon a Trial by Arcane Duel, it must be scheduled with at least forty-eight hours of notice to the Aegis Magi for the purpose of establishing a neutral arena and safety wards. Any mage who initiates an unscheduled duel in a public space or within the bounds of the Autumn Wood shall be deemed to have forfeited their right to a fair trial and shall be subject to summary detention. See § 800.1 for the range of sanctions applicable to such violations.

body.heading: Seal of Silence; Duration and Review
body.text:
The Seal of Silence is a restorative and punitive measure utilized primarily when a caster has engaged in the unauthorized recitation of the Quiet List or has engaged in speech that threatens the stability of local mana-currents. Upon the imposition of the Seal, the subject’s vocal apparatus shall be magically locked, preventing any audible speech, including the casting of verbal components. The duration of this Seal is determined by the presiding Council based on the severity of the infraction as outlined in § 300.3. For minor infractions, such as the accidental utterance of a restricted name in a tavern, the Seal may be set for a period of no less than one lunar cycle. For grave violations, including the deliberate dissemination of forbidden knowledge, the Seal may be rendered permanent, subject only to a formal petition for review.

A mage under the Seal of Silence is not exempt from the basic rights of the Accords, yet they are strictly prohibited from using any form of telepathic communication to circumvent the vocal restriction. Any attempt to bypass the Seal via external magical means shall be viewed as an act of defiance against the Accords Desk and may result in the extension of the current Seal or a transition to a more severe penal status. The Seal is intended to provide a period of reflection and to "cool" the magical residue of the offender’s intent. During this time, the mage may still be required to perform manual labor or study non-verbal theory, provided such activities do not involve the manipulation of the Weave in a way that could trigger a resonance with the Seal.

Review of the Seal of Silence shall occur at the conclusion of each designated period. The mage may submit a written petition, transcribed by a designated proxy or through a pre-arranged series of non-verbal signs, requesting a reduction in the Seal’s duration. The Council shall review the mage’s conduct during the period of silence; if the mage has demonstrated a marked decrease in erratic magical behavior and has complied with all other Guild mandates, the Seal may be lifted or shortened. If the mage has shown signs of escalating magical instability or has attempted to subvert the Seal, the Council shall maintain the current duration or increase it accordingly. See § 200.4 for procedures regarding the lapse of such magical effects.

body.heading: Duel Stakes Converted to Fees
body.text:
In instances where a dispute cannot be settled through standard arbitration and the parties involved insist upon a Trial by Arcane Duel, the Accords Desk shall intervene to ensure the fiscal and structural integrity of the Guild. While the duel serves as the mechanism for determining guilt or innocence, it is not a mechanism for the private transfer of wealth or the destruction of assets. All stakes agreed upon by the combatants—whether they be gold, land, magical artifacts, or services—shall be automatically converted into administrative fees payable to the Accords Desk. This conversion is mandatory and shall be calculated based on the estimated cost of the magical wards, the Aegis Magi presence, and the logistical overhead required to host the duel.

The conversion of stakes ensures that the Guild is not burdened by the costs of policing private magical violence. Should the combatants agree to a stake of one thousand gold, the Accords Desk shall seize that amount and apply it toward the maintenance of the Autumn Wood facilities. If the stake involves a tangible asset, such as a deed to a workshop or a rare reagent, the Desk shall assess a fair market value and levy a corresponding fee. The winning party shall receive their judicial victory—the legal recognition of their claim—but they shall not receive the physical stake or the converted gold. The purpose of this provision is to strip the profit motive from the act of magical combat, ensuring that mages do not engage in duels for mercenary gain.

Any attempt to circumvent this fee conversion by entering into "side-agreements" with outside parties, such as the Regal Empire or the Goodstyle Artisans, shall be considered a violation of the Accords. If a mage is found to be using a duel as a pretext for a private transaction, the duel shall be declared void, and both parties shall be subject to immediate investigation. The Aegis Magi are authorized to seize any assets involved in such a fraudulent arrangement. Mages who find this provision burdensome are encouraged to seek mediation through the Archmage Sovereign to avoid the high costs associated with formal duels. See § 800.2 for the procedures regarding the scheduling of such duels.

body.heading: Pocket-Prison Procedure
body.text:
The Pocket-Prison is a specialized containment facility utilized for mages whose magic has become fundamentally volatile or whose crimes against the Accords necessitate total isolation from the physical plane. Unlike a standard detention cell, a Pocket-Prison is a self-contained pocket dimension, isolated from the primary Weave to prevent the prisoner from drawing upon external mana or affecting the world outside. The keys to these dimensions are held exclusively by the High Conservators, and access to the prison is strictly regulated by the Accords Desk. No mage may enter a Pocket-Prison without a direct mandate from Archmage Veyra or a unanimous vote from the Council of Peers.

The procedure for incarceration involves the "Sealing of the Threshold," where the prisoner is cast into the dimension and the entrance is collapsed, leaving only a singular, magically-locked point of entry. Once the threshold is closed, the prisoner is effectively removed from the timeline of the Midlands. The maintenance of the Pocket-Prison requires a constant, low-level expenditure of mana from the Guild’s central reserves, making it a costly and significant undertaking. Consequently, incarceration is reserved for the most dangerous offenders or those whose magic poses a systemic risk to the Autumnwood Accords. The prisoner is provided with a basic existence—sustenance and environment—but these are to be sufficient only for survival, not for comfort.

Regarding the status of visiting hours, the Accords Desk maintains a policy of absolute secrecy. While rumors persist among the lower-tier mages that certain high-profile prisoners may receive visitors, the official stance of the Guild is that no such visits are permitted. Any attempt to establish a communication link with a prisoner in a Pocket-Prison is a felony under the Accords and may result in the immediate sentencing of the visitor to a similar confinement. The isolation of the prisoner is a matter of public safety; any breach of this isolation, whether through physical entry or magical scrying, is to be met with the highest tier of sanction. See § 400.2 for regulations regarding the use of pocket dimensions for authorized research purposes.

sections.title: Seal of Silence; Duration and Review
sections.brief: How long a mouth stays quiet.

body.heading: Seal of Silence; Duration and Review
body.text:
Any mage found in violation of the Accords who is sentenced to a Seal of Silence by the presiding council of the Paradox Trial shall be subject to the temporal constraints set forth in this section. The Seal of Silence is not merely a prohibition on vocalization but a metaphysical dampening of the subject’s ability to transmit intentional information through any conventional or arcane medium. The initial duration of the Seal shall be determined by the severity of the breach; minor infractions regarding the unauthorized recitation of the Quiet List shall result in a standard period of three lunar cycles. For violations involving the dissemination of restricted research or the breach of the Iron Mandate’s boundaries, the Sovereign may extend this duration indefinitely, subject to a biennial review by the Conservators.

The duration of the Seal is strictly governed by the principle of Arcane Stability. If a mage is found to be experiencing significant magical degradation or "mana-fraying" as a result of the Seal, a petition for early release may be filed with the Desk. However, such a petition must be accompanied by a certified report from a Master of the Conservator faction confirming that the mage’s silence no longer poses a risk to the public safety of the Midlands. The Desk shall not grant a review until the initial term has passed at least fifty percent of its allotted duration. During the review period, the mage shall remain under the jurisdiction of the Aegis Magi and may be relocated to a designated holding cell within the Autumn Wood.

Furthermore, the Seal of Silence is not a total erasure of identity. While the subject may not speak, they are permitted to communicate via written notation, provided such notation does not contain forbidden schools of magic or references to the Quiet List. Any attempt to bypass the Seal using unauthorized innovative techniques shall be viewed as a secondary offense, punishable by a doubling of the remaining sentence. The Desk maintains the right to revoke the Seal prematurely should the Sovereign determine that the mage’s silence is being leveraged as a tool for political coercion or if the mage is required to provide testimony in a high-priority matter of Guild security. See § 800.2 for the standard procedure regarding the initiation of the Seal.

body.heading: Duel Stakes Converted to Fees
body.text:
In the event that a mage elects to resolve a dispute through a formal Paradox Trial by Arcane Duel rather than accepting a standard sanction, the Accords mandate that the administrative costs of the proceedings remain the responsibility of the participants. While the outcome of a duel may determine the victor’s rights over a disputed artifact, land, or magical property, the Guild Desk shall not waive the requisite filing fees, logistical surcharges, or the mandatory "Aegis Oversight Levy." These fees are non-negotiable and are assessed regardless of whether the duel ends in a decisive victory, a magical stalemate, or a mutual exhaustion of resources.

The Desk shall convert all declared stakes of a duel into a standardized Guild Fee structure upon the filing of the Duel Request. If a mage seeks to wager a specific sum of gold or a physical asset, the Guild shall calculate the equivalent market value at the time of filing. This value shall be added to the base administrative fee. Should the duel result in the destruction of public property or the unintended alteration of the local environment—such as the unauthorized growth of titan-class flora or the opening of minor rifts—the participants shall be held jointly liable for the restoration costs. These restoration costs are billed as "Emergency Stabilization Fees" and are due immediately upon the conclusion of the duel.

It is strictly prohibited for a mage to attempt to "waive" the Guild's fees by offering the Desk a portion of the duel's spoils as a gesture of goodwill. The Accords are clear: the Guild is an administrative body, not a beneficiary of private litigation. The Desk shall not accept Wario Coins, nor shall it accept any tender that is not recognized as official Guild currency. Any attempt to settle a duel's administrative debt through illicit trade or the offering of "favors" shall result in an immediate stay of the duel and a secondary investigation into the parties' conduct. See § 800.2 for the primary procedure on Duel Stakes.

body.heading: Pocket-Prison Procedure
body.text:
The utilization of pocket dimensions as a means of incarceration for mages sentenced during a Paradox Trial is governed by the principle of Spatial Integrity. The key to the pocket-prison—whether it be a localized fold in reality or a fully realized sub-dimension—is held exclusively by the Archmage Sovereign or their designated deputy within the Conservator faction. No mage, regardless of rank or seniority, shall have the authority to grant entry, exit, or unauthorized communication to a prisoner held within a pocket-prison. This measure is intended to ensure that the punishment remains absolute and that the prisoner cannot use their remaining influence to subvert the Accords from within a vacuum.

Regarding the status of visiting hours, the Guild Desk officially maintains that such a concept is a matter of rumor and lacks any codified legal standing within the Autumnwood Accords. There is no scheduled time for family, peers, or legal counsel to enter the pocket-prison. Any attempt to organize a "visitation" shall be treated as a breach of the prison's spatial seal and will be met with immediate disciplinary action against the petitioner. The only permissible interaction with a prisoner is the formal delivery of sustenance and the occasional reading of the Guild’s daily decrees, conducted by an authorized Aegis Mage under strict supervision.

The maintenance of the pocket-prison is the responsibility of the Innovators, provided they operate under the direct oversight of the Conservators to ensure the dimension does not suffer from "entropy-leak" or "spatial erosion." If a pocket-prison is found to be unstable, the Desk may authorize a transfer of the prisoner to a physical holding cell, though this is a matter of safety rather than a grant of parole. Prisoners held in pocket-prisons are considered "temporally isolated" and are exempt from standard public appearance requirements, but they remain bound by the laws of the Accords. See § 400.2 for the regulations regarding the use of pocket dimensions as laboratories and their distinction from penal facilities.

sections.title: Duel Stakes Converted to Fees
sections.brief: If they insist on a duel, the Desk still invoices.

body.heading: Duel Stakes Converted to Fees
body.text:
In the event that a practitioner of the arcane elects to settle a legal dispute, a breach of contract, or a violation of the Autumnwood Accords through the mechanism of a formal Arcane Duel rather than a standard adjudicative hearing, the Desk shall maintain its right to assess all standard administrative costs. It is a common misconception among the more martial elements of the Aegis Magi and the radical elements of the Innovator faction that the physical or metaphysical destruction of an opponent’s magical capacity exempts the victor from the bureaucratic oversight of the Guild. To the contrary, the Desk views the conversion of a duel into a resolution as a mere alternative method of evidence processing. Therefore, regardless of whether the outcome is decided by a clash of wills or a decree of the Sovereign, the victor shall be held liable for the full extent of the filing fees associated with the initial grievance.

Furthermore, any "stakes" declared by the combatants—be they the forfeiture of a specific artifact, the surrender of a research permit, or the renunciation of a specific school of study—do not supersede the Guild's right to invoice for the logistical burden of the Paradox Trial. The Desk shall not be intimidated by the volatility of a duel; the fact that a mage may be reduced to a state of magical exhaustion or permanent sealing does not diminish the fact that the Guild provided the venue, the peer oversight, and the regulatory framework for said engagement. All such costs shall be added to the victor's outstanding balance, and the loser shall be responsible for the costs of their own containment or rehabilitation, as dictated by the prevailing sanctions. See § 800.2 for the overarching procedures of the Paradox Trial.

The Desk explicitly rejects the notion that "blood for blood" or "mana for mana" constitutes a waiver of administrative fees. If a mage chooses to engage in a duel to avoid a fine, the fine remains due, and the duel costs shall be added as a secondary surcharge. The Accords are a matter of civil and magical order, not a theater for unregulated violence. Any attempt to use a duel as a means to circumvent the fiscal responsibilities of a Guild member shall be met with an immediate escalation of fees and a potential referral to the Conservators for a review of the individual’s fitness to hold a license. The Desk is a repository of law, not a spectator to theater; every spark of magic spent in the name of justice must be accounted for in the ledger of the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: Pocket-Prison Procedure
body.text:
When a judgment rendered by the Paradox Trial necessitates the removal of a rogue mage from the public sphere, the Guild shall utilize a pocket-prison as the primary means of containment. The administration of such a facility is strictly governed by the protocols of the Conservators to ensure that the spatial integrity of the Midlands remains uncompromised. The "key" to such a prison is not a physical object but a cryptographic arcane sequence held exclusively by the Archmage Sovereign or their designated deputy within the Aegis Magi. No individual mage, regardless of rank or factional standing, shall be granted the authority to initiate an entry or exit sequence without a direct writ from the Desk. The purpose of the pocket-prison is isolation, not rehabilitation; it is designed to negate the subject's ability to exert influence over the physical world or to facilitate the unauthorized propagation of forbidden schools.

Regarding the matter of visiting hours, the Desk formally declares that any reports of scheduled social calls, visitation windows, or "dialogue sessions" with incarcerated mages are entirely unsubstantiated rumors. The pocket-prison is a vacuum of social interaction designed to prevent the subversion of the Accords through clandestine communication. While the Innovators may argue for the necessity of "re-education" through dialogue, the Conservators maintain that the risk of a breach—either physical or ideological—outweighs the benefits of such interaction. Consequently, any mage found attempting to establish a communication link with a prisoner, whether through scrying, familiar proxy, or authorized teleportation, shall be subject to immediate sanctions under § 800.1.

The maintenance of the pocket-prison is funded by the seized assets of the condemned. The Desk shall not provide public tours, nor shall it provide transcripts of any internal communications that may occur within the void. The prisoner exists in a state of suspended legal personhood, their rights suspended until such time as the Archmage Sovereign deems a re-evaluation of their status necessary. Any unauthorized attempt to "liberate" a prisoner, whether through heroic intervention or clandestine infiltration, will be treated as an act of high treason against the Autumnwood Accords. The sanctity of the prison is the sanctity of the law itself; if the walls of the pocket-prison can be breached, the stability of the Midlands is forfeit. See § 800.2 for the primary sentencing guidelines leading to incarceration.

sections.title: Pocket-Prison Procedure
sections.brief: Who holds the key. Visiting hours are a rumor.

body.heading: § 800.5 Pocket-Prison Procedure
body.text:
The administration of extra-planar incarceration, colloquially referenced as the Pocket-Prison, shall be governed by the sovereign authority of the Archmage Sovereign as mediated by the High Council of the Autumnwood Accords. Any mage found in violation of the Accords who is sentenced to such a confinement by the Paradox Trial shall be subject to immediate transition into a localized, magically-sustained pocket dimension. This dimension is to be constructed such that its internal geometry is disconnected from the primary ley lines of the Midlands, ensuring that any uncontrolled magical discharge or temporal leakage does not affect the stability of the Autumn Wood or the surrounding territories. The purpose of this procedure is not merely punitive but serves as a containment measure for high-risk arcane anomalies and rogue casters whose presence poses a systemic threat to the Guild’s structural integrity.

The custody of the "Key"—defined herein as the specific arcane sequence and focal point required to initiate entry into or exit from the pocket dimension—shall reside exclusively with the Aegis Magi assigned to the Custodial Oversight Division. No individual mage, regardless of rank or factional affiliation, may possess the Key or the means to bypass the dimensional threshold without a direct, written mandate from Archmage Veyra. This strict prohibition is intended to prevent the unauthorized liberation of high-risk individuals or the clandestine entry of non-authorized personnel into the prison. Any attempt to manufacture a secondary Key, or to utilize forbidden schools of magic to breach the dimensional veil, shall be classified as an act of High Treason against the Autumnwood Accords, punishable by immediate permanent sealing of the offender’s arcane essence.

Regarding the maintenance of the prisoner, the Guild recognizes that biological and cognitive degradation may occur over extended periods of isolation. However, the provision of "Visiting Hours" is officially categorized as a rumor and is not recognized by the Accords as a legal right or a standard procedure. The Guild maintains that the psychological state of the prisoner is secondary to the safety of the public and the preservation of the magical equilibrium. While the Conservators may occasionally argue for the periodic auditing of prisoner health to ensure the continued viability of the "Seal and Seal" policy, the Innovators frequently advocate for more sophisticated, albeit experimental, stimuli to prevent cognitive collapse. Regardless of these internal debates, no communication between the prisoner and the exterior world shall be permitted unless such communication is deemed essential for the extraction of specific, non-hazardous information required for the defense of the Guild.

All records pertaining to the location, dimensions, and occupant list of the Pocket-Prison are classified as Restricted and shall not be entered into any public catalogue. Any mage who attempts to disclose the coordinates or the existence of a specific prisoner shall be subject to the Quiet List Procedure as outlined in § 300.3. Furthermore, the use of any One-T cartography to locate the prison is strictly prohibited, as such maps are intended for navigation and do not serve as licenses for exploration or raid. The Pocket-Prison shall remain a closed system; any unauthorized breach, whether by an internal agent or an external hostile force such as the Iron Legion or the Silver Flame, shall be met with a full-scale Aegis response to ensure the integrity of the Guild’s penal infrastructure.

sections.title: Duty to File Before Casting
sections.brief: If value, composition, or risk will move, file first.

body.heading: Duty to File Before Casting
body.text:
The preservation of the weave and the stability of the Midlands require that all significant alterations to reality, whether intentional or incidental, be documented by the Accords Desk prior to the initiation of the somatic or verbal components of the spell. Under the authority of the Archmage Sovereign, all practitioners of the arts are hereby commanded to submit a formal Notice of Intent to Cast (NIC) whenever the intended enchantment, transmutation, or evocation is likely to result in a measurable shift in material value, a fundamental change in chemical or metaphysical composition, or a demonstrable increase in environmental risk. This duty is not merely a bureaucratic formality; it is a preventative measure designed to ensure that the Aegis Magi can monitor for potential paradoxes or violations of the forbidden schools as defined in § 300.2. A mage who proceeds with a casting that meets these criteria without a filed and acknowledged NIC is in immediate breach of the Accords and may be subject to the sanctions detailed in § 800.1.

Furthermore, the "filing first" requirement dictates that the documentation must be physically or magically deposited at the Accords Desk before the first syllable of the incantation is uttered. Failure to comply shall result in the immediate forfeiture of any protections afforded by the Guild and may lead to an immediate summons for a Paradox Trial as outlined in § 800.2. In instances where the risk of the casting is deemed "imminent" by the practitioner—such as in cases of self-defense or the containment of a burgeoning rift—the practitioner may act first but must provide a sworn affidavit of emergency within one hour of the event's conclusion. Such affidavits must be notarized by a summoned notary as per § 600.5. If the casting results in a permanent alteration of the landscape or the creation of a permanent magical construct, the practitioner shall be held liable for all subsequent registry fees and maintenance costs. See § 900.2 for reporting thresholds.

body.heading: Reporting of Material Enchantments
body.text:
Any enchantment that imparts a permanent or semi-permanent property to a physical object, known as a Material Enchantment, must be reported to the Accords Desk to ensure the integrity of the regional market and the safety of the citizenry. The threshold for mandatory reporting is set at a minimum of fifty gold pieces in perceived material value, or any enchantment that alters the weight, volume, or elemental state of an object beyond a five percent variance from its natural state. For example, a blade that glows is a minor enchantment requiring no filing, but a blade that cuts through stone as if it were silk constitutes a Material Enchantment and requires full disclosure. Practitioners who fail to report such enchantments are liable for a "Late Reporting Surcharge." This surcharge shall accrue at a fixed rate of ten percent of the estimated market value per sunrise, calculated in the caster's original time zone.

The reporting period begins at the moment the enchantment is finalized and the object is released from the casting circle. Should a practitioner attempt to obfuscate the nature of the enchantment by claiming it is a mere "aesthetic flourish," the Aegis Magi reserve the right to seize the object for inspection. If the object is found to exceed the reporting thresholds, the practitioner shall be fined the full accrued surcharge plus a penalty of double the base fee. This ensures that the Innovators do not flood the markets with unregulated, high-potency items while the Conservators maintain the stability of the Midlands. For questions regarding the specific chemical changes of materials, see § 1001.7. For the disposal of failed enchantments, see § 400.4.

body.heading: Record Retention
body.text:
The Mages' Guild Accords Desk serves as the ultimate repository of magical history, and as such, the retention of records is paramount to the continuity of the Accord. All filings, including Notices of Intent to Cast, Material Enchantment reports, and Paradox Trial transcripts, shall be preserved in the Guild archives for a minimum duration of seven years. However, in the event that a record pertains to a "Geological Age" event—defined as any enchantment or ritual that results in the formation of new landmasses, the shifting of tectonic plates, or the creation of permanent, non-degradable geological features—the record shall be maintained indefinitely. The determination of whether a record qualifies as a "Geological Age" event is at the sole discretion of the Clerk of the Accords Desk, based on the Clerk's subjective assessment of the "humor" or "significance" of the event's permanence.

During the standard seven-year retention period, records may be accessed by authorized Conservators or Innovators for the purposes of research or litigation. During this time, the Desk may redact sensitive information regarding the Quiet List to protect the privacy of the high-ranking mages involved. Once a record is deemed to have reached its retention limit, it may be moved to the deep archives or, if the Clerk deems the content sufficiently trivial or amusing, may be ceremonially incinerated. No mage shall have the right to demand the destruction of their personal records before the expiration of the mandatory retention period. For the specific procedures regarding the redaction of sensitive data, see § 300.3.

body.heading: Identify Fees; Who Pays
body.text:
The administration of the Autumnwood Accords is a self-sustaining bureaucratic entity; therefore, the Guild shall not provide administrative services, permit processing, or enforcement actions gratis. Every action taken by the Accords Desk—from the filing of a Notice of Intent to Cast to the adjudication of a Paradox Trial—incurs a mandatory Administrative Fee. The fundamental principle of the Accords regarding these costs is simple: the individual who requests the service is the individual who shall bear the burden of the cost. The Accords Desk is expressly prohibited from waiving these fees for any reason, including political pressure from the Regal Empire, requests from the Silver Flame, or appeals from the Innovator faction.

The person who asks for the magical privilege pays for the bureaucratic oversight. This applies to all interactions with the Aegis Magi, who may levy additional "Enforcement Surcharges" if a mage's actions require the deployment of Guild resources to contain a magical anomaly. It is strictly forbidden for a third party to pay the fees on behalf of a mage without a signed Power of Attorney and a pre-payment of the "Proxy Fee." Furthermore, the Guild shall not accept Wario Coins as a valid form of tender for any official fees; all payments must be rendered in gold, mana-crystals, or other approved Guild-recognized currencies. Any attempt to bribe a Clerk with unauthorized tender is a felony offense punishable by immediate referral to the Paradox Trial. For details on the conversion of duel stakes into administrative fees, see § 800.4.

body.heading: False Provenance of Relics
body.text:
The Accords Desk serves as the arbiter of truth regarding the history and origin of magical artifacts. A common misconception among the lay public and even some novice casters is that a compelling narrative or a "story" constitutes a valid chain of title for a relic. The Accords Desk formally declares that a story is not a chain of title. For an artifact to be registered with a valid provenance, the owner must provide a continuous, documented history of ownership, including the names of previous keepers, the locations of previous storage, and the specific magical signatures of those who have held the item. A tale of a "lost king" or a "fallen civilization" is insufficient for the purpose of legal registration or the removal of restrictive wards.

If a practitioner attempts to register a relic based solely on oral tradition or unverified mythos, the filing shall be rejected as "Speculative Provenance." The practitioner may be required to submit to a forensic arcane audit, wherein the Aegis Magi will attempt to trace the magical "echoes" of the object's history. If the audit reveals that the artifact's history has been intentionally obscured or falsified—such as attempting to hide a relic's origin from the Conservators—the practitioner shall be subject to immediate prosecution for Fraudulent Provenance. This law is designed to prevent the illicit trade of stolen artifacts and to ensure that the Guild can properly monitor the movement of high-risk items. For the protocols regarding the scrying of closed books to verify provenance, see § 700.2.

sections.title: Reporting of Material Enchantments
sections.brief: Thresholds. Late reports accrue per sunrise in the caster's original time zone.

body.heading: Reporting of Material Enchantments
body.text:
All mages operating under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords shall be mandated to register any enchantment of a material nature that exceeds the standard threshold of common utility. A "Material Enchantment" is defined herein as any permanent or semi-permanent alteration of physical matter, including but not limiteded to the infusion of mana into structural masonry, the creation of sentient constructs, or the transmutation of base metals into durable alloys for commercial use. Any enchantment that possesses the capacity to affect a public thoroughfare, a private residence, or a communal resource must be filed with the Accords Desk within three lunar cycles of its completion. Failure to report such enchantments constitutes a breach of the Guild’s transparency protocols and may result in the immediate seizure of the enchanted object for safety inspection.

The threshold for mandatory reporting is determined by the magnitude of the arcane resonance. Minor household charms, such as self-lighting lanterns or cooling stones, do not require filing. However, any enchantment capable of sustaining a continuous magical output of more than fifty units of mana per hour, or any object capable of independent locomotion without a direct tether to a caster, falls under the mandatory reporting category. Mages who neglect to file these reports shall be subject to administrative fines. In the event of a failure to report, late reports shall accrue a penalty of twenty gold sovereigns per sunrise in the caster's original time zone. This penalty is designed to ensure that the Guild maintains an accurate and timely ledger of all active arcane signatures within the Midlands.

Furthermore, mages who engage in the mass production of material enchantments for sale to non-casters must provide a certificate of stability signed by a recognized Conservator. This is to prevent the proliferation of unstable artifacts that may lead to localized mana-voids or structural collapses. See § 900.1 for general duty to file before casting. See § 400.1 for research permits regarding experimental enchantments. All records of reported enchantments are subject to audit by the Aegis Magi at any time without prior notice. The Guild reserves the right to reclassify any "common" enchantment as a "Material Enchantment" if it is found to be utilized in a manner inconsistent with public safety or the preservation of the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: Record Retention
body.text:
The Mages' Guild Accords Desk shall maintain a rigorous system of record retention to ensure the continuity of magical jurisprudence and the preservation of historical precedent. All filings, including but not limited to research permits, contract notations, and incident reports, shall be preserved for a period of seven years. This timeframe is intended to provide sufficient historical context for the adjudication of ongoing disputes and to ensure that the lineage of magical permissions remains unbroken for the duration of a standard practitioner's career. During this period, records may be accessed by authorized officials, including Archmage Veyra and her appointed deputies, for the purposes of auditing or mediation.

Notwithstanding the standard seven-year rule, certain records may be held indefinitely if they pertain to "High-Risk" arcane activities, such as those involving the Forbidden Schools or restricted research. In such cases, the Clerk of the Accords Desk shall determine the retention period based on the enduring nature of the magical threat. For records involving the preservation of the Midlands' geological or ecological integrity, the Guild acknowledges the principle of "Geological Age." Specifically, records pertaining to the shifting of ley lines, the creation of permanent geographic features, or the stabilization of deep-earth rifts may be held for one geological age, or until such time as the Clerk finds the humor in the passage of time to be sufficiently profound to warrant archival rotation.

The determination of "funny" in the context of geological age is at the sole discretion of the presiding Clerk. This serves as a safeguard against the infinite accumulation of data that does not serve a practical administrative purpose, while still honoring the necessity of preserving ancient pacts. Records that have exceeded their retention period but are deemed of significant cultural or historical value may be moved to the deep archives, where they shall remain unless requested by the High Council. The destruction of records prior to the expiration of the seven-year period is strictly prohibited without a signed waiver from the Archmage Sovereign. See § 300.4 for reclassification of records.

body.heading: Identify Fees; Who Pays
body.text:
The administration of the Autumnwood Accords requires the collection of various fees to maintain the infrastructure of the Hall and the salaries of the clerks. These fees include, but are not limited to, filing fees for new enchantments, processing fees for Paradox Trials, and licensing fees for the use of restricted research facilities. It is the established policy of the Accords Desk that the responsibility for the payment of these fees rests solely upon the individual who initiated the request. The Desk shall not be held liable for the procurement of funds, nor shall it provide credit or extensions of payment to mages who lack the necessary capital.

The Desk is a neutral administrative body and does not function as a lending institution. Therefore, if a mage seeks a permit for a project, a license for a familiar, or a notation for a new contract, that mage is the primary debtor. If a third party provides the funding for such a project, that third party may be designated as the "Payor of Record," but the "Requesting Party" remains legally responsible for the completion of the payment. Should a payment fail to materialize, the Desk shall suspend all pending applications and revoke any temporary permissions granted during the application phase. No magic, including the transmutation of currency or the manipulation of debt, shall be used to circumvent these fees.

Furthermore, the Desk shall not be compelled to provide services for free under the guise of "public interest" unless a direct decree is issued by Archmage Veyra. While the Guild serves the Midlands, the administrative costs of maintaining the Accords are a burden that must be borne by those who benefit from the protections and privileges of the law. Mages who find the fees to be burdensome are encouraged to seek sponsorship from the Goodstyle Artisans or other licensed commercial entities. The Desk shall not accept Wario Coins as a valid form of tender for any administrative fees, as they are not recognized as legal currency under the Accords. See § 800.4 for duel stakes converted to fees.

body.heading: False Provenance of Relics
body.text:
The integrity of the magical marketplace and the historical record relies upon the accurate provenance of all artifacts, relics, and enchanted items brought before the Guild for registration or appraisal. A mage who presents a relic for official recognition must provide a verifiable chain of custody. It is a fundamental principle of the Accords that a story is not a chain of title. While the Guild acknowledges the importance of oral tradition and the mystical "weight" of a narrative, these elements do not constitute legal evidence of ownership or origin. A compelling tale of a relic's journey through the hands of heroes does not grant the bearer the right to claim it as a sanctioned artifact if the physical evidence of its history is lacking.

Mages who knowingly submit false provenance records to the Accords Desk shall be subject to immediate investigation. This includes the fabrication of historical documents, the forging of signatures from deceased masters, or the invention of "ancient" origins for newly created items. The Guild seeks to prevent the flooding of the market with fraudulent "relics" that could mislead other casters or lead to the misappropriation of significant cultural items. If a relic's history is murky or purely anecdotal, it shall be registered as an "Artifact of Unknown Origin" rather than being granted a prestigious designation. The Desk shall not be responsible for correcting the historical record once a false claim has been entered into the ledger.

Furthermore, the provenance of a relic must be sufficient to prove that the item was not acquired through illicit means, such as the theft of Guild property or the violation of the Iron Mandate. While the Accords Desk does not recognize the laws of the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion, it does maintain a policy against the trade of stolen goods. Any item whose provenance is tied to a known crime or a violation of the Accords shall be confiscated. Mages are advised to maintain meticulous records of their acquisitions to ensure that their collections remain in good standing. See § 700.1 for evidence generally. See § 300.5 for research copies of quiet items.

sections.title: Record Retention
sections.brief: Seven years or one geological age, whichever the clerk finds funnier.

body.heading: Record Retention
body.text:
The Archival Integrity of the Autumnwood Accords dictates that the preservation of magical records is paramount to the stability of the Midlands. All filings, including but not limited to research permits, Paradox Trial transcripts, and unauthorized field use reports, shall be maintained in the permanent registry of the Mages' Guild. The duration of such retention is governed by the principle of Perpetual Continuity; specifically, records shall be preserved for a period of seven years or one geological age, whichever the clerk finds funnier. This clause serves to acknowledge the inherent fluidity of temporal magic and the unpredictable nature of arcane decay. While a standard administrative cycle may suggest a fixed term, the Clerk of the Accords reserves the sole prerogative to determine the "humorous" expiration of a record based on its thematic relevance to the Guild's ongoing history.

In instances where a record pertains to a Paradox Trial, the retention period may be extended indefinitely if the resulting pocket-prison remains active, as the existence of the prison constitutes a continuous event. Conversely, records pertaining to minor infractions or the mundane activities of the Goodstyle Artisans may be subject to expedited purging should the Clerk deem the aesthetic of the archive to be cluttered. It is strictly forbidden for any mage, including those of the Innovator faction, to request the destruction of a record to obscure past transgressions. Any attempt to influence the Clerk’s sense of humor regarding retention periods shall be viewed as an act of administrative subversion. For matters regarding the specific handling of restricted research copies, see § 300.5. All records must be inscribed in a medium resistant to standard transmutation or erosion.

body.heading: Identify Fees; Who Pays
body.text:
The financial obligations arising from the administration of the Autumnwood Accords are governed by the Principle of Origin. It is the established mandate of the Mages' Guild that the costs associated with the filing, mediation, and enforcement of these laws shall be borne by the person who asked. This means that any mage seeking a research permit under § 400.1, requesting a Paradox Trial, or seeking mediation from Archmage Veyra is solely responsible for the procurement of necessary fees. The Desk, as a neutral administrative body, shall not be held liable for the costs of magical auditing, archival storage, or the logistical requirements of the Aegis Magi.

No fee shall be levied against the Guild's general treasury for the processing of standard requests, nor shall any fee be diverted to the Innovators or Conservators for the purpose of political lobbying. If a request involves a third party, such as a merchant from the Regal Empire or a representative of the Silver Flame, the requesting mage must provide a signed guarantee of payment from said party before the Desk will initiate the filing. The Desk shall not provide credit, nor shall it accept Wario Coins as a valid form of tender, as such currency is explicitly barred from Guild circulation. If a mage finds themselves unable to produce the required funds, the request shall be returned without action. For more information on the conversion of duel stakes to administrative fees, see § 800.4.

body.heading: False Provenance of Relics
body.text:
The authentication of magical artifacts and relics within the Midlands is subject to the Doctrine of Verifiable Lineage. A story, regardless of its narrative complexity, evocative power, or historical weight, does not constitute a chain of title. The Mages' Guild explicitly rejects "mythic provenance" as a valid legal basis for the ownership or authorized use of artifacts. To establish a valid chain of title, a relic must possess a documented history of physical transfer, verified by the signatures of previous owners or the seals of recognized authorities such as the Conservators. A tale of a relic being "gifted by a dying star" or "forged in the fires of the first rift" is considered a literary achievement but holds no weight in the eyes of the Accords.

Mages who attempt to register a relic based solely on oral tradition or "inherited legend" shall be flagged for a secondary audit. If the provenance is found to be fabricated or intentionally misleading to circumvent restrictions on the Unsanctioned Arts, the offending mage shall be subject to the Paradox Trial as outlined in § 800.2. The Desk shall not recognize any artifact whose history is obscured by the "Quiet List" protocols unless a formal waiver is granted by Archmage Veyra. Furthermore, any relic claiming to be a component of the Heartstone or a product of the Great Rift must be surveyed by a Guild-approved cartographer before a provenance can even be considered for preliminary filing. For matters regarding the scrying of closed books to determine true origins, see § 700.2.

sections.title: Identify Fees; Who Pays
sections.brief: The person who asked. Not the Desk.

body.heading: Identify Fees; Who Pays
body.text:
In the matter of identification, verification, and administrative processing of magical artifacts, relics, or items of significant arcane density, the Guild shall establish a clear distinction between the act of identification and the liability for the associated costs. Any mage, initiate, or contracted agent seeking to have an object cataloged, verified for safety, or assessed for its potential violation of the Autumnwood Accords shall be deemed the primary petitioner. Consequently, all fees associated with the identification of such items shall be the sole responsibility of the individual or entity who initiated the request. The Accords Desk serves as a neutral administrative body; it does not provide identification services as a public utility, nor shall it ever be held liable for the costs incurred during the processing of a petitioner's property.

Should a petitioner claim that the identification of an item was performed as a matter of Guild necessity—for instance, if an item was seized by the Aegis Magi for immediate containment—the petitioner shall still be held liable for the administrative fees unless a formal waiver is granted by Archmage Veyra. In cases where multiple parties claim ownership of a single relic, the Desk shall not adjudicate the underlying title; it shall instead require a deposit from all claiming parties to cover the identification costs, with the fees being refunded only upon the final resolution of the ownership dispute. The Desk is strictly prohibited from utilizing Guild treasury funds to offset the costs of private identifications.

Furthermore, any mage who attempts to have the Accords Desk assume the role of a debt collector for unpaid identification fees shall be found in violation of administrative protocol. If a petitioner fails to provide the requisite tender, the Desk shall cease all work immediately and return the item to the petitioner in its current state, with no further liability on the part of the Guild. The Desk shall not be compelled to provide identification for items of unknown origin if the petitioner refuses to provide a bond against the risk of arcane leakage during the inspection process. See § 900.4.

body.heading: False Provenance of Relics
body.text:
The Guild recognizes that the history of a magical artifact is often obscured by the passage of centuries, the erosion of memory, or the deliberate obfuscation of its previous owners. However, the Accords Desk shall maintain a strict distinction between a "narrative of origin" and a "legal chain of title." A story, regardless of its poetic depth, historical resonance, or the prestige of its supposed author, does not constitute a valid legal conveyance of ownership or a certification of the item’s provenance. Any mage attempting to register a relic based solely on oral tradition, transcribed legends, or "inherited" myths without corroborating evidence shall find their application for registration suspended until such time as a verifiable audit of the item's movement can be produced.

The Guild shall not accept "mythic provenance" as a substitute for legal clearance. For example, an item described as "the blade of a fallen king" provides no more legal standing than a common iron rod if the Guild cannot trace the transfer of the blade from the kingdom to the current holder. Mages seeking to register relics of high arcane potency must provide a documented history of ownership that satisfies the requirements of the Conservators. If a relic’s history is broken or lost, it must be declared "Orphaned" and subjected to the standard quarantine procedures before any identification can occur. The Desk shall not be held responsible for the validity of a petitioner’s claims; it is the petitioner’s burden to prove that the item was not stolen, cursed, or illegally extracted from a protected site.

Furthermore, any deliberate attempt to provide a false provenance to circumvent the restrictions placed upon certain schools of magic—specifically those categorized as "Forbidden" by the Conservators—shall be treated as a felony under the Accords. If a mage knowingly presents a fabricated history to gain access to restricted research facilities or to bypass the Innovators' oversight, they shall be subject to the Paradox Trial. The Guild's records are a matter of law, not a library of fiction. A story is not a chain of title, and the Desk shall not permit the romanticization of history to supersede the rigorous demands of magical safety and legal clarity. See § 300.5.

sections.title: False Provenance of Relics
sections.brief: A story is not a chain of title.

body.heading: False Provenance of Relics
body.text:
Any individual, entity, or faction seeking to introduce a relic, artifact, or enchanted object into the public sphere, the Guild’s archives, or any sanctioned marketplace under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords shall be held strictly liable for the veracity of the item’s provenance. The Accords Desk hereby establishes that the mere existence of a narrative surrounding an object does not constitute a legal chain of title. A story, regardless of its antiquity, poetic resonance, or perceived historical weight, is not a substitute for documented evidence of lawful acquisition or ancestral right. Practitioners who attempt to bypass the rigorous standards of § 1101.2 Relics; Chain of Title by weaving elaborate tapestries of mythic origin are subject to immediate investigation by the Aegis Magi.

The Guild recognizes that the "mystique" of an object often serves as a veil for illicit trafficking or the misappropriation of cultural heritage. Therefore, any claim of provenance based solely on oral tradition, "found-item" anecdotes, or "ancestral memory" without corroborating physical evidence of transition shall be deemed insufficient for the purposes of legal registration. To prevent the laundering of stolen goods through the manufacture of convenient legends, the Accords Desk requires a verifiable paper trail—or its magical equivalent—detailing the movement of the object from its point of origin to the current holder. If the lineage of an object is broken by a period of "lost history," the burden of proof remains on the claimant to demonstrate that the acquisition was not performed through coercion, theft, or violation of previous sovereign treaties.

Furthermore, the intentional fabrication of a false provenance is classified as a Grade III Arcane Fraud. Any mage or merchant found to have knowingly authored a fictitious history for a relic to increase its market value, influence political standing, or obscure its dangerous nature shall face immediate referral to the Paradox Trial for adjudication. During such proceedings, the court shall weigh the discrepancy between the "story" provided and the actual magical signature of the item. If the magical resonance of the relic contradicts the stated history—for instance, if an object claimed to be a gift of peace displays a signature of violent subjugation—the provenance shall be struck from the record, and the item may be seized as contraband.

In instances where an object’s history is genuinely unknowable due to the destruction of records, the owner must register the item as "Unverified Origin." Such items may be held privately but are prohibited from being sold, gifted, or traded within the Midlands without a specific waiver from the Archmage Sovereign. The Accords Desk shall not be misled by the eloquence of a scholar or the passion of a collector; a story is a matter of art, while a chain of title is a matter of law. For further guidance on the required documentation for relic registration, see § 1101.2. For matters regarding the preservation of existing records, see § 900.3.

sections.title: Financial Fraud and Manipulation Generally
sections.brief: General prohibition. Cross-ref later 1001 sections.

body.heading: Financial Fraud and Manipulation Generally
body.text:
Any act of deception involving the deliberate manipulation of arcane, material, or ethereal assets to induce a party into an involuntary transaction or to misrepresent the nature of a magical contract shall be deemed a primary violation of the Autumnwood Accords. The Guild maintains that the integrity of the magical marketplace is the bedrock of civil stability within the Midlands; therefore, any mage or non-mage entity utilizing the arcane to distort the perception of value, ownership, or intent shall be subject to immediate investigation by the Aegis Magi. This prohibition encompasses, but is not limited to, the fabrication of magical provenance, the clandestine alteration of enchantment potency, and the use of coercive mental influence to bypass the voluntary nature of a trade. All such actions constitute a breach of the public trust and may result in the initiation of a Paradox Trial as outlined in § 800.2.

Furthermore, any individual found to be engaging in systematic financial fraud shall be barred from holding a Provisional Guild Pass, regardless of their political standing or historical contributions to the Innovators or Conservators. The Accords Desk reserves the right to seize all assets involved in a fraudulent transaction, including the forfeiture of the magical components used to facilitate the deceit. See § 1001.6 for specific rules regarding the transfer of assets and see § 1001.10 regarding the visibility of underlying obligations. Any entity found in violation of this section may be referred to the Archmage Sovereign for a determination of permanent expulsion from the Guild's jurisdiction.

body.heading: Prohibited Spells in Financial Markets
body.text:
The use of specific classes of magic within the context of trade, lending, or the valuation of assets is strictly prohibited to ensure the impartiality of the market. This includes, but is not limited to, spells of mass compulsion, truth-distortion, and any high-level divination used to extract private financial secrets from a counterparty without express, written consent. The Innovators may argue that such restrictions hamper the flow of information; however, the Conservators maintain that these spells undermine the fundamental principle of free will in commerce. Any mage utilizing these prohibited schools in a commercial setting shall face immediate sanction and potential sealing of their primary casting focus.

It is further mandated that the Quiet List shall remain strictly confidential. No mage shall recite, reference, or hint at the contents of the Quiet List in any tavern, marketplace, or public forum. Any attempt to use the existence of the Quiet List as a basis for market manipulation or as a tool of intimidation is a felony under the Accords. The Aegis Magi are authorized to use any means necessary to silence a mage who violates this confidentiality. For matters involving the specific reporting of forbidden research in trade, see § 400.1. For the consequences of unauthorized casting in public spaces, see § 500.2.

body.heading: Valuation After Alteration
body.text:
Any magical object or item that undergoes a significant transfiguration, enchantment, or physical alteration must be formally re-assayed by a Guild-certified appraiser before it may be traded or used as collateral. The mere act of alteration does not change the legal status of the item; for example, a petrified inventory remains a liability of the owner until the petrification is reversed and the item is re-certified. The burden of proof regarding the original state of the item lies with the seller. If a seller fails to provide a pre-alteration certificate, the item shall be valued at its lowest possible utility state for the purposes of all Guild-governed contracts.

In cases where an item is altered to increase its magical potency, the seller must disclose the source of the enhancement. If the enhancement involves the use of restricted materials or unauthorized schools of magic, the item is subject to immediate seizure by the Conservators. This rule ensures that the sudden influx of "enhanced" goods does not destabilize the local economy or introduce volatile elements into the Midlands. For inquiries regarding the custody of such specimens during the assay period, see § 400.4. For matters regarding the unauthorized growth of magical entities as a form of asset, see § 400.5.

body.heading: Illusion-Based Fraud
body.text:
The use of illusions to misrepresent the physical properties, quantity, price, or identity of goods, buyers, or sellers is strictly prohibited. A mage who casts an illusion to make a crate of common grain appear as enchanted wheat, or to make a small sum of gold appear as a mountain of wealth, is in direct violation of the Autumnwood Accords. This applies equally to the fabrication of a buyer’s identity; any mage who assumes the guise of a known entity to secure a favorable trade agreement shall be prosecuted for identity fraud. The Guild views the manipulation of perception as a direct assault on the sanctity of the agreement.

Furthermore, illusions used to obfuscate the true price of an item during a negotiation are considered a form of price-gouging and shall be met with heavy fines. If an illusion is used to hide a lien or a pre-existing debt on an object, the transaction is null and void, and the offending mage may be remanded to a pocket-prison. The Aegis Magi are tasked with patrolling major trade hubs to ensure that "visual honesty" is maintained. For procedures regarding the use of pocket dimensions as a means to hide these illusions, see § 400.2. For the reporting of material enchantments that may be mistaken for illusions, see § 900.2.

body.heading: Material Alteration of Traded Goods
body.text:
Any trade involving the aggregation, permissible transfiguration, or material alteration of goods must be accompanied by a full disclosure of the changes made to the base material. The burden of disclosure lies entirely with the seller. If a mage transfigures a common metal into a more valuable alloy, they must provide the chemical and arcane blueprints of the process to the Guild's records. Failure to disclose such alterations is a violation of the Accords and may result in the immediate revocation of the seller's trading license. This ensures that the "hidden" properties of a sold item do not cause unforeseen magical reactions for the buyer.

Historical annotations regarding the transmutation of materials are kept in the central archives; any mage performing these actions must cite the relevant precedents to ensure compliance with existing safety protocols. For example, the transmutation of lead into gold is subject to specific reporting thresholds as detailed in § 1001.8. Any transfiguration that results in a permanent change to the molecular structure of the trade good must be registered within three lunar cycles of the sale. For further details on the legality of transfiguring materials into laboratory equipment, see § 400.2. For the identification of fees associated with these registrations, see § 900.4.

body.heading: Endowments and Gifts of Magical Assets
body.text:
A magical asset provided as an endowment or a gift is not exempt from the laws of the Accords; rather, it is subject to specific oversight regarding its long-term obligations. A "hat that later bills the wearer" for its magical services is a classic example of a deceptive endowment. Any gift that carries a hidden cost, a retroactive debt, or a self-replicating fee structure must be disclosed in full at the moment of the gift's delivery. If a gift is found to contain a hidden "billing" enchantment or a parasitic mana-drain, the gift is declared a violation of the Accords and the provider shall be liable for triple damages.

Furthermore, the transfer of a magical asset as a gift does not transfer the liability of any existing liens or debts attached to that asset unless such a transfer is explicitly stated in a notarized deed. The Guild recognizes that many magical items possess "sentience-lite" properties that may attempt to claim ownership or demand payment; the owner of the original asset is responsible for suppressing such behaviors until a formal transfer of title is complete. For the identification of fees regarding these transfers, see § 900.4. For the reporting of material enchantments that might facilitate such "billing," see § 900.2.

body.heading: Disclosure of Composition, Value, and Risk
body.text:
All mages and merchants are required to provide a full and accurate disclosure of the composition, value, and inherent risk of any magical item offered for trade. This disclosure must be provided in a language that the buyer understands; a disclosure provided in a dead tongue or a complex arcane cipher that the buyer cannot read is not considered a "full" disclosure and is treated as a deliberate obfuscation. This includes the disclosure of any "side effects," such as minor telepathic echoes, unintended environmental shifts, or the risk of the item becoming volatile under specific conditions.

Failure to disclose a known risk—such as an item's tendency to teleport when exposed to moonlight—shall result in the immediate forfeiture of the sale and a permanent mark on the seller's Guild record. The seller is liable for any damages incurred by the buyer due to non-disclosure. The Accords Desk requires that all high-risk items be accompanied by a "Warning of Volatility" scroll. For the reporting of such material enchantments, see § 900.2. For the legal consequences of providing false provenance for such items, see § 900.5.
