The Guild recognizes the inherent danger in the trade of "Bound Objects"—items that possess a degree of sentience, independent movement, or the ability to act as an agent of their owner. When such objects are used as collateral or as part of a secured transaction, they are subject to unique "Walk-Away" clauses. Because a bound object can potentially move itself out of a physical vault or flee a site of seizure, the owner must provide a "Binding Guarantee" that the object will remain stationary and compliant during the duration of the transaction.

Any contract involving a bound object as collateral must include a "Stationary Clause." If the object "walks away" during a period of legal encumbrance, the owner is held strictly liable for the loss of the asset and for any damage caused by the object’s flight. The Guild considers the loss of a bound object from a secured location as a breach of the Accord's stability measures. Sellers of bound objects must disclose the object’s level of autonomy and its history of compliance.

In the event that a bound object flees its designated location, the Aegis Magi may be authorized to track and retrieve it using "Recall" magic, the costs of which shall be borne by the owner. Transactions involving objects with high levels of agency (such as golems or sentient constructs) must be overseen by a Guild Notary to ensure that the "binding" is sufficient to prevent the asset from abandoning its legal obligations. Collateral that can walk away requires extraordinary security; failure to provide such security is a violation of the Accord.

sections.title: Layered Transfiguration Schemes
sections.brief: Read as one scheme if a reasonable toad would be confused.

body.heading: Layered Transfiguration Schemes
body.text:
The Guild hereby establishes the "Reasonable Toad" standard for the interpretation of complex magical transmutations. If a mage employs a series of layered transfigurations—where an object is changed into one form, then another, then a third, and so on—the entire sequence shall be read as a single, continuous scheme if a reasonable toad would be confused by the intermediate steps. This prevents mages from using "nested" transmutations to bypass the Guild’s reporting thresholds or to hide the original nature of an asset.

For example, if a mage transmutes lead into a copper pot, then into a silver bowl, and finally into a gold goblet, the Guild will view this as a single transmutation of lead into gold. The intermediate steps of "copper" and "silver" do not reset the reporting requirements or exempt the mage from the taxes associated with the final gold product. The intent of the mage is the primary factor in legal determination; if the sequence of changes is clearly designed to obfuscate the final result from the Assay Desk, it shall be treated as a fraudulent "Layered Scheme."

All mages who engage in complex transmutations are required to file a "Sequence of Intent" form before beginning the process. This form must outline the final intended form and the steps required to reach it. If a mage fails to file such a form and the final result is found to be a violation of the Accords, the Guild may impose the maximum penalty for "Deceptive Transmutation." The Guild's goal is to ensure that the complexity of a spell does not provide a loophole for the evasion of the Accords.

sections.title: Gifts That Later Move
sections.brief: A gift with a remaining geas is not a gift.

body.heading: Gifts That Later Move
body.text:
A gift with a remaining geas is not a gift. Under the prevailing statutes of the Autumnwood Accords, a "gift" is defined as a voluntary transfer of magical, physical, or metaphysical property without the expectation of future consideration or the imposition of lingering obligations. When a donor purports to bestow an item upon a recipient, but the item remains bound by a geas, enchantment, or lingering magical tether that dictates the recipient's actions, the transfer is legally categorized as a "conditional conveyance" rather than a gift. Such an act constitutes a violation of the principle of free agency and may be subject to immediate seizure by the Aegis Magi. If the geas is active at the time of transfer, the donor has effectively bypassed the requirements of a formal contract, and the recipient is not entitled to the protections afforded to gift-receivers. See § 1001.6.

Furthermore, the presence of a lingering geas implies a continuing interest of the donor in the object's utility or the recipient's behavior. This is a fundamental breach of the Accords’ guidelines on the movement of magical assets. Any individual seeking to dispose of a geased object as a gift must first undergo a "Purification of Intent" at a recognized Guild station to ensure all ties to the original owner are severed. Failure to do so shall result in the item being declared "Contraband of Bound Origin." In cases where the geas is clandestine—hidden from the recipient by illusion or complex layering—the donor shall be held liable for "Malicious Tethering," a felony under the current Innovator-Conservator mediation.

The Accords Desk maintains that a gift must be a clean break. If a hat, for instance, begins to bill its wearer for "maintenance" or "protection" after being gifted, it is not a gift but an endowment or a hidden lease. The legal fiction of the gift is dissolved the moment a new obligation is detected. Any party attempting to argue that the geas was a "feature" of the gift is barred from such defense unless the geas was explicitly disclosed in a written deed of transfer. For the purposes of the Paradox Trial, any mage who uses a geased gift to compel a peer into an unauthorized action shall be treated as if they had directly cast the compulsion themselves. See § 800.2.

body.heading: Relics; Chain of Title
body.text:
Provenance, Quiet List relics. All relics of significant arcane magnitude, historical weight, or cultural importance must possess a clear and unbroken chain of title as recognized by the Accords Desk. A relic is defined as any object that has been the focus of a major magical event, a seat of power for a recognized lineage, or an artifact of the Quiet List. For items originating from the Quiet List, the chain of title is inherently restricted; while the existence of such items is not a matter of public record, their movement between private collectors and Guild-sanctioned vaults must be documented via "Shadow Ledgers." Any relic whose provenance is obscured by more than three generations of ownership, or which lacks a verified signature from a known artisan or mage of standing, shall be subject to a "Provenance Inquiry."

During a Provenance Inquiry, the Aegis Magi may seize the artifact for a period not to exceed thirty days to verify its history. If the artifact is found to be a product of the Iron Mandate or the Regal Empire’s illicit seizures, it shall be confiscated immediately. Furthermore, relics associated with the Silver Flame or the Cosmic Jesters are subject to heightened scrutiny and may be declared "Hostile Assets" if their chain of title involves any recognized agents of these factions. The Accords Desk does not recognize "finders keepers" as a valid basis for the acquisition of relics; any item of power found in the wild must be reported to the nearest Conservator outpost for appraisal and registration.

The Quiet List, while not a public catalogue, serves as the primary registry for items that pose a risk to the stability of the Midlands. Relics held by the public that are found to be on the Quiet List without proper authorization shall be placed under "Active Custodianship." Owners of such relics are granted the right to possess them but are strictly prohibited from displaying, selling, or lending them to non-Guild entities. Any breach of these restrictions shall result in the immediate revocation of the owner's right of possession and the initiation of a Paradox Trial to determine if the relic’s misuse constitutes a threat to the Accords. See § 800.2.

body.heading: Curse as Warranty Disclaimer
body.text:
A curse is not 'as is' unless disclosed. In the commerce of magical artifacts and enchanted goods, the "As Is" clause is frequently invoked by vendors to absolve themselves of liability for the inherent properties of an item. However, the Autumnwood Accords explicitly state that a curse—defined as a persistent, harmful, or restrictive magical effect intended to afflict the owner or user—does not qualify as an "inherent property" for the purpose of warranty disclaimer. If a vendor sells a cursed object without a prominent, magically-detectable warning, they are in violation of the Accords. The burden of disclosure lies with the seller; the buyer is not required to possess advanced scrying capabilities to identify a hidden curse.

Any contract of sale that includes a "Curse as Warranty Disclaimer" is considered null and void. The presence of a curse is viewed as a defect in the item's utility, much like a structural flaw in a physical building. If a buyer discovers a curse that was not disclosed at the time of sale, they are entitled to a full refund of the purchase price, plus any "Restoration Fees" incurred to cleanse the object. The seller may be further fined for "Negligent Enchantment," particularly if the curse is of a nature that causes permanent physical or mental harm. The Aegis Magi are authorized to perform "Truth-Binding" on vendors who claim they were unaware of the curse's existence.

For the purposes of the Accords Desk, a "curse" is distinguished from a "volatile enchantment." A volatile enchantment is a known risk associated with high-level magic (such as a rift-prone focus) and may be sold with a standard warning. A curse, however, is a targeted malicious effect. Therefore, while a mage may sell a staff that has a chance of exploding (volatile), they may not sell a staff that actively drains the user's life force (curse) without a specific, notarized disclosure. Failure to provide such disclosure shall result in the immediate suspension of the vendor’s Guild license and a mandatory appearance before the Conservators. See § 800.1.

body.heading: Blessing of a Competing Vendor
body.text:
A blessing sold against a rival is advertising, then fraud if it binds. The Accords recognize the right of mages to engage in the trade of blessings, which are categorized as "Positive Efficacy Charms." However, when a blessing is specifically designed to provide a mechanical or magical advantage over a competitor’s product—for example, a blessing that causes a rival’s shield to shatter upon contact—it is classified as "Aggressive Advertising." Such blessings must be clearly labeled as "Competitive Efficacy" and are subject to a higher licensing fee. If a blessing is sold with the intent to sabotage a rival's goods, the seller must ensure that the effect is localized and does not cause collateral damage to the general populace or the Midlands' infrastructure.

Fraud occurs when a blessing sold against a rival contains a "Binding Clause" or a "Hidden Malus." If a mage sells a "Loyalty Blessing" for a customer that secretly binds the customer to the mage’s own services while simultaneously degrading the customer's ability to use any other merchant's products, this is a violation of the Accords. The transition from "Aggressive Advertising" to "Fraud" occurs at the moment the magic exerts unauthorized control over the recipient’s agency or financial independence. The Accords Desk views the use of magic to create "Monopolistic Bindings" as a severe violation of the principles of fair trade and magical stability.

Any party found guilty of such fraud shall be subject to a Paradox Trial. The punishment for "Binding Fraud" is often the "Seal of Silence" on the offending mage's commercial magic, preventing them from selling any blessings for a period of no less than ten years. Furthermore, the mage may be required to issue a "Public Rectification," a magically-broadcasted apology to all affected customers. The Aegis Magi are tasked with monitoring the marketplaces of the Midlands to ensure that blessings remain tools of protection and enhancement rather than instruments of economic enslavement. See § 800.3.

sections.title: Relics; Chain of Title
sections.brief: Provenance, Quiet List relics.

body.heading: Relics; Chain of Title
body.text:
The acquisition, transfer, and possession of any artifact of significant thaumaturgical potency, hereafter referred to as a "Relic," shall be governed by the strict requirements of the Chain of Title as established under the Autumnwood Accords. A Relic is defined as any object imbued with persistent magical properties, historical significance, or a lineage of ownership that exceeds three consecutive owners within a single century. To establish a valid Chain of Title, a claimant must provide a documented history of possession that is free from "arcane gaps"—periods of time where the Relic’s location or ownership is unaccounted for by any recognized Guild registry. Any Relic lacking a continuous history of provenance is deemed "Orphaned" and may be subject to seizure by the Aegis Magi for the purpose of public safety and the prevention of unauthorized ritual activation.

Provenance must be verified by a licensed Notary of the Accords Desk. A mere oral history or a personal narrative provided by a seller does not constitute a legal Chain of Title; as stated in § 900.5, a story is not a chain of title. The claimant must present physical evidence of transfer, such as signed Deeds of Relinquishment, notarized Wills of the deceased, or verified records of auction. In instances where a Relic was obtained through non-standard means, such as "discovery" in wild zones or ruins, the claimant must provide a Certificate of Discovery, which includes a survey of the site to ensure no local treaties or sovereign boundaries were violated. Failure to provide such documentation shall result in the Relic being classified as "Unsanctioned," rendering it illegal to transport or trade within the Midlands.

Special provisions apply to items designated on the Quiet List. Any Relic identified as a Quiet List asset is subject to heightened secrecy and restricted movement. The Chain of Title for a Quiet List Relic must be held in a sealed, magically-locked vault accessible only by the owner and the Archmage Veyra. Public disclosure of the existence of a Quiet List Relic, or any attempt to register its Chain of Title in a public ledger, shall be grounds for immediate prosecution. See § 300.3 for specific procedures regarding the non-public listing of such items. Furthermore, any Relic whose provenance involves the Regal Empire, the Iron Legion, or the Silver Flame is subject to immediate confiscation and "Sanction and Seal" procedures, as these entities are deemed hostile to the Accord's jurisdiction.

Mages who possess Relics without a verified Chain of Title are prohibited from utilizing the Relic's primary functions for any public-facing purpose. This includes, but is not limited to, the use of Relics in street duels, public demonstrations, or the charging of local mana-grids. Should a Relic be found to have a fractured Chain of Title due to a lapse in documentation, the owner may apply for a "Restoration of Title" through a formal petition to the Conservators. This process requires a full audit of the object’s history and may involve a fee to the Aegis Magi to cover the costs of investigative magical tracing. If the petition is denied, the Relic shall be held in escrow by the Guild until such time as a valid Chain of Title can be produced or the item is declared a public hazard and subsequently neutralized.

sections.title: Curse as Warranty Disclaimer
sections.brief: A curse is not 'as is' unless disclosed.

body.heading: Curse as Warranty Disclaimer
body.text:
§ 1101.3 Curse as Warranty Disclaimer. The transfer of any enchanted object, relic, or mundane item bearing a lingering metaphysical burden shall not be governed by the standard "as is" clauses of common commerce under the Autumnwood Accords. Specifically, the presence of a curse—defined herein as any persistent, deleterious magical effect intended to harm, hinder, or drain the vitality, sanity, or resources of a subsequent owner—constitutes a material defect in the item's condition. Any merchant, practitioner, or private citizen seeking to divest themselves of a cursed object may not utilize the standard "as is" disclaimer to insulate themselves from liability. If a curse is present and remains undisclosed at the point of sale or transfer, the seller shall be held in breach of the Accords, subject to the penalties outlined in § 1001.5.

Furthermore, the legal distinction between a "dormant" curse and an "active" curse is irrelevant for the purposes of warranty disclosure. If the magical signature of a curse is detectable by a standard sensory appraisal by a licensed Aegis Mage or a certified Conservator, the seller is mandated to provide a full disclosure of the curse’s origin, potency, and duration. Failure to do so constitutes a willful concealment of a hazard. A curse is not "as is" unless the buyer has been explicitly warned of its existence and has voluntarily accepted the risk of its activation. In such cases of explicit disclosure, the seller may be granted immunity from subsequent claims of "hidden defects," provided the disclosure was made in writing or through a binding verbal contract witnessed by a Guild-recognized notary.

The Innovators may argue that certain "reactive" curses—those that only trigger under specific, rare conditions—do not constitute an immediate defect. The Conservators, however, maintain that any potential for harm constitutes a breach of the stability of the local weave. Therefore, for the purposes of the Autumnwood Accords, any curse that possesses the capacity to manifest harm shall be treated as a primary defect. Any attempt to bypass these requirements by claiming the curse is a "feature" of the item's history, rather than a flaw in its current state, shall be viewed as a fraudulent misrepresentation. See § 1001.7 for requirements regarding the disclosure of risk in complex magical assets.

body.heading: Blessing of a Competing Vendor
body.text:
§ 1101.4 Blessing of a Competing Vendor. The use of benevolent magic, specifically "blessings," to actively undermine the commercial interests of a rival entity is strictly regulated as a form of illicit advertising. While the Mages' Guild recognizes the right of practitioners to promote their services, the application of a blessing to an object or person with the express intent of rendering a competitor's product unusable, unappealing, or magically incompatible is prohibited. If a blessing is sold as a service to a customer with the primary purpose of creating a hostile metaphysical environment against a specific rival vendor, such an act shall be classified as unauthorized advertising.

Should such a blessing contain binding components—namely, magic that actively prevents a consumer from utilizing a competitor's goods or creates a persistent magical barrier against a rival’s influence—it shall be elevated from a mere advertising violation to a felony of magical fraud. Under the Accords, a blessing that binds a consumer to a single vendor by magically suppressing the efficacy of all other competing products is considered a violation of the free flow of magical commerce. Such "exclusive bindings" are prohibited unless the vendor can prove a legitimate safety concern or a unique, non-compressive magical synergy that does not infringe upon the consumer's right to seek alternative services.

The Aegis Magi are authorized to seize any artifacts or objects imbued with such "hostile blessings" and may levy heavy fines against the practitioner who cast them. Furthermore, any vendor found to be distributing blessings of this nature shall be barred from Guild certification for a period of no less than five years. This provision ensures that the marketplace remains a space of open competition rather than one governed by magical monopolies or "blessed" coercion. Practitioners are encouraged to seek counsel with the Conservators to ensure their promotional enchantments do not cross the threshold into prohibited binding magic. See § 1001.1 for general principles on financial fraud and manipulation.

sections.title: Blessing of a Competing Vendor
sections.brief: A blessing sold against a rival is advertising, then fraud if it binds.

body.heading: Blessing of a Competing Vendor
body.text:
Under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords and the oversight of the Accords Desk, all magical services provided by licensed practitioners within the Midlands shall be subject to the standards of fair commerce and arcane integrity. While the Mages' Guild acknowledges the inherent right of a practitioner to solicit patronage, the application of liturgical or protective enchantments for the express purpose of undermining a specific, identified competitor is strictly regulated. A blessing, by its fundamental nature, is a metaphysical enhancement of a subject's state; however, when such a blessing is structured to actively diminish the efficacy, reputation, or commercial viability of a rival entity, it transcends the realm of standard mercantile competition and enters the sphere of regulated magical advertising.

Any practitioner who offers a "Blessing of Superiority" or a "Ward of Market Dominance" that specifically names, targets, or references a competing vendor shall be required to file a Notice of Commercial Intent with the Accords Desk prior to the casting of said enchantment. Such notices must clearly delineate the scope of the blessing to ensure it does not infringe upon the existing magical protections or established trade rights of the aforementioned rival. If a blessing is sold as a means to "outshine" a competitor without specific naming, it remains a permissible act of promotion, provided it does not utilize prohibited schools of magic as defined in § 1.6. However, the moment a practitioner employs a binding oath or a persistent enchantment that actively suppresses the rival's ability to conduct business—such as a "Curse of Diminished Appeal" or a "Ward of Consumer Aversion"—the act shall be reclassified as fraudulent conduct.

Fraud, as defined under § 1001.1, occurs when a magical effect is deployed with the intent to deceive the public or to create an artificial monopoly through coercive arcane means. A blessing that binds a customer to a specific vendor by magically inhibiting their ability to seek services from a competitor is a violation of the Accords. Such binding effects are considered predatory and shall be subject to immediate dissolution by the Aegis Magi. Practitioners found guilty of selling such binding blessings shall be liable for restitution to the affected vendor and may face sanctions under § 800.1. Furthermore, any practitioner who knowingly sells a blessing that contains hidden "leash" mechanics—where the blessing provides a benefit to the buyer while simultaneously siphoning mana or influence from a rival—shall be subject to the Paradox Trial for the use of deceptive and destabilizing magic.

The Distinction between legitimate promotion and prohibited fraud rests upon the presence of a "binding" element. If the magic merely encourages a preference, it is a matter of trade; if the magic removes the agency of the consumer or the viability of the rival through persistent, involuntary arcane interference, it is a breach of the Accords. Practitioners are encouraged to consult the Goodstyle Artisans for approved methods of non-binding promotional magic to ensure compliance with these statutes. Any dispute regarding the "competitive reach" of a blessing shall be mediated by Archmage Veyra’s office, though the burden of proof shall rest upon the petitioner to demonstrate that the blessing in question is non-consensual in its suppression of the rival's interests.

sections.title: Transit Stamps
sections.brief: Planar instability surcharge. Archie-related invoices are not a defense.

body.heading: Transit Stamps
body.text:
The Accords Desk hereby establishes the mandatory requirement for Transit Stamps upon any manifestation of translocation magic that crosses established jurisdictional boundaries between the Midlands and neighboring territories. Any mage, regardless of factional affiliation—be it Conservator or Innovator—who utilizes a portal, rift, or teleportation circle to move sentient beings, sentient goods, or significant arcane masses must secure a stamped authorization from the local Aegis Magi before the final weaving of the spell. Failure to produce a valid Transit Stamp at the point of emergence shall result in immediate seizure of the transit vessel or the magical focus used to initiate the movement. The surcharge for these stamps is calculated based on the volume of the displaced space and the inherent magical pressure of the destination.

Furthermore, the Accords Desk explicitly clarifies the liability regarding specific administrative exemptions. It is strictly understood that any invoice, receipt, or correspondence originating from the individual known as Archie Miser shall not constitute a valid defense against the assessment of a Planar Instability Surcharge. While the holder of a Provisional Guild Pass may enjoy certain diplomatic protections regarding the Iron Mandate, such protections do not extend to the fiscal obligations of transit. If a mage attempts to utilize an Archie-related invoice to offset the costs of a planar breach or a high-pressure translocation, the Accords Desk shall deem the invoice null and void for the purposes of this specific surcharge. Mages are encouraged to maintain separate ledgers for political navigation and logistical transit to avoid such clerical complications.

In instances where the destination of a transit is obscured by atmospheric interference or planar shifting, the mage is required to pay a "High-Risk" premium. This premium is levied to compensate the Guild for the potential degradation of the Midlands' ley lines caused by erratic arrivals. See § 1201.2 for rules regarding the evasion of such tolls. Any attempt to bypass the stamping process through the use of "natural" rifts or uncatalogued fissures is strictly prohibited; such actions are to be treated as unauthorized field use and may be subject to the Paradox Trial. Mages found in violation of these requirements may have their translocation foci temporarily bound by the Aegis Magi until all outstanding surcharges are settled in full.

body.heading: Planar Tolls
body.text:
The Accords Desk mandates that all planar tolls must be paid in full prior to the opening of any dimensional aperture. This requirement is designed to ensure that the Guild can maintain the integrity of the Midlands' magical infrastructure against the erosion caused by constant external peering and internal extraction. Mages who attempt to evade these tolls through the use of "Shadow-Leaping" or other clandestine methods of movement are in violation of the Accords. Such evasion is not merely a fiscal offense but a breach of the collective stability maintained by the Conservators. Any mage caught evading a toll shall be subject to immediate detention and a formal inquiry by the Aegis Magi.

Corridor courtesy is a primary tenet of the Accords regarding the use of shared magical conduits. When utilizing established "highways" of mana, mages are expected to maintain a steady flow and avoid "magical drafting," which is the act of riding the wake of another mage's translocation spell to save on personal mana expenditure or toll costs. Drafting is considered a form of theft and shall be prosecuted as such. Mages must maintain a respectful distance from one another during transit to prevent harmonic interference, which can lead to localized reality fractures or the unintended displacement of nearby flora and fauna.

Should a mage find a toll to be exorbitant or the corridor to be under-maintained, they are instructed to file a formal grievance with the Accords Desk rather than attempting to bypass the gate. The Guild does not recognize "self-service" toll reduction. Any mage who attempts to sabotage a toll gate or use a "blanking" spell to hide their transit signature from the Aegis Magi will be flagged for a Paradox Trial. The Guild’s primary objective is the preservation of the Midlands; therefore, the stability of the toll system is paramount. Mages are reminded that the Iron Mandate does not provide any sanctuary for those who violate the internal fiscal codes of the Autumnwood Accords.

body.heading: Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber
body.text:
The Accords Desk strictly prohibits the unauthorized casting of spells into any designated "Diet Chamber" located outside the primary jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords. A Diet Chamber is defined as any consecrated or sequestered space dedicated to the consumption of sustenance, ritualistic feeding, or the preservation of biological matter for consumption. Casting into such a space, particularly when the magic involves transmutation, necromancy, or the alteration of biological properties, is considered a severe violation of the sanctity of the Midlands' social order. Such actions are often associated with the illicit practices of the Silver Flame or the forbidden schools monitored by Archmage Theron.

Mages who believe they have a legitimate requirement to interact with a Diet Chamber—such as for the purpose of large-scale banquet enchantment or the preservation of perishable goods for a public festival—must not cast directly into the chamber. Instead, the mage shall be required to file a formal Letter of Intent with the local Aegis Magi at least forty-eight hours prior to the intended casting. This letter must detail the specific spells to be used, the expected duration of the enchantment, and the names of the primary casters. Once the letter is filed and approved, a temporary permit will be issued, allowing for the supervised execution of the magic.

Direct casting into a Diet Chamber without a filed letter will result in the immediate seizure of the mage's focus and a mandatory appearance before the Council of Peers for a Paradox Trial. The Guild takes these restrictions seriously to prevent the contamination of food supplies and the desecration of sacred feeding grounds. This rule applies regardless of whether the chamber is public or private. Mages are cautioned that "minor" charms intended to enhance flavor or temperature are still subject to these filing requirements if they involve the fundamental alteration of the food's essence. For questions regarding the specific wording of a Letter of Intent, mages may consult the archives of the Conservators.

body.heading: Cartography Sold as a License to Raid
body.text:
The Accords Desk hereby clarifies the legal distinction between the possession of a map and the authorization of a magical operation. It is a strictly enforced rule that any cartographic document, including those of the One-T mountain range or other high-altitude regions, is classified solely as a navigational aid. The mere possession of a map, regardless of its detail, provenance, or the inclusion of marked "points of interest," does not constitute a license to raid, mine, or perform any form of extractive magic in the depicted area. Mages who attempt to use a map as a "permit" to enter restricted zones or to conduct unauthorized field research shall be held liable for trespassing and unauthorized arcane interference.

Mages are reminded that the One-T mountain is a site of significant geological and magical sensitivity. The use of "One-T cartography" as a justification for entering the peaks without a specific Expedition Permit is a violation of the Accords. A map shows where a mage *can* go; it does not grant the right to *do* anything once they arrive. Any mage found in possession of a map who is subsequently caught engaging in unauthorized "raid" behavior—defined as the organized extraction of minerals, relics, or mana-rich flora—will be subject to immediate arrest by the Aegis Magi. The Guild will not recognize the "exploration" defense as a valid excuse for the violation of territorial boundaries.

Furthermore, the sale of maps by Goodstyle Artisans or other licensed merchants is encouraged, but these sales are not tied to any underlying rights of access. If a mage purchases a map of a restricted zone, they are still bound by the same restrictions as any other unaffiliated traveler. To obtain a license to raid or perform research in such areas, the mage must petition the Innovators for a research grant or the Conservators for a stability clearance, depending on the nature of the activity. A map is a map; it is not a key, a shield, or a license. Any attempt to conflate the two in a legal defense shall be dismissed by the Accords Desk without prejudice.

sections.title: Planar Tolls
sections.brief: Evasion. Corridor courtesy.

body.heading: Planar Tolls
body.text:
Evasion. Corridor courtesy.

Pursuant to the jurisdictional oversight established under the Autumnwood Accords, all mages who facilitate the transit of sentient beings, goods, or essence across planar boundaries shall be held strictly liable for the payment of designated Planar Tolls. The Accords Desk maintains that the stabilization of the Midlands’ local reality necessitates a standardized taxation of inter-planar flux. Any mage who utilizes a rift, gateway, or dimensional fold to bypass these established checkpoints shall be deemed in violation of the Accord. Such evasion is categorized as a breach of corridor courtesy, as it places an undue burden on the structural integrity of the local weave and risks the degradation of the surrounding geography. All transit fees are to be calculated by the volume of mana displaced and the duration of the aperture maintained.

Mages seeking to move assets across planes must consult the current schedules maintained by the Accords Desk. Failure to declare a planned transit prior to activation may result in the immediate seizure of the traveling assets by the Aegis Magi. Furthermore, any mage who intentionally obscures the nature of their cargo to circumvent toll assessment shall face a formal inquiry. The Accords Desk emphasizes that "corridor courtesy" is not merely a social suggestion but a legal requirement for the continued stability of the Midlands. Mages who refuse to acknowledge the necessity of these tolls are viewed as contributing to the entropy of the realm. See § 1.2 for the overarching authority of the Accords Desk in matters of inter-planar regulation.

Regarding the physical maintenance of transit points, any mage who creates a temporary rift or gateway is responsible for the immediate stabilization of the exit point. If a gateway results in structural damage to the local environment—be it cracked stone, scorched earth, or lingering arcane radiation—the initiating mage is liable for all repair costs. This includes the hiring of Goodstyle Artisans for physical reconstruction if the damage exceeds minor surface abrasions. If the exit point is located within a public thoroughfare, the mage must ensure that no debris or residual mana lingers for more than one standard hour. Failure to clear the "corridor" of magical residue is a violation of local ordinances and shall be prosecuted as a public nuisance.

In instances where a planar toll cannot be paid due to the immediate threat of a predatory entity or an imminent collapse of the rift, a "Force Majeure" petition must be filed with the Accords Desk within three days of the event. Until such a petition is granted, the mage remains liable for the full toll. The Accords Desk reserves the right to levy additional penalties for any mage who repeatedly utilizes "emergency" exemptions to avoid their fiscal obligations to the Guild. For further details on the classification of planar entities and their associated toll rates, see § 1201.1.

body.heading: Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber
body.text:
Do not. File a letter instead.

The Autumnwood Accords strictly prohibit the direct casting of offensive, transformative, or high-variance magic into any designated "Diet Chamber" or sanctuary of sustenance. A Diet Chamber is defined as any consecrated or secular space dedicated to the preparation, storage, or consumption of food and drink, where the sanctity of the meal is protected from arcane interference. This prohibition is absolute and applies regardless of the location of the casting. A mage who casts a spell into such a chamber—whether for the purpose of preservation, flavor enhancement, or hostile disruption—shall be subject to immediate sanctions under the Paradox Trial. The Guild recognizes that the integrity of sustenance is a fundamental pillar of civil stability; to corrupt a meal is to corrupt the social fabric of the Midlands.

Mages who find it necessary to alter the properties of food or drink through arcane means must do so via the approved "Sanctified Modification" process. This process requires the mage to submit a formal request to the Accords Desk for a specific permit. Once the permit is granted, the mage may proceed with the modification, provided they do not exceed the parameters outlined in the approved petition. If a mage believes that a Diet Chamber requires a permanent arcane enhancement, they are strictly forbidden from casting such a spell directly into the chamber. Instead, the mage shall draft and file a formal letter of intent with the Accords Desk, detailing the desired outcome, the safety measures to be employed, and the intended duration of the effect.

The filing of a letter of intent allows the Conservators and Innovators to review the proposed magic for potential risks to the local weave and the safety of the consumers. If the request is denied, the mage must seek an alternative method of modification that does not involve direct casting into the sanctuary. Any mage caught casting into a Diet Chamber without a filed letter and a corresponding permit shall be apprehended by the Aegis Magi. The penalty for such an act shall be determined by the severity of the contamination; minor alterations may result in a fine, while the corruption of a communal feast or the poisoning of a public well may result in a full Seal of Silence or a transition to a pocket-prison.

Furthermore, this regulation extends to the "flavoring" of beverages with ephemeral magic. While the Innovators may argue for the creative freedom of such arts, the Conservators maintain that the unpredictable nature of such magic can lead to unintended physiological consequences for the consumer. Therefore, all "flavor-casting" must be documented and the ingredients of the magic must be disclosed to the Guild. Mages who refuse to file the necessary paperwork for their culinary enchantments are considered to be acting in bad faith against the Accords. For guidance on the submission of formal letters to the Desk, see § 900.1.

body.heading: Cartography Sold as a License to Raid
body.text:
One-T mountain. A map is a map. It is not a permit.

The Accords Desk hereby clarifies the legal distinction between the acquisition of geographical data and the authorization of martial action. It is a frequent point of contention among the Innovators that the possession of a detailed map of a restricted area, such as the One-T mountain or other contested territories, constitutes a tacit permission to explore or occupy said region. This is a legal fallacy. Under the Autumnwood Accords, a map is merely a record of topographical and arcane data; it confers no rights of passage, no license to harvest resources, and no permit to engage in hostile action. A mage who purchases or commissions a map of a restricted zone is merely acquiring information. The use of that information to bypass Guild-sanctioned boundaries or to initiate a raid is a separate and punishable offense.

Mages who intend to enter restricted territories for the purpose of research, trade, or exploration must secure a formal "Field Expedition Permit" from the Accords Desk. This permit must be filed well in advance and must specify the duration of the stay, the number of participants, and the intended scope of activity. The possession of a map, even a high-fidelity one provided by a Goodstyle Artisan, does not exempt the mage from this requirement. Should a mage be intercepted by the Aegis Magi while in a restricted zone, the mere possession of a map shall not serve as a defense. The mage must produce a valid, stamped Expedition Permit to avoid immediate detention and potential referral to a Paradox Trial.

Furthermore, the sale of maps that include "tactical notations"—such as identified weak points in defenses, hidden ingress points, or unguarded resource deposits—is strictly regulated. Such maps are classified as "Sensitive Intelligence" and may only be sold to Guild-affiliated entities with the express permission of Archmage Veyra. Any third party caught selling such maps to non-Guild actors, including the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion, shall be prosecuted for espionage. The Accords Desk reminds all mages that while knowledge is power, the unauthorized application of that knowledge in a manner that threatens the stability of the Midlands is a breach of the Accord.

In the event that a mage discovers a new geographical feature or a previously unmapped rift during a sanctioned expedition, they are required to report these findings to the Accords Desk within forty-eight hours. Failure to report new data, or the deliberate withholding of such information for private gain, is a violation of the Guild's data-sharing protocols. A map is a tool for navigation; a permit is a tool for legality. The two are not interchangeable. Mages who attempt to use the "I only had a map" defense during a seizure of assets shall be subject to the maximum fines as outlined in § 1001.4. For information on obtaining a Field Expedition Permit, see § 900.2.

sections.title: Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber
sections.brief: Do not. File a letter instead.

body.heading: Extraterritorial Casting into a Diet Chamber
body.text:
Any practitioner of the arcane who intends to project, manifest, or otherwise exert magical influence upon a designated Diet Chamber—defined as a consecrated space for the consumption of sustenance by non-magical entities or for the communal nourishment of those under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords—is strictly prohibited from performing such actions if the target chamber exists outside the immediate terrestrial boundaries of the Midlands. This prohibition is absolute and applies to all schools of magic, including but not limited to transmutation of food, telekinetic delivery of beverages, or any atmospheric manipulation intended to enhance the olfactory profile of a meal. The Guild recognizes that while the logistical needs of travelers and diplomats are significant, the risk of cross-planar contamination, unintended caloric inflation, or the disruption of local culinary sanctity outweighs any perceived convenience of such remote casting.

Furthermore, any mage found in violation of this clause shall be subject to immediate review by the Aegis Magi. The intent of the caster is irrelevant; the mere act of reaching across a jurisdictional boundary to influence a dining environment constitutes a breach of the Accords. This is particularly relevant when dealing with the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion, as their culinary standards are considered sovereign and their reactions to unsolicited magical intervention are often hostile. Mages seeking to provide logistical support to allies, such as the Goodstyle Artisans, must ensure that all such services are performed within the physical vicinity of the recipient. If a request for remote nourishment arises, the mage shall not utilize arcana to bridge the distance.

In instances where a mage feels compelled to provide sustenance to a party in a remote location, they are hereby commanded to forgo all magical intervention and instead utilize traditional courier methods. See § 1201.1 regarding transit stamps for such couriers. If the distance is prohibitive for physical transit, the mage may instead draft a formal letter of intent and request that the local authorities or the host party arrange for local procurement. This letter must be filed with the Accords Desk and bear the official seal of the caster’s faction, be it Conservator or Innovator. No exceptions shall be granted for "emergency" hunger, provided the emergency was not caused by the mage's own failure to plan for sufficient supplies. Failure to comply with this directive will result in a referral to the Paradox Trial for review of the caster's stability.

body.heading: Cartography Sold as a License to Raid
body.text:
The production, sale, and distribution of topographical records, hereafter referred to as Cartography, are governed by the principles of objective observation. It is strictly forbidden for any Cartographer, Merchant, or Mage to represent a map of a geographical feature—specifically the One-T mountain range or any similar landmark—as a license, permit, or authorization to engage in "raiding," "looting," or "resource extraction." A map is a tool of navigation and spatial awareness; it confers no legal right to the contents of the terrain it depicts. Any individual attempting to sell a map with the express intent of implying it grants the bearer permission to bypass local defenses or enter restricted zones is committing a felony of Deception under the Accords.

The Guild finds that the "One-T mountain" has been the subject of frequent confusion regarding its status. While the map of the mountain is a public utility for those seeking to traverse the Midlands, the mountain itself remains subject to the laws of the presiding sovereign or the territorial claims of the dominant faction. The presence of a map in a traveler's possession does not mitigate the penalties associated with trespassing or the unauthorized seizure of materials. If a mage or adventurer intends to conduct a raid, they must secure a formal Raid License from the appropriate regional authority. A map is not a substitute for a license, and the sale of a map as such shall be treated as a fraudulent transaction, subject to the penalties outlined in § 1001.1.

Furthermore, the Cartography Department of the Accords Desk warns that the sale of "Tactical Maps" which include notations on "weak points" or "unprotected entrances" does not exempt the buyer from the consequences of an assault. Such notations are considered descriptive, not permissive. If a mage is caught utilizing a map to conduct an unauthorized raid, the map itself may be seized as evidence of premeditation. Practitioners of the Innovator faction are specifically cautioned against creating "dynamic maps" that update in real-time to show the movements of guards or the location of hidden caches, as these may be classified as forbidden surveillance tools. For all matters regarding the legal acquisition of land or the right to harvest resources, mages must consult the proper civic channels rather than relying on the mere possession of a parchment.

sections.title: Cartography Sold as a License to Raid
sections.brief: One-T mountain. A map is a map. It is not a permit.

body.heading: Cartography Sold as a License to Raid
body.text:
The Autumnwood Accords, as mediated by Archmage Veyra, maintain a strict distinction between the acquisition of geographical knowledge and the authorization of hostile incursions. It is a fundamental principle of the Accords that the possession of a map, regardless of its detail, historical depth, or the arcane means by which it was compiled, does not constitute a legal license for the seizure, pillaging, or tactical engagement within the designated territory. This distinction is particularly critical regarding the One-T mountain range, where historical precedents of unauthorized "treasure expeditions" have led to significant ecological and arcane destabilization. Any individual, entity, or guild-affiliated party found to be asserting that a purchased map grants them sovereign right of entry for the purpose of raiding shall be subject to immediate summary citation.

The Accords Desk hereby clarifies that cartography is a scholarly pursuit and a tool for navigation, not a instrument of martial permission. Under these statutes, a map serves only to define the physical boundaries of a landmass; it does not supersede the territorial rights of the local inhabitants, the sovereign claims of the regional powers, or the environmental preservation mandates established by the Conservators. Any entity attempting to use the purchase of a One-T mountain chart as a justification for bypassing the standard requisitioning process for exploration shall be deemed to be in violation of the peace. The presence of a map in one's possession shall not be admitted as evidence of "prior consent" from the land's overseers.

Furthermore, the Guild warns against the illicit sale of "Raid Licenses" disguised as topographical scrolls. Merchants or clandestine brokers who market maps with clauses implying permission to enter restricted zones, extract resources, or engage in combat are in direct violation of the Accords. Such sales are considered fraudulent and may lead to the seizure of the maps in question and the revocation of the seller's mercantile privileges. The Accords Desk recognizes that the One-T mountain range is a sensitive zone; therefore, any expeditionary force must secure a formal Permit of Incursion from the appropriate regional authority. A map is a representation of the world, not a key to its secrets.

Mages and explorers who rely on the "Cartographic Exemption"—the notion that a map provides a legal shield against charges of trespassing or looting—shall find such defenses void. If a party is apprehended within the One-T mountains without a valid, stamped Permit of Incursion, the mere production of a map shall not serve as a mitigating factor in their sentencing. The Aegis Magi are instructed to prioritize the apprehension of those who use "exploratory intent" as a veneer for unauthorized raiding. See § 1.2 for matters regarding the enacting authority of the Accords Desk. All parties seeking to survey the One-T range are reminded that one-T cartography is a map, not a raid license.

sections.title: Schedule of Fees
sections.brief: Named amounts in Guild marks. No Wario Coin.

body.heading: Schedule of Fees
body.text:
The Guild shall maintain a definitive schedule of fees for all administrative, investigative, and regulatory actions performed by the Accords Desk. These fees are established to ensure the continued maintenance of the Autumnwood infrastructure and to compensate the Guild for the oversight of arcane stability. All fees must be rendered in standard Guild marks. The Guild hereby declares that any currency of irregular origin, including but not limited to the Wario Coin, is not a valid tender for the settlement of debts, fines, or administrative costs. Any attempt to utilize non-standard coinage in the settlement of a Guild fee shall result in the immediate rejection of the tender and the assessment of a secondary "Invalid Tender" surcharge as dictated by the current fiscal year's guidelines.

Fees are categorized by the severity of the violation and the complexity of the requested service. Administrative services, such as the filing of a Provisional Guild Pass or the registration of a new cartographic survey, are subject to a fixed entry fee. Investigative services, including the surveying of a Heartstone or the verification of a rift's boundaries, are billed at a rate commensurate with the risk of planar instability. All fees are non-refundable once the Accords Desk has initiated the requested procedure. See § 1301.1.

The Guild reserves the right to adjust the Schedule of Fees with a notice period of no less than three lunar cycles. Such adjustments shall be mediated by Archmage Veyra to ensure that the balance between Conservator traditionalism and Innovator expansionism is maintained in the economic health of the Guild. No individual mage, regardless of rank or factional standing, is exempt from these fees unless a formal waiver is granted by the Archmage Sovereign. Failure to pay fees within the allotted timeframe shall result in the suspension of the mage's right to perform authorized research or transit within the Midlands.

body.heading: Penalties; Sunrise Accrual
body.text:
All penalties, fines, and interest accrued on outstanding debts to the Guild shall be calculated based on the temporal flow of the original time zone, specifically the standard time of the Autumnwood region. This provision is enacted to prevent mages from utilizing temporal manipulation, pocket dimensions, or chronal displacement to stall the accumulation of penalties. A mage who is incarcerated within a pocket-prison or a sealed ward does not enjoy a "temporal reprieve." The Accords Desk shall calculate the duration of the penalty based on the time elapsed in the Midlands, regardless of how many years or seconds may pass within the confined space of the sanction.

The accrual of penalties begins at the moment of the initial violation or the issuance of a formal summons by the Aegis Magi. If a mage remains in a state of non-compliance, the penalty shall increase at a fixed rate per sunrise as observed in the Autumnwood. This ensures that the Guild's interests are protected against the exploitation of "slow-time" environments. See § 800.5 for specific procedures regarding the maintenance of pocket-prisons.

Any attempt to argue for a "subjective time" calculation based on the experience of the offender is strictly prohibited. The Guild maintains that the preservation of the Accords is a matter of objective reality. Should a mage attempt to use high-level chronomancy to circumvent these accruals, such an act shall be considered a Grade-A violation of the stability protocols, punishable by an immediate and permanent sealing of the offending arcane circuits. The Accords Desk shall provide a weekly statement of accrued penalties to any mage currently under sanction, ensuring transparency in the calculation of the debt.

body.heading: Appeals
body.text:
Any mage who believes a ruling of the Accords Desk to be in error may initiate a formal appeal process. The first stage of appeal resides solely with the Accords Desk. The Clerk shall review the filing for procedural correctness and ensure that all required documentation, including any relevant one-T cartography and proof of identity, has been submitted. If the Clerk finds the appeal has merit, the matter may be elevated for internal review. This stage is intended to resolve clerical errors, misunderstandings of the written word, or minor disputes regarding the interpretation of the Schedule of Fees.

If the appeal is denied at the Desk level, the mage may request a transition to the Paradox Trial. This is a formal judicial proceeding where the mage's peers shall sit in judgment. The Paradox Trial is the ultimate arbiter of the Guild's internal laws. During this process, the facts of the case are presented to the council, who may choose to uphold, vacate, or modify the original ruling. The Paradox Trial may result in various outcomes, including the sealing of magic, the issuance of a new mandate, or the confirmation of the original penalty. See § 800.4 for the conversion of duel stakes into fees during such proceedings.

Once a decision is rendered by the Paradox Trial, it is considered final and binding. There is no further mechanism for appeal within the Guild's jurisdiction. The Guild does not provide a secondary court of appeals, and any attempt to seek further adjudication through external means—such as the courts of the Regal Empire or the laws of the Iron Mandate—shall be viewed as an act of secession and a violation of the Autumnwood Accords. Mages are advised to ensure their appeals are well-reasoned and supported by evidence, as the path to "nowhere useful" begins once the Paradox Trial concludes.

body.heading: Who May Inspect
body.text:
Access to the internal records of the Accords Desk, the physical archives of the Autumnwood, and the sensitive logs of the Quiet List is strictly restricted. Only authorized Clerks of the Accords Desk and named officers of the Guild may enter these areas for the purpose of official business. This restriction is designed to protect the privacy of the mages, the integrity of the Guild's secrets, and the security of the Midlands from external threats such as the Silver Flame or the Cosmic Jesters.

No member of the general public, including non-affiliated mages, may request an inspection of the archives without a signed warrant from Archmage Veyra. Furthermore, "crowd" inspections are strictly prohibited. Even in the event of a formal inquiry, the inspection shall be conducted by a designated small group of officials rather than a public gathering. This prevents the unauthorized dissemination of information regarding the Quiet List and ensures that the delicate balance of the Guild's internal politics remains undisturbed by outside scrutiny.

Mages who are granted "Provisional Guild Passes" for political reasons, such as those held by Archie Miser, are not granted automatic inspection rights. Their access is limited to the specific documents required for their current diplomatic engagement and may be revoked at any moment by the Aegis Magi. Any unauthorized individual found attempting to peer into the archives or overhear the deliberations of the Desk shall be subject to immediate detention and a formal review for a Paradox Trial. Security is paramount; the Guild's secrets are the foundation of its power, and their preservation is the primary duty of every Clerk.

sections.title: Penalties; Sunrise Accrual
sections.brief: Original time zone, not the pocket's.

body.heading: Penalties; Sunrise Accrual
body.text:
Any punitive measures, fines, or temporal sanctions levied by the Autumnwood Accords Desk against a practitioner found in violation of these statutes shall be calculated based upon the temporal progression of the practitioner’s point of origin. This principle of Sunrise Accrual ensures that the Guild maintains a consistent standard of justice that is not subject to the manipulation of localized chronomancy or the dilation of extra-planar environments. When a mage is detained within a pocket-prison, a localized rift, or any other magically-induced sub-dimension where the flow of time deviates from the standard progression of the Midlands, the duration of the penalty shall be measured by the sunrises occurring in the practitioner’s home jurisdiction at the time of the offense.

The Guild explicitly rejects the "subjective duration" defense. A practitioner who remains in a state of stasis for what they perceive to be a mere hour, but which constitutes a century of elapsed time in the Midlands, shall be held liable for the full century of accrued penalties. Conversely, a practitioner who utilizes a time-dilated pocket-dimension to attempt to "outlast" a sentence shall find that the Accords Desk recognizes only the progression of the external world. This provision serves to prevent the evasion of justice through the use of sophisticated chronometric shielding or the exploitation of natural anomalies. See § 1.2 for the enacting authority of these calculations.

Furthermore, the calculation of interest on outstanding magical debts or the duration of "Seal and Silence" sanctions shall be reconciled at the moment of the first sunrise following the initial infraction. If a practitioner is currently located in a region where the sun does not rise—such as the deep subterranean vaults or certain high-altitude celestial rifts—the Accords Desk shall defer to the nearest recognized terrestrial municipality that adheres to the Midlands standard. The goal of the Sunrise Accrual is to ensure that the cost of magical delinquency remains proportional to the impact of the crime upon the stability of the Autumnwood Accords, rather than the convenience of the offender's current location.

body.heading: Appeals
body.text:
The right to appeal a ruling issued by the Accords Desk is a fundamental prerogative of any licensed practitioner, provided such a request is filed within three lunar cycles of the initial judgment. The primary venue for such appeals is the Desk itself, wherein the presiding Clerk shall review the filing for procedural errors, misinterpretations of the Accords, or evidence of clerical oversight. The Desk maintains the authority to vacate a penalty or issue a stay of execution should it be determined that the original ruling was inconsistent with the prevailing mediation of Archmage Veyra or the established precedents of the Conservators.

Should the Desk uphold its original ruling, the practitioner may petition for a formal Paradox Trial. This is the highest level of judicial review within the Guild’s jurisdiction. A Paradox Trial involves a council of peers—selected from both the Conservator and Innovator factions—who shall determine the validity of the original charge through a process of magical arbitration. During these proceedings, the accused may present a defense, and the council may demand the presentation of artifacts, spell-scrolls, or testimonies. The outcome of a Paradox Trial is final and binding; it represents the ultimate consensus of the Guild’s magical community.

Be it known that there is no further recourse beyond the Paradox Trial. Once the peer council has rendered its verdict, the decision is considered absolute and immutable. No further petitions, grievances, or appeals may be filed with the Accords Desk, the Office of the Archmage, or the Aegis Magi regarding the specific matter at hand. To attempt to seek a higher court of law outside the Guild’s jurisdiction is to forfeit all remaining protections afforded by the Accords. Practitioners are cautioned that seeking "external" justice—particularly from the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion—will result in the immediate revocation of their Guild standing and the permanent sealing of their arcane signature. See § 800.5 for the specific procedures regarding the enforcement of these final judgments.

body.heading: Who May Inspect
body.text:
The sanctity of the Archives and the privacy of the practitioner’s registered magical laboratory are upheld by the principle of Restricted Access. Only authorized personnel of the Autumnwood Accords are permitted to conduct formal inspections of any site where restricted research is being conducted or where a magical artifact of significant provenance is being held. These inspectors are strictly limited to active Clerks of the Accords Desk and named Officers of the Aegis Magi. Any individual not holding a verified Guild Seal of Inspection may be barred from entry at the discretion of the site’s primary licensee.

Under no circumstances shall a public inspection be permitted. The Guild recognizes that the exposure of experimental methodologies—particularly those pursued by the Innovators—could lead to the unintended dissemination of volatile arcana or the compromise of the Quiet List. A crowd, including non-practitioners, journalists, or unauthorized observers, is strictly prohibited from entering any zone designated for inspection. Should a practitioner fail to grant access to a named Officer of the Aegis Magi during a scheduled audit, they shall be subject to immediate summary fines and a potential referral for a Paradox Trial.

In cases where a practitioner is under active investigation for a violation of the Iron Mandate or other rival laws, the Accords Desk may grant temporary inspection rights to designated mediators, provided these mediators are bound by a non-disclosure oath. However, these rights do not extend to the general populace or to representatives of the Silver Flame or the Cosmic Jesters. Any unauthorized breach of a laboratory or archive by a non-Guild entity shall be treated as an act of hostility against the Accords. See § 900.1 for the requirements regarding the filing of notice before any authorized inspection commences.

sections.title: Appeals
sections.brief: Desk, then Paradox Trial, then nowhere useful.

body.heading: Appeals
body.text:
Any mage, practitioner, or entity aggrieved by a final determination issued by the Accords Desk may initiate a formal petition for review under the provisions of § 1301.3. The primary venue for such a grievance remains the Accords Desk itself, where the presiding Clerk shall review the administrative record to ensure that the original ruling was rendered in strict accordance with the Autumnwood Accords. This initial review is a matter of procedural integrity; the Desk shall not re-litigate the underlying merits of the magical variance or the specificities of the arcane transgression, but shall instead determine if the Desk's own internal protocols were violated during the initial adjudication. If the Clerk finds that the record is complete and the procedure was followed, the petition shall be denied, and the ruling shall stand as a matter of administrative finality.

Should the petitioner maintain that the Desk’s procedural determination is fundamentally flawed or that a grave miscarriage of arcane justice has occurred, the matter may be elevated to a formal Paradox Trial. Pursuant to § 800.2, a Paradox Trial shall be convened by a council of peers selected from the relevant faction—be it the Conservators or the Innovators—depending on the nature of the original charge. During this phase, the peer council shall examine the substantive evidence, the efficacy of the seals applied, and the proportionality of the sanctions imposed. The trial by peers serves as the highest deliberative body within the Guild's legal framework, intended to balance the traditionalist requirements of Archmage Theron with the research liberties championed by Janna Brightspark.

Upon the conclusion of a Paradox Trial, the verdict rendered by the peer council is considered absolute and binding. There is no further mechanism for appeal within the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords. The Guild recognizes that the paradoxes of magic are inherently volatile; therefore, the legal system must eventually reach a point of closure to prevent infinite recursive litigation. Once a Paradox Trial has concluded, the petitioner is advised that the matter is closed. Any attempt to seek further redress outside of the Guild’s established legal channels shall be viewed as an act of defiance against the Accords. The law provides no further sanctuary for those who seek to endlessly contest the sovereign mediation of Archmage Veyra. See § 1301.2 for penalty accruals.

body.heading: Who May Inspect
body.text:
The sanctity of the Accords Desk and the confidentiality of its archives are paramount to the stability of the Midlands. Consequently, access to the internal records, active dockets, and the physical premises of the Accords Desk is strictly limited to authorized personnel. Only a designated Clerk of the Desk, as defined in § 100.1, possesses the standing to enter the archives and handle the primary ledgers. These Clerks are the sole custodians of the Guild's legal history and are tasked with ensuring that no unauthorized magical signatures or mundane intrusions compromise the integrity of the bound codes.

Furthermore, inspection of specific dockets or the status of a pending Paradox Trial may be granted to named officers of the Guild. These officers must be explicitly identified in a written requisition and must possess a high-level clearance granted by the Archmage Sovereign. Such access is granted only on a need-to-know basis, typically for the purposes of enforcement by the Aegis Magi or for high-level mediation by Archmage Veyra. No individual, regardless of their rank within the Conservator or Innovator factions, may demand a general inspection of the archives without a specific warrant signed by the presiding Archmage.

The public, including unaffiliated mages, traveling merchants, and members of the Goodstyle Artisans, are strictly prohibited from entering the Accords Desk or attempting to inspect the Guild's private records. No crowd, assembly, or group of observers shall be permitted to view the proceedings of the Desk or the contents of the archive. Any attempt to breach this perimeter or to solicit information from a Clerk regarding the Quiet List or other sensitive records shall be met with immediate summary expulsion. Violations of this inspection protocol may result in the immediate revocation of a Provisional Guild Pass or the initiation of a Paradox Trial for interference with Guild sovereignty. See § 900.3 for record retention limits.

sections.title: Who May Inspect
sections.brief: Clerks, named officers. Not a crowd.

body.heading: Who May Inspect
body.text:
The authority to conduct physical, metaphysical, or administrative inspections of Guild-sanctioned properties, research laboratories, and personal vaults held under the jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords is strictly limited to designated personnel. The Guild maintains that the integrity of arcane research and the safety of the public rely upon a controlled environment where the presence of unauthorized observers could lead to the contamination of magical signatures, the theft of intellectual property, or the accidental triggering of volatile enchantments. Consequently, any individual seeking to enter a site of restricted research or to audit a ledger of magical assets must be formally recognized by the Accords Desk as an authorized inspector.

Under the provisions of the Autumnwood Accords, only Clerks of the Accords Desk and named officers of the Aegis Magi possess the standing to conduct such inspections. This includes, but is not limited to, high-ranking members of the Conservator and Innovator factions who have been granted specific, time-bound mandates by Archmage Veyra. These officers must present their official seals and a signed warrant of inspection upon arrival at any site. The presence of a named officer does not grant an inherent right of entry to their subordinates; rather, only those individuals explicitly named in the writ of inspection may cross the threshold of the designated area. Any officer who permits an unnamed individual to accompany them into a restricted zone shall be held personally liable for any breach of security, as defined in § 1301.2.

The prohibition against public inspection is absolute. No crowd, group of commoners, religious congregation, or unauthorized body of mages may gather to demand a viewing of Guild archives, research facilities, or private magical holdings. The Guild acknowledges the public's interest in the safety of the Midlands, yet maintains that the nuances of arcane regulation are not suited for public consumption. Any attempt to organize a mass inspection or a "public viewing" of a restricted site shall be deemed an act of civil unrest and may be met with the immediate deployment of the Aegis Magi to disperse the assembly. Furthermore, the mere presence of a crowd in the vicinity of an active inspection site may result in the immediate suspension of the inspection and a filing of grievances against the organizers.

Furthermore, the Guild clarifies that "public interest" does not constitute a legal basis for the bypass of these restrictions. While the Goodstyle Artisans may occasionally request collaborative oversight of specific craftsmanship projects, such requests must still be processed through the standard petitioning system and result in a formal appointment of a specific, named inspector. The Guild shall not be compelled to provide access to any individual who does not hold the requisite rank or specific designation within the Accords. Any violation of these protocols, including the unauthorized recording of an inspection or the covert observation of a Clerk performing their duties, shall be subject to the penalties outlined in § 1301.2. See § 100.1 for the list of authorized offices and titles.

sections.title: Historical Annotations; Form
sections.brief: How to write C.C.D. numbers, MR pages, weekdays.

body.heading: Historical Annotations; Form
body.text:
The formal recording of historical annotations within the Autumnwood Accords requires strict adherence to the chronological and archival standards established by the Accords Desk. All annotations pertaining to the evolution of magical law, the shifting boundaries of the Forbidden Schools, or the legislative history of the Innovator and Conservator factions must be inscribed using the C.C.D. numbering system. This system serves as the primary indexing method for all legislative evolution. A C.C.D. number shall consist of a three-digit prefix denoting the primary category of the decree, followed by a period and a four-digit sequence identifying the specific chronological entry. Failure to utilize the correct C.C.D. sequence may result in an annotation being rendered legally invisible to the Aegis Magi, thereby stripping the historical context from the active statute.

Furthermore, all annotations must include a corresponding MR page reference. The MR page denotes the specific archival leaf in the Midlands repository where the original parchment or scroll of the decree is housed. When a mage or clerk references a change in the Accords, they must provide both the C.C.D. number for the current legal standing and the MR page for the foundational text. This dual-referencing ensures that the current interpretation of the law remains tethered to its historical origin. Any annotation that fails to provide a valid MR page shall be deemed a "floating decree" and may be struck from the record during the next biennial audit.

The recording of weekdays is also mandatory for all annotations concerning specific events, such as the Paradox Trials or the formal signing of the Accords. The weekday must be recorded in the standard liturgical format of the Midlands. This requirement exists to prevent the retroactive manipulation of timelines, a risk inherent in the high-level chronomancy practiced by some radical Innovators. If a decree was enacted on a Tuesday, it must be noted as such; any attempt to rewrite the day of enactment to suit a political agenda shall be grounds for immediate prosecution under the Paradox Trial protocols. Clerks shall ensure that all entries are written in permanent ink, and any alterations to the C.C.D. numbers or MR pages must be initialed by both a Conservator representative and an Innovator representative to ensure bipartisan verification. See § 1.2 for the enacting authority of these forms.

body.heading: Dead Citations
body.text:
A repealed section of the Autumnwood Accords may be cited as historical context, scholarly precedent, or cultural lore, but it shall never be cited as a valid permit, license, or justification for contemporary magical conduct. The expiration of a statute does not erase its existence from the collective memory of the Guild, nor does it strip the text of its descriptive power. However, the legal weight of a repealed section is extinguished the moment the Accords Desk issues a formal notice of repeal. A mage who attempts to perform a ritual or conduct research by citing a defunct law—claiming that the "old ways" still hold authority—shall be found in violation of the Accords. Such an act is considered a deliberate attempt to circumvent the current oversight of Archmage Veyra and the presiding councils.

The distinction between historical citation and legal application is paramount. For instance, a mage may study the historical records of the Forbidden Schools to understand the dangers of necromancy; however, they may not use those records to argue that the prohibition on such magic was once relaxed and therefore remains valid. The Accords Desk maintains a "Graveyard of Statutes" where these repealed sections are stored. While they are available for study by licensed researchers—provided they have the express permission of the Innovators—they possess no power to grant rights or waive duties. Any petition for a magical variance that relies upon the authority of a dead citation will be summarily rejected without a hearing.

Furthermore, the use of dead citations in public discourse, particularly in taverns or common areas, is strictly regulated. While a scholar may discuss the history of the Accords, they must clearly preface such discussions with the "Historical Notice" disclaimer to ensure the public does not mistake old law for current mandate. The Aegis Magi are instructed to monitor for any attempts to weaponize defunct laws against the Guild's current standing. If a peer is found to be actively advocating for the restoration of a repealed school or practice by citing it as a living permit, they shall be subject to the Paradox Trial. See § 1.6 for the general rules of citation.

body.heading: Savings Against the Iron Mandate
body.text:
The jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords is absolute within the Midlands and across all territories where the Guild maintains recognized sovereignty. This title, and all statutes contained herein, shall not be repealed, superseded, or rendered null by the mere existence of the Iron Mandate, nor by any proclamation issued by the Regal Empire, the Iron Legion, or any other external political entity. The Accords are a sovereign magical compact, not a civil contract subject to the whims of secular empires. Should an external power issue a decree that conflicts with the Accords, the Guild shall recognize only the Accords as the governing law for all mages under its protection. Any mage who attempts to obey the Iron Mandate in a manner that violates the Accords shall be deemed to be in breach of their oath to the Guild.

The Guild acknowledges that the Regal Empire and the Iron Legion may exert significant physical and economic pressure upon the Midlands. However, the magical infrastructure of the Accords is independent of the Mandate's administrative reach. No "shouting" by an Empire—whether expressed through military threat, economic sanction, or diplomatic coercion—constitutes a legal mechanism for the alteration of Guild law. The Accords Desk serves as a fortress of legal stability; it does not buckle under the weight of external demands. Mages who are pressured by Imperial agents to surrender their magical rights or to acknowledge the Mandate as a superior legal authority are to report such interactions to Archmage Veyra immediately.

Furthermore, any attempt by the Iron Legion to impose their "Mandate" laws upon the Guild's internal proceedings is to be treated as a hostile act of magical and political aggression. The Guild does not recognize the Iron Mandate as a valid source of magical regulation. While the Guild may engage in trade or diplomacy with entities subject to the Mandate, such interactions must be conducted under the "Foreign Exchange" protocols and must never involve the surrender of the Accords' jurisdiction. The stability of the Midlands depends upon the unwavering nature of these laws; if the Accords were to yield to every external shout, the very fabric of the Guild's authority would unravel. The Accords remain, as always, the primary and final word on the use of magic.

sections.title: Dead Citations
