sections.brief: A repealed section may be cited as history, not as a permit.

body.heading: Dead Citations
body.text:
§ 1401.2 Dead Citations. A repealed section may be cited as history, not as a permit.

The integrity of the Autumnwood Accords rests upon the continuity of its own administrative evolution. It is a fundamental principle of the Accords Desk that the act of legislative repeal does not constitute a retroactive erasure of the facts of the past, nor does it grant a license for the continued application of the repealed substance. When a statute, decree, or sub-clause is struck from the active Codex, it is moved into the state of "Dead Citation." A mage or entity may reference such a section for the purposes of historical analysis, genealogical research of magical doctrine, or the demonstration of prior precedents; however, any attempt to invoke the legal protections, permissions, or obligations contained within that repealed section shall be deemed a nullity. The mere existence of a text in the archives does not grant it the force of law.

Furthermore, the citation of a Dead Citation in a formal petition or a Paradox Trial shall be interpreted by the presiding council as an admission of ignorance regarding current regulations. While the Archivists may allow the inclusion of such citations to provide context for the development of specific schools of magic—particularly those involving the transition from the Conservator-led restrictions to the Innovator-led permissions—the petitioner must explicitly state that the citation is for historical reference only. Any submission that seeks to use a repealed section as a basis for a current legal defense, a request for restricted research, or a claim of immunity shall be summarily dismissed. The Accords Desk shall not be bound by the logic of a defunct law, and the Aegis Magi are instructed to ignore any "rights" claimed under the authority of a Dead Citation.

This distinction is vital for maintaining the stability of the Midlands. If an old law regarding the handling of rift-energy were to be cited as a current permit, it could lead to catastrophic breaches that the current Accords were specifically designed to prevent. Therefore, any scholar seeking to utilize the data of a repealed section must ensure that their application clearly delineates between "historical fact" and "current mandate." See § 1.2 for the authority of the Desk to maintain these distinctions. Failure to comply with this distinction may result in a summary fine or a referral to the Paradox Trial for the willful subversion of current legal reality.

body.heading: Savings Against the Iron Mandate
body.text:
§ 1401.3 Savings Against the Iron Mandate. This title does not repeal itself because an Empire shouted.

The jurisdiction of the Autumnwood Accords is sovereign and absolute within the established boundaries of the Midlands and the territories governed by the Archmage Veyra. It is hereby decreed that the Accords are not subject to the external pressures, declarations, or legislative overreach of the Regal Empire, the Iron Legion, or any other external geopolitical body. Specifically, this title serves as a permanent stay against the "Iron Mandate"—the legal framework imposed by the Empire and the Legion—asserting that the Accords do not recognize the Mandate as a superior legal authority. The Accords Desk shall not, under any circumstances, voluntarily cede its jurisdiction to the Iron Mandate, nor shall it allow the Mandate’s statutes to supersede the Guild’s internal regulations regarding the study of magic, the conduct of mages, or the distribution of magical assets.

Any attempt by external agents, including the Silver Flame or the Cosmic Jesters, to argue that the Accords are superseded by the Mandate due to "geopolitical necessity" or "military cooperation" is strictly prohibited. The Accords are a binding agreement of the magical community, not a treaty of submission. While the Guild may engage in diplomacy with the Regal Empire, such diplomacy does not equate to a legal merger of codes. The Aegis Magi are authorized to use all necessary force to repel any attempt to enforce Mandate-specific laws on Guild grounds or upon any mage currently under the protection of the Accords. Any mage who attempts to "voluntarily" submit to the Iron Mandate while still holding a valid Guild license shall be investigated for potential treason against the Accords and may be subject to a Paradox Trial.

Moreover, the Accords Desk shall not be intimidated by the "shouting" of empires. The mere presence of Iron Legion forces or the threat of Imperial sanctions does not grant the Mandate the power to rewrite the internal laws of the Autumnwood Accords. If a conflict arises between a Mandate decree and an Accord statute, the Accord statute shall prevail in all matters of magical conduct and internal Guild governance. This title ensures that the delicate balance between the Conservators and the Innovators remains undisturbed by the crude legalisms of the outside world. The Guild’s internal friction is its own; the Mandate’s external pressure is a nuisance to be ignored or resisted, but never integrated. See § 1301.2 for the determination of penalties regarding the unauthorized importation of Mandate-governed mandates into the Midlands.

sections.title: Savings Against the Iron Mandate
sections.brief: This title does not repeal itself because an Empire shouted.

body.heading: Savings Against the Iron Mandate
body.text:
It is hereby established by the sovereign authority of the Autumnwood Accords that this Codex of Law remains the primary and binding legal framework for all practitioners of the arcane within the jurisdiction of the Midlands and the territories served by the Guild. The existence of external legislative bodies, specifically those of the Regal Empire or the Iron Legion, shall not constitute a valid mechanism for the revocation, amendment, or repeal of the Accords. Any decree issued by the Iron Legion or the Regal Empire—collectively referred to herein as "External Mandates"—that seeks to supersede, diminish, or nullify the rights and responsibilities of the Guild members is deemed legally void and unenforceable within the sovereign magical space of the Autumnwood.

The Accords recognize that the Iron Mandate, passed by the Midlands Diet on the 21st of Highsun, 1040 BF, represents an emergency measure of secular and martial nature. While the Guild acknowledges the existence of the Iron Legion and the Regal Empire as geopolitical entities, the magical laws governing the manipulation of the Weave, the conduct of the Aegis Magi, and the adjudication of the Paradox Trial are not subject to the whims of secular military authority. No shout from an Emperor, no proclamation from a General, and no emergency decree from a Diet may strip a mage of their standing under the Accords, nor may such decrees impose restrictions on the practice of the Unsanctioned Arts that were not already established by the Conservators and the Innovators.

Furthermore, any attempt by an external power to enforce the Iron Mandate upon a Guild member in a manner that conflicts with the Accords shall be viewed as a violation of the Sovereign Mediation of Archmage Veyra. In instances where the Iron Legion attempts to seize magical artifacts or enforce martial labor on mages, the Guild shall maintain its right to sanctuary and legal autonomy. The Accords do not bow to the "emergency" status of the Iron Mandate; the stability of the Weave is a permanent concern, not a temporary one subject to the shifting tides of imperial warfare. Consequently, the provisions of this Codex shall persist in perpetuity, regardless of the political climate, the presence of the Silver Flame, or the expansionist desires of the Regal Empire.

Any practitioner who attempts to use the Iron Mandate as a legal defense for the violation of a Guild statute shall be found in breach of the Accords. The Guild does not recognize "Imperial Necessity" as a valid excuse for the unauthorized use of forbidden schools or the evasion of the Paradox Trial. See § 1.2 for the definition of Enacting Authority. Should an external entity attempt to impose a competing legal reality, the Aegis Magi are authorized to defend the integrity of the Accords with all necessary arcane measures. The Accords are the law of the land; the Iron Mandate is merely the noise of the world outside our gates. This title does not repeal itself because an Empire shouted.
